name: AACR Project GENIE (public releases)
description: International registry pooling real-world targeted tumor-panel sequencing from dozens of centers, with twice-yearly public releases of mutation, copy-number and fusion data plus limited clinical variables. The BPC (Biopharma Collaborative) adds deeply curated outcome data for selected cancer types.
scale: ~242,000 patients / ~290,000 samples (release ~20.0, mid-2026)
license: Custom GENIE terms of use — NO redistribution without AACR written permission; free registration

provenance.maintainer: AACR + Sage Bionetworks (Synapse); mirrored on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Largest real-world panel-sequencing corpus; strong for mutation-frequency/recurrence priors and for population-level validation of shared/actionable antigen targets.

agent_access: Download requires a free Synapse account and acceptance of terms; fetch via the Synapse Python/R client or command line (token auth), or query the public mirror on cBioPortal's API. Automatable with stored Synapse credentials.
caveats: REDISTRIBUTION PROHIBITED without AACR written permission — flag for any derived product. Targeted panels only (not WES/WGS); heterogeneous gene coverage across centers and releases; retractions occur between releases (track version).

name: GSE302161 / GSE301538 — Canine Anal Sac Adenocarcinoma vs Hepatoid Gland Adenoma (PLoS ONE 2026)
description: A hallmarks-of-cancer comparison between malignant apocrine gland anal sac adenocarcinoma (AGASAC), including sublumbar nodal metastases, and benign hepatoid gland adenoma (HGA) from FFPE archival tissue. The paper reports RNA-seq on 25 samples from 21 cases (15 AGASAC, of which 11 primaries and 4 nodal metastases, plus 10 HGA), deposited as GEO GSE302161 (BioProject PRJNA1289115). A NanoString nCounter panel is deposited as GSE301538 (PRJNA1285400, 45 samples). Analysis code is on figshare.
scale: RNA-seq: 25 samples per paper (6 public SRA runs); nCounter: 45 samples

provenance.maintainer: Institute of Veterinary Pathology, Freie Universität Berlin

relevance.why: This is the first public transcriptome we have found for AGASAC, a common canine tumour that was absent from the catalog. It includes paired primary and nodal-metastasis samples and a benign comparator.

agent_access: GEO supplementary files and SRA runs, no auth.
caveats: Count mismatch: GEO/ENA list only 6 RNA-seq samples/runs, while the paper reports 25 RNA-seq samples. Check whether the remaining samples are only in the GEO TSV count matrix. FFPE material. No explicit reuse license (NCBI).

name: GSE317244 / GSE317641 — Canine Acanthomatous Ameloblastoma & Oral SCC RNA-seq + snRNA-seq
description: Bulk RNA-seq (GEO GSE317244) and single-nucleus RNA-seq (GSE317641; 19 samples — 6 canine acanthomatous ameloblastoma, 10 oral squamous cell carcinoma, 3 healthy gingiva; ~205k nuclei) characterizing neuroepithelial reprogramming and ERBB vulnerability in canine oral tumours (Mol Ther Oncol 2026).
scale: snRNA: 19 samples / ~204,967 nuclei; + bulk RNA-seq

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Molecular Therapy: Oncology 2026)

relevance.why: Oral-tumour gap filler with single-nucleus resolution across two tumour types plus healthy gingiva; ERBB axis is an actionable target and the atlas supports TME/antigen-expression work.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Bulk per-dataset sample counts not stated in text (DS1 new, DS2 reused prior data) — inspect GEO metadata.

name: APOLLO Network (Applied Proteogenomics OrganizationaL Learning and Outcomes)
description: DoD/VA/NCI proteogenomic program profiling DNA, RNA and protein from thousands of annotated tumor specimens (lung, ovary, endometrium, prostate, breast in phase 1). A proteogenomics resource beyond core CPTAC, distributed across NCI's Cancer Research Data Commons: genomics in GDC, proteomics in the Proteomic Data Commons, images in TCIA.
scale: ~8,000 annotated specimens targeted; first studies lung-focused
license: NIH GDS Policy (dbGaP phs003488 for controlled genomics); PDC/ProteomeXchange open proteomics

provenance.maintainer: NCI + U.S. Department of Defense + Department of Veterans Affairs

relevance.why: Matched proteomics + genomics on large tumor cohorts lets antigen pipelines test whether candidate neoantigens are actually translated (protein-level evidence), not just encoded.

agent_access: Proteomics (mzML/raw + processed) openly downloadable from PDC and ProteomeXchange via API/FTP, no auth. Controlled genomics need a dbGaP DAR (phs003488) + GDC token. Imaging via TCIA.
caveats: Not all APOLLO studies are public yet (some "in queue"); release status differs between the PDC FAQ (describes PDC as open) and the program page (genomics permissioned) — verify per study. Genomics is controlled; proteomics raw files are large.

name: Braun et al. 2020 — advanced RCC nivolumab (CheckMate 009/010/025)
description: Integrated WES + RNA-seq of advanced renal-cell carcinoma from the CheckMate nivolumab trials with clinical outcome; dissected genomic and transcriptomic correlates of PD-1 blockade response in RCC.
scale: ~311 patients across CheckMate 009/010/025 (WES; RNA-seq subset)

provenance.maintainer: Choueiri / Wu labs, Dana-Farber; Bristol Myers Squibb trials

relevance.why: Trial-grade RCC cohort with matched expression and outcome — strong for validating antigen/expression response models in a non-melanoma, low-TMB setting.

agent_access: Raw data controlled in EGA (three study accessions); access via EGA DAC approval + EGA download client (pyega3) with credentials. Processed tables/clinical in supplement.
caveats: EGA accessions sourced from a secondary re-analysis paper — confirm against the Nature Medicine data-availability statement. EGA access is per-dataset and can take days.

name: Canine Tumor WES/WGS Cohorts (lymphoma, melanoma, hemangiosarcoma)
description: Collection of public canine tumor exome/genome cohorts in SRA/ENA: lymphoma exomes across three breeds (Broad-sequenced), oral melanoma (ENA PRJEB12081), hemangiosarcoma/angiosarcoma comparative WGS/WES, glioma (PRJNA579792), mammary (PRJNA489159), and pan-tumor TMB/TP53 reanalyses (~600-710 cases).
scale: hundreds of tumor-normal pairs aggregated across studies

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA / ENA (various depositing labs incl. Broad, UPenn, UMN)

relevance.why: Somatic mutation landscapes across canine tumor types — raw material for canine neoantigen prediction (mutation calls -> candidate peptides), to be paired with DLA presentation models.

agent_access: SRA/ENA FASTQ/BAM (prefetch, no auth). Mixed references (CanFam3.1 mostly) — re-align/liftover.
caveats: Heterogeneous references, capture kits and metadata; many lack breed/germline detail. No MHC typing. Neoantigen calling blocked downstream by the DLA-prediction gap.

name: PRJNA1222422 / GSE289443 — Canine Thyroid Carcinoma WES + RNA-seq (Commun Biol 2025)
description: Comparative genomic/transcriptomic profiling of canine thyroid carcinomas: whole-exome (SRA BioProject PRJNA1222422) and RNA-seq (GEO GSE289443) on 30 tumours (25 follicular, 5 medullary; WES+RNA on 27, RNA-only on 3), contrasting molecular profiles with human thyroid cancer (Commun Biol 2025). Normal-thyroid RNA comparators drawn from BarkBase.
scale: 30 tumours sequenced (of 60 total); 27 WES+RNA, 3 RNA-only

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Communications Biology 2025)

relevance.why: New endocrine tumour type for the catalog with matched exome+expression and an explicit canine-vs-human molecular comparison; supports cross-species driver mapping.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). WES (SRA) and RNA (GEO) in separate archives — join by sample. Figure source data on figshare; some data on-request.

name: Pediatric Brain Tumor Atlas (PBTA) — Children's Brain Tumor Network / PNOC
description: Multi-institution pediatric brain-tumor atlas assembled by the Children's Brain Tumor Network (CBTN) and the Pacific Pediatric Neuro-Oncology Consortium (PNOC): >1,000 tumors across many CNS histologies with WGS, WXS, RNA-seq, methylation and matched clinical/ imaging/specimen data, harmonized in the Kids First Data Resource Center. The raw-data source behind OpenPBTA and the proteogenomic pediatric-brain studies.
scale: >1,000 tumors / ~940+ patients (OpenPBTA core); full CBTN release spans ~7,600 subjects
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs002517); CBTN data-use terms

provenance.maintainer: Children's Brain Tumor Network (CBTN) + PNOC; hosted by Kids First DRC / CAVATICA

relevance.why: Pediatric CNS tumors with paired germline and expression — low-mutation-burden settings that stress-test neoantigen pipelines and provide fusion/structural antigen candidates distinct from adult cohorts.

agent_access: Open/registration metadata browsable on the Kids First Portal and PedcBioPortal; raw harmonized files need a Kids First account plus dbGaP approval (phs002517, eRA Commons ID). Specimen/raw requests route through CBTN. CAVATICA offers in-cloud analysis.
caveats: Controlled under dbGaP DUA; pediatric consent sensitivity. Release versions move (phs002517.v4.p2 at time of writing) — pin the version. Raw data "upon request to CBTN" for some material.

name: Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA)
description: Large functional-genomics resource for Chinese glioma patients: ~1,000 mRNA-seq samples (two batches), 286 WES samples, plus microarray, DNA-methylation and miRNA data, with clinical annotation. Openly downloadable processed matrices; raw FASTQ via a Chinese bioinformatics archive. An Asian, organ-specific CNS cohort complementary to TCGA-GBM/LGG.
scale: ~1,018 mRNA-seq, 286 WES, 301 microarray, 159 methylation, 198 miRNA samples
license: unknown — portal states open download but no explicit license/SPDX or use terms

provenance.maintainer: Beijing Neurosurgical Institute / Chinese Glioma Cooperative Group

relevance.why: Asian glioma expression + WES at scale — broadens the HLA/mutation diversity behind CNS antigen models and offers an independent validation set to TCGA glioma.

agent_access: Processed clinical/expression/methylation/mutation tables are direct downloads from the CGGA portal (no auth, scriptable). Raw FASTQ via NGDC/BIGD (PRJCA001636) may need an application.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG: no explicit license or data-use/redistribution/ML terms stated on the portal — treat redistribution and ML-training rights as unverified until confirmed. Sample counts vary across sources; verify against the current download page.

name: CNHPP Early-stage Hepatocellular Carcinoma Proteomics (Jiang et al.)
description: Proteomic (and phosphoproteomic) characterization of early-stage HBV-related HCC from the Chinese Human Proteome Project, with matched transcriptome and clinical outcome; defines proteomic subtypes (e.g., S-III) linked to prognosis and identifies SOAT1 as a target. Organ-specific Asian cohort complementary to Gao et al.
scale: ~110 paired early-stage HCC tumors/normals (proteome)
license: custom — CNHPP liver data portal terms; summary-level genetics only, on application

provenance.maintainer: Chinese Human Proteome Project (CNHPP)

relevance.why: Early-stage HCC proteome with outcome — protein-level validation of antigen candidates in a stage and population underrepresented in TCGA.

agent_access: Proteome/phosphoproteome and gene-expression data available via Supplementary Information and the CNHPP liver data portal; proteomics also on iProX/ProteomeXchange. No anonymous bulk genomics.
caveats: LICENSE/ACCESS RED FLAG: the paper states individual genetic data cannot be uploaded/shared under Chinese human genetic resources rules — only summary-level genetics are shared, on application. Not redistributable at individual level.

name: CPTAC pathology & radiology imaging (TCIA collections)
description: Per-cancer TCIA Collections holding CPTAC whole-slide tissue images (SVS) and, for most, matched radiology (CT/MR/PET), linked by subject ID to CPTAC proteogenomics (genome, proteome, phosphoproteome) in the Proteomic Data Commons and GDC. Covers GBM, LSCC, LUAD, PDA, CM (melanoma), STAD, BRCA, COAD, OV, UCEC and others — a true radiology+pathology+proteogenomics triad.
scale: Dozens of GB per cancer type (e.g. CPTAC-GBM 195.5 GB: 41.1 GB radiology + 154.4 GB pathology)
license: Tissue slides CC BY 4.0 (older versions CC BY 3.0); CPTAC radiology often NIH Controlled Data Access

provenance.maintainer: NCI Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC); imaging hosted on TCIA

relevance.why: Rare human cohorts with co-registered histology, radiology, AND deep proteogenomics — the richest substrate for multimodal models tying tissue/imaging phenotype to protein/immune state.

agent_access: Tissue slides downloadable via TCIA NBIA API / idc-index, no auth (CC BY). CPTAC radiology series are frequently under NIH Controlled Data Access and require authorization — not agent-fetchable.
caveats: MIXED ACCESS per data type: pathology slides are CC BY 4.0 (open); much CPTAC radiology is under NIH Controlled Data Access (restricted). License differs across collection versions (CC BY 3.0 vs 4.0). Cite each collection DOI used.

name: CPTAC Pediatric Brain Tumor Proteogenomics (Petralia et al.)
description: Proteogenomic characterization of 218 pediatric brain tumors across seven histologies (including low- and high-grade glioma, ependymoma, medulloblastoma, ATRT, ganglioglioma, craniopharyngioma, germinoma). Integrates genome, transcriptome, proteome and phosphoproteome. A non-core (pilot) CPTAC proteogenomics study in a pediatric setting, with an interactive ProTrack portal.
scale: 218 pediatric brain tumors, 7 histologies
license: PDC open-access proteomics; underlying genomic data via Kids First DRC (dbGaP)

provenance.maintainer: CPTAC / Children's Brain Tumor Network; analysis by Wang lab (Mount Sinai) et al.

relevance.why: Pediatric-brain proteome + phosphoproteome anchored to genomics — protein-level confirmation of expressed antigens in a tumor class with few mutations, where RNA evidence alone is weak.

agent_access: Proteomics raw + processed openly downloadable from PDC (API/FTP). Processed proteogenomic tables also queryable/downloadable from the ProTrack web tool (pbt.cptac-data-view.org). Genomic reads route through Kids First DRC (controlled, dbGaP).
caveats: Pilot-study scope. Genomic layer is controlled (Kids First / dbGaP); only proteomics are openly downloadable. Confirm current PDC study IDs for proteome vs phosphoproteome.

name: Cristescu et al. 2018 — pan-tumor PD-1 biomarkers (KEYNOTE trials)
description: Retrospective analysis across four KEYNOTE pembrolizumab trials (>300 samples, ~22 tumor types) jointly evaluating TMB and a T-cell-inflamed gene-expression profile (GEP) as predictors of PD-1-blockade response.
scale: >300 samples across ~22 tumor types (4 KEYNOTE trials)

provenance.maintainer: Merck & Co. / Dana-Farber

relevance.why: Defines the operational T-cell-inflamed GEP and its interplay with TMB across many tumor types — a reference for combining expression context with antigen burden.

agent_access: No open individual-level repository; signature definitions and aggregate results are in the paper/supplement. Patient-level trial data require sponsor (Merck) data-sharing request (e.g. via a clinical-trial data-request platform).
caveats: Sponsor-controlled; not an automated-fetch resource. Useful mainly for the published GEP gene set and thresholds. License for supplementary content not explicitly stated.

name: Melanoma checkpoint-blockade WES/RNA cohort (dbGaP phs000452; Van Allen 2015 + Liu 2019)
description: Whole-exome (and later RNA-seq) of metastatic melanoma treated with checkpoint blockade, with response/survival outcomes — a core resource for neoantigen-load vs response modeling. Van Allen 2015 (anti-CTLA-4) deposited as v2.p1; Liu 2019 (anti-PD-1, integrative) extended it as v3.p1.
scale: Van Allen: ~110 WES tumor/normal pairs (anti-CTLA-4); Liu 2019: larger integrative anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort (WES+RNA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen / Liu et al., Dana-Farber / Broad Institute (dbGaP)

relevance.why: Response-annotated melanoma exomes/transcriptomes to relate neoantigen load/quality to ICB outcome — a benchmark cohort for Veritope's presentation/immunogenicity signals.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: dbGaP DAR/DUA approval + eRA Commons required. Not agent-fetchable. Note version split (v2 = Van Allen, v3 = Liu); confirm the version a given analysis needs.
caveats: Controlled-access; no redistribution. Processed MAF/mutation tables for these cohorts are often re-published openly via cBioPortal (study 'skcm_dfci_2015' etc.) — prefer those for open reuse.

name: DepMap / CCLE (Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia + Dependency Map)
description: Broad Institute's cell-line multi-omics: whole-exome/WGS, RNA-seq expression, fusions, copy-number, methylation and metabolomics for ~1,800 cancer cell lines, alongside CRISPR and RNAi dependency and drug-sensitivity screens. The reference resource for cancer cell-line genotype-to-phenotype.
scale: ~1,800 cell lines (omics); ~1,000+ with deep multi-omic profiles
license: DepMap Terms and Conditions (usage agreement; attribution); some metadata CC BY 4.0

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute (DepMap) + Novartis (original CCLE)

relevance.why: Cell lines are the experimental substrate for testing predicted antigens (expression + HLA + presentation). DepMap links a line's mutations/expression to its genotype, so predicted neoantigens can be matched to validatable in-vitro models.

agent_access: Fully automatable: CSV/parquet from the download page, an open AWS bucket (s3://depmap-omics-ccle/, no account), and a portal API. No DUA. Click-through terms ask for attribution only.
caveats: License is a usage agreement, not a standard open license — attribution required, verify before redistribution. Cell lines are not patients (no germline/tumor-microenvironment context); HLA types must be inferred from the omics or from the companion lines.

name: Early-Onset Gastric Cancer Proteogenomics (Mun et al., Korean cohort)
description: Proteogenomic characterization of 80 diffuse-type early-onset gastric cancers (patients ≤45 yr) from a Korean cohort: genome, transcriptome, proteome, phosphoproteome and glycoproteome, defining molecular subtypes with therapeutic implications. An organ- and population-specific proteogenomics resource beyond core CPTAC.
scale: 80 tumor/normal pairs (early-onset diffuse gastric cancer)
license: PDC open-access proteomics; expression in GEO (GSE122401); mutations in Korean Variant Archive (KOVA)

provenance.maintainer: Korea University / CPTAC-associated (Hwang, Lee, Paik et al.)

relevance.why: Diffuse gastric cancer in a young Asian population with multi-layer proteomics — protein- and glycoprotein-level evidence for candidate antigens in a tumor type and demographic underrepresented in Western atlases.

agent_access: Proteome/phospho/glyco raw + processed openly downloadable from PDC (API/FTP). Expression via GEO (GSE122401, verify). Mutation data via the Korean Variant Archive (KOVA).
caveats: Confirm GSE122401 and the exact KOVA deposition before relying on the genomic layer. Proteomics are open; genomic/variant terms differ by repository.

name: Equine sarcoid DNA methylation (GSE208778 / GSE89859)
description: DNA-methylation profiling of equine sarcoid versus normal skin: a reduced-representation bisulfite (RRBS) dataset (GSE208778) paired with the transcriptome study, and an earlier array/methylation profiling dataset (GSE89859). Characterizes aberrant methylation in papillomavirus-associated equine sarcoids.
scale: paired sarcoid/skin methylation cohorts (RRBS + earlier profiling)

provenance.maintainer: Semik-Gurgul et al. and earlier equine epigenetics groups; NCBI GEO

relevance.why: Equine tumor epigenetics complementing the sarcoid transcriptome; cross-species methylation context for comparative oncology.

agent_access: Two GEO series (GSE208778, GSE89859); download via GEO FTP / SRA, no auth.
caveats: Two distinct studies/platforms bundled here — treat as separate records if granularity matters. Confirm both accessions resolve.

name: Equine sarcoid vs healthy skin transcriptome (GSE226986 / PRJNA942611)
description: RNA-seq of equine sarcoid tumors versus matched/healthy equine skin (12 sarcoid and 12 healthy skin samples), used to characterize altered coding and long non-coding RNA expression in bovine papillomavirus-associated equine sarcoids. Companion species (equine) tumor transcriptomics.
scale: 12 sarcoid + 12 healthy skin RNA-seq samples

provenance.maintainer: Semik-Gurgul et al. (National Research Institute of Animal Production, Poland); NCBI GEO/SRA; OmicsDI PRJNA942611

relevance.why: Extends comparative tumor transcriptomics to horses; a virally-driven skin tumor contrasting with canine/feline tumor biology for cross-species TME and oncogenesis comparison.

agent_access: GEO GSE226986 (also BioProject PRJNA942611 on OmicsDI); raw reads via SRA/ENA, no auth.
caveats: Sarcoid is a locally aggressive fibroblastic (papillomavirus-driven) tumor, not a classic metastatic carcinoma — scope comparisons accordingly. Verify accession currency.

name: Feline Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma genomics (Rodrigues et al. 2023)
description: Whole-exome sequencing of tumor and matched blood from six cats with feline oral squamous cell carcinoma (FOSCC), plus RNA-seq of six tumors and normal oral mucosa from three healthy cats. Characterizes the FOSCC genomic landscape and gene-expression profiles as a model of HPV-negative human head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
scale: 6 FOSCC tumors (WES + RNA-seq) + 3 normal mucosa (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Study authors (deposited in NCBI); see PMC10229771

relevance.why: Feline cancer genomics extending comparative oncology to cats; FOSCC as a spontaneous model of HPV-negative human HNSCC for mutational and expression comparison.

agent_access: Exome data under BioProject PRJNA844099 (SRA); programmatic download via SRA Toolkit / ENA. RNA-seq accession not explicitly stated in the data-availability text — check the paper/supplement.
caveats: Small n (6 tumors). RNA-seq accession must be confirmed from the paper. SRA data are raw reads (no license per se; NCBI public-access terms).

name: Feline Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma exome (Chu et al. 2026)
description: Whole-exome sequencing cohort of feline oral squamous cell carcinoma showing genomic parallels with human head and neck SCC: TP53 as the most commonly mutated gene (consequential variants in 71% of tumors) and a very low tumor mutational burden (0–1.6, mean 0.66).
scale: FOSCC tumor exomes (cohort); TMB 0–1.6

provenance.maintainer: Chu et al. (deposited in NCBI SRA); see PMC13420018

relevance.why: Second independent feline FOSCC exome resource; strengthens cross-species comparison of TP53-driven, low-TMB squamous carcinomas between cats and humans.

agent_access: Openly available in SRA under BioProject PRJNA1135178; fetch via SRA Toolkit / ENA.
caveats: Raw reads; low TMB limits neoantigen yield but informs comparative mutational-signature work.

name: GSE261790 / GSE261791 — Canine Archival-Tissue 3' RNA-seq vs nCounter Benchmark (Front Vet Sci 2025)
description: A method benchmark comparing QuantSeq 3' RNA-seq (GSE261790, PRJNA1089080, 25 samples) with NanoString nCounter hybridisation (GSE261791, PRJNA1089079) on FFPE canine archival tumour tissue. GEO sample records list AGASAC samples, and NCBI search also indexes the series under histiocytic sarcoma.
scale: 25 FFPE samples (3' RNA-seq) + matched nCounter

provenance.maintainer: Institute of Veterinary Pathology, Freie Universität Berlin

relevance.why: Adds more AGASAC expression samples and tests how far FFPE archives can be used for canine transcriptomics, which matters because most canine tumour material is FFPE.

caveats: Exact tumour-type composition was not verified sample by sample; read the GEO characteristics before use. 3' tag libraries give gene counts only, with no isoform or variant calling. No explicit reuse license (NCBI).

name: FidoCure / One Health Company Canine Clinico-Genomics
description: Real-world canine precision-oncology platform: targeted panel sequencing (coding exons of oncogenes/tumor suppressors) plus treatment outcomes. Published analyses cover 2,119 dogs (genomics for ~1,108) across >19 tumor types, and a 508-dog splenic hemangiosarcoma study.
scale: ~2,119 dogs (genomics ~1,108); company claims >5,500 dogs
license: article CC BY (2023 npj Precis Oncol); raw data not public

provenance.maintainer: One Health Company (FidoCure)

relevance.why: Largest real-world canine clinico-genomic outcome linkage; valuable aggregate statistics, but not an open dataset.

agent_access: Only summary/supplementary tables are public; patient-level data "upon reasonable request". No bulk download, no API.
caveats: Proprietary; targeted panel (not WES/WGS); company scale claims unverified. NOT redistributable — treat as reference/collaboration target, not a fetchable corpus.

name: Recurrent Glioblastoma Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 trial (Cloughesy et al.)
description: Randomized trial of neoadjuvant vs adjuvant pembrolizumab in recurrent glioblastoma with tumor RNA-seq and TCR sequencing; neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 induced intratumoral interferon signaling, clonal T-cell expansion and a survival benefit. An immunotherapy-outcome cohort in GBM with openly deposited expression data (beyond the usual melanoma/RCC/ urothelial ICB cohorts).
scale: ~35 patients (neoadjuvant + adjuvant arms); tumor RNA-seq + TCR-seq

provenance.maintainer: UCLA (Cloughesy/Prins labs) and multi-institution consortium

relevance.why: Paired expression + TCR with ICB response in GBM — directly links the presented-antigen/ T-cell axis to clinical benefit in a cold tumor, a hard test case for recognition models.

agent_access: GEO series GSE121810 is openly downloadable (supplementary tables; SRA-linked reads), no auth. Some data "available from the corresponding author on reasonable request."
caveats: Small cohort. GEO holds the RNA-seq; full clinical/remaining data may require author request. Confirm whether SRA raw reads (controlled-of-origin? no — open) suit your need.

name: NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC)
description: NCI's harmonized cancer genomics repository and the canonical home of TCGA, TARGET, CPTAC, HCMI, Foundation Medicine, MMRF and dozens of other projects. All data are reprocessed against a common reference (GRCh38) with uniform pipelines, so mutation, copy-number, expression and clinical files are directly comparable across projects. Data are split into an open tier (reprocessed somatic mutation calls, gene expression, copy-number, clinical/biospecimen) and a controlled tier (BAM/CRAM reads, germline, raw genotypes) gated by dbGaP.
scale: ~50,000+ cases across ~90+ projects (portal current count; ~44k cases at v39)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (data-use terms; no single SPDX license)

provenance.maintainer: National Cancer Institute (NCI), Center for Cancer Genomics; operated by U. Chicago

relevance.why: Primary open source of somatic mutation calls (MAF) and RNA-seq expression across tumor types — the raw material for enumerating candidate neoantigens and confirming that the mutated gene is expressed. Controlled tier gives read-level evidence for variant/allele-specific-expression validation.

agent_access: Open-tier files via a documented REST API and the gdc-client download tool — no auth, scriptable, bulk manifests supported. Controlled-tier files require a GDC token minted after dbGaP authorization (Authorization header / token file); the token expires and must be refreshed. No scraping needed; everything is API-addressable.
caveats: Controlled tier (reads, germline) needs an approved dbGaP Data Access Request tied to a specific study (e.g. phs000178 for TCGA) — per-study, renewable, institution-signed. Open-tier redistribution is governed by NIH GDS/data-use certification, not an open license; cite and respect publication-embargo norms. GRCh38 harmonization means legacy hg19-based calls differ from current ones.

name: GDC / TCGA diagnostic & tissue whole-slide images
description: The pathology image layer of the NCI Genomic Data Commons: diagnostic (FFPE) and tissue (frozen) H&E whole-slide images for ~11,000 TCGA cases across 33 cancer types, directly linked by case barcode to GDC genomics/transcriptomics/methylation. The de facto corpus for tissue-to-molecular multimodal learning on human cancer.
scale: ~30,000 WSIs (diagnostic + tissue) across 33 TCGA cancer types, ~11k cases (multi-TB)
license: custom — NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (open-access, research use)

provenance.maintainer: NCI Genomic Data Commons / The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)

relevance.why: The largest barcode-linked human tumor histology + multi-omics resource; foundational for any model that joins tissue morphology to genomic/transcriptomic/immune features.

agent_access: Filter files by data_category=Biospecimen, data_type="Slide Image" (format SVS); bulk download via the GDC Data Transfer Tool or REST API, no auth for open data. Slides are large; download programmatically. Images also mirrored in DICOM form via IDC.
caveats: Open-access but "for research purposes only" under the NIH GDS Policy (not a Creative Commons license): users must not re-identify participants and must acknowledge accession numbers. Not a redistribution license — share derived features, cite source. Multi-TB; frozen (tissue) slides are lower quality than diagnostic (FFPE) slides.

name: Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project (Cancer Programme)
description: UK national WGS programme; the cancer arm provides matched tumor/germline whole genomes with linked NHS clinical and cancer-registry data. Data never leave a secure Research Environment (NGRL) — no bulk export; approved researchers analyze in situ.
scale: ~15,600 cancer-programme participants (germline+somatic WGS); ~13,880 tumors analyzed
license: Genomics England Research Network / Discovery Forum access agreement (no redistribution; no download)

provenance.maintainer: Genomics England Ltd (UK Department of Health)

relevance.why: Population-scale WGS with deep real-world clinical linkage; valuable for validating antigen/driver findings in an independent national cohort and for outcome association.

agent_access: NO data download. Analysis only inside the secure Research Environment after joining the Research Network or a Discovery Forum (industry) partnership. Pipelines must run inside the walled garden; results export is reviewed. Not compatible with an external automated fetch pipeline — the compute goes to the data.
caveats: Membership application + (for industry) paid access; airlock review on any results taken out. UK-governed, consent/registry-linked. Hardest fit for an automated external pipeline.

name: GSE238110 — Canine Osteosarcoma Bulk RNA-seq (DOG^2 / COTC022)
description: Bulk mRNA-seq of 186 canine primary osteosarcoma tumors (DOG^2 cohort / COTC022), NovaSeq 6000 (GPL25760). Widely reused by comparative OSA studies. Raw count matrix provided.
scale: 186 primary tumors
license: public (NCBI GEO; no explicit license, US-gov public-domain norms)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI GEO (depositing lab)

relevance.why: Largest single canine osteosarcoma transcriptome series; TME deconvolution and expression context for antigen candidates.

agent_access: GEO supplementary counts + SRA FASTQ (prefetch); no auth; FTP bulk.
caveats: Expression only — no HLA/DLA typing, no immunopeptidome. Align to a fixed reference.

name: Gide et al. 2019 — melanoma anti-PD-1 +/- anti-CTLA-4 (WES/RNA-seq)
description: Metastatic melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 monotherapy or combined anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4, with WES and RNA-seq and response/survival; emphasized on-treatment biopsies as stronger predictors than baseline.
scale: ~73-91 patients (WES and/or RNA-seq across pre/on-treatment)
license: ENA/EGA submission terms (RNA-seq open on ENA; WES controlled on EGA)

provenance.maintainer: Wilmott / Scolyer / Long labs, Melanoma Institute Australia

relevance.why: Combination-therapy melanoma cohort with on-treatment transcriptomes — complements Hugo/Riaz for antigen/expression dynamics under single vs dual blockade.

agent_access: RNA-seq openly retrievable from ENA PRJEB23709 (no auth). WES controlled in EGA EGAD00001005738 (DAC + pyega3).
caveats: Accessions sourced from re-analysis papers — confirm against the Cancer Cell data statement. Mixed open/controlled by modality.

name: GSE122916 — Canine Prostate Cancer FNA + Tissue RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of canine prostate tissue and fine-needle aspirates spanning malignant and non-malignant samples (reanalyzed in a biomarker-prioritization framework, PMC8584104: 10 malignant and 14 non-malignant prostate tissue/FNA samples). Canine prostate cancer is predominantly castration-resistant, a model for aggressive human disease.
scale: ~24 samples (malignant + non-malignant tissue and FNA)

provenance.maintainer: (see papers)

relevance.why: Canine prostate expression reference; underpins a canine/human castration-resistance comparison (bioRxiv 2024) relevant to cross-species target discovery.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Small malignant n. The comparative bioRxiv preprint key_ref was rate-limited at verification — confirm whether it deposits new accessions beyond this series. Framework DOI verified on PMC8584104.

name: GSE190374 / PRJNA786902 — Nine Canine Prostate Cancer Cell Lines RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of nine canine prostate cancer cell lines compared with original tumour tissues, revealing diverse therapeutic-target signatures (Cancer Cell Int 2021). SRA study SRP349649 / BioProject PRJNA786902.
scale: 9 canine prostate cancer cell lines (+ tumour tissue)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Cancer Cell International 2021)

relevance.why: Canine prostate cancer cell-line panel expands the canine in-vitro model collection and pairs cell lines with source tumours for expression fidelity checks.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Cell lines — not primary cohort.

name: GSE196108 — Canine Cortisol-Secreting Adrenocortical Tumour RNA-seq (Vet Comp Oncol 2023)
description: RNA-seq of 48 canine cortisol-secreting adrenocortical tumours (csACTs) and 10 normal adrenal cortices. The study defines two prognostic subtypes and nominates CYP26B1 as a therapeutic target, cross-checked against a human cortisol-secreting ACC dataset. SRA SRP358249, BioProject PRJNA803356.
scale: 59 samples (48 csACT + 10 normal + 1); 118 runs

provenance.maintainer: Utrecht University, Faculty of Veterinary Medicine

relevance.why: Adrenocortical tumours were absent from the catalog. This is a sizeable cohort with survival data and an explicit cross-species (human ACC) comparison.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI). GEO lists 59 samples, while the paper describes 48 + 10; check metadata.

name: GSE208664 — Canine Soft-Tissue Sarcoma, 3 Subtypes FFPE RNA-seq (PLoS ONE 2022)
description: Comparative whole-transcriptome RNA-seq across three canine soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes from FFPE material, with FASTQ, metadata and read-count files deposited (PLoS ONE 2022). Complements GSE214154 with subtype-resolved expression.
scale: canine STS, 3 subtypes (FFPE RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — PLoS ONE 2022)

relevance.why: Subtype-level STS expression reference; useful to stratify the integrated cohort and for canine-human STS expression mapping.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). FFPE-derived — expect degradation artifacts.

name: GSE214154 / PRJNA882864 — Canine Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Integrated Omics (Sci Rep 2023)
description: Integrated RNA-seq (GEO GSE214154, 29 samples) and matched tumour/normal whole-exome sequencing (SRA BioProject PRJNA882864) of canine soft-tissue sarcomas, reporting recurrent TP53 and KMT-gene mutations and recurrent PDGFB fusions (Sci Rep 2023).
scale: 29 STS RNA-seq samples + 29 tumour/normal WES pairs

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Scientific Reports 2023)

relevance.why: Matched expression + exome in an under-covered tumour group; fusion and driver calls give both neoantigen candidates (fusions) and expression context for them.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). RNA in GEO, WES in SRA — link by sample IDs. Heterogeneous STS subtypes within the cohort.

name: GSE223526 — Canine Pheochromocytoma / Paraganglioma RNA-seq (Front Vet Sci 2023)
description: Whole-transcriptome RNA-seq of 19 canine pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas (18 PCC, 1 PGL) and 10 normal adrenal medullas. The study defines two transcriptional groups with significantly different survival. BioProject PRJNA926644.
scale: 29 samples (19 tumours + 10 normal medulla); 58 runs

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Frontiers in Veterinary Science 2023)

relevance.why: Adds a neuroendocrine tumour type with a matched normal-tissue baseline and a link between expression subtype and survival.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI). Two tumours were excluded as PCA outliers in the paper.

name: GSE288068 — Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma Tumour + Cell-Line Transcriptomes (Engleberg 2025)
description: RNA-seq of canine histiocytic sarcoma (18 HS-affected tumours vs 5 normal samples, plus three HS cell lines), identifying multiple therapeutic target pathways (Engleberg et al., Cancers 2025). Canine HS is a spontaneous model for the rare human histiocytic/dendritic neoplasms, with breed predisposition (e.g. Bernese Mountain Dog, Flat-Coated Retriever).
scale: 18 tumours + 5 normal + 3 cell lines (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Michigan State University / NIH Genomics Core

relevance.why: First-pass transcriptome for a previously uncovered canine tumour type with a direct rare-human-cancer analogue; supplies HS expression references and candidate targets.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI open). Modest cohort; normals n=5. Cell-line and tumour data mixed in one series — separate by sample metadata.

name: GSE295311 — Canine Osteosarcoma GeoMx Spatial Transcriptomics
description: NanoString GeoMx digital spatial profiling of osteosarcoma-bearing pet dogs enrolled in a clinical trial; companion spatial layer to the bulk GSE238110 cohort.
scale: spatial ROIs across trial dogs

provenance.maintainer: NCBI GEO

relevance.why: Spatially resolved immune/tumor compartments — rare canine spatial dataset for microenvironment work.

agent_access: GEO download; no auth.
caveats: Targeted panel (not whole-transcriptome spatial); small ROI count.

name: GSE346824 — Canine Oral SCC Spatial Transcriptomics, Tumour and Lymph Node (Int J Mol Sci 2026)
description: GeoMx digital spatial profiling (306 areas of illumination) of canine oral squamous cell carcinoma and of regional lymph nodes with and without locoregional metastasis. Regions include subcapsular/medullary sinus and paracortex. The aim is spatial signatures that detect occult nodal metastasis. BioProject PRJNA1526669.
scale: 306 AOIs (GeoMx DCC/PKC)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2026)

relevance.why: Spatially resolved immune context of the tumour-draining lymph node in a canine HNSCC model; complements the domain-14 ameloblastoma/OSCC snRNA atlas.

caveats: GeoMx probe-count data only, with no raw reads in SRA. Requires a canine-compatible GeoMx PKC. No explicit reuse license (NCBI).

name: GSE45832 — Flat-Coated Retriever Histiocytic Sarcoma Expression Arrays (PLoS ONE 2013)
description: Two-colour expression microarrays of soft-tissue and visceral histiocytic sarcomas in the highly predisposed Flat-coated Retriever breed (38 arrays). BioProject PRJNA196521.
scale: 38 arrays

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — PLoS ONE 2013)

relevance.why: A breed-specific HS expression reference that separates the soft-tissue and visceral forms.

caveats: Legacy two-colour array against a reference design, so it is not directly comparable with RNA-seq. No explicit reuse license.

name: GSE95048 — Canine Meningioma FFPE RNA-seq (PLoS ONE 2017)
description: RNA-seq of FFPE and flash-frozen canine meningiomas against normal meninges. The final analysis kept 13 tumours (11 FFPE, 2 frozen) and 3 controls out of 24 tumours sequenced. BioProject PRJNA375808.
scale: 16 samples deposited (13 tumours + 3 normal analysed)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — PLoS ONE 2017)

relevance.why: An early canine meningioma expression set with normal meninges; useful as an independent validation set for GSE250310.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI). FFPE degradation; small n; 2 excluded samples were reclassified as melanoma.

name: Hartwig Medical Foundation database
description: Dutch non-profit hosting uniformly processed whole-genome sequences of metastatic (and increasingly primary) tumors with matched normals and clinical/treatment-response data. A leading resource for metastatic cancer genomics and mutational landscapes under treatment.
scale: ~8,000+ patients WGS (metastatic solid tumors)
license: Hartwig license agreement per data request (DR-xxx); no redistribution

provenance.maintainer: Hartwig Medical Foundation (Netherlands)

relevance.why: Metastatic-tumor WGS captures the antigen landscape at the disease stage therapy actually targets, including treatment-driven evolution — complementary to primary-tumor cohorts like TCGA.

agent_access: Submit a data request; a Data Access Board reviews it and you sign a license agreement. On approval, data are delivered (typically cloud bucket/transfer), after which access is programmatic. No anonymous or API-first access; application-gated.
caveats: Request is project-scoped and license-bound with publication rules; no redistribution. Each project gets a DR-number. Turnaround is weeks.

name: Hartwig Medical Foundation metastatic cancer WGS database
description: One of the largest uniformly-processed metastatic pan-cancer whole-genome resources: tumor WGS with matched germline and (for many) RNA-seq, plus structured clinical and treatment-response data, from patients across the Netherlands (CPCT/DRUP/WIDE). Captures advanced/treated disease and structural variation absent from primary-tumor atlases.
scale: >5,000 metastatic tumor WGS (growing); 360+ approved data requests served
license: custom — Hartwig license agreement + data transfer agreement (academic use)

provenance.maintainer: Hartwig Medical Foundation (Netherlands)

relevance.why: Metastatic WGS + RNA-seq + treatment outcome at scale — the setting where therapy- resistant, expressed neoantigens matter, and where structural-variant antigens are enriched relative to exome cohorts.

agent_access: No open download: email dataaccess@hartwigmedicalfoundation.nl, submit an online request on behalf of an institution, sign the license/DTA; data are delivered to an authorized GCP account with time-limited access. An agent can fetch from GCP only after approval.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG: bespoke license + DTA, institution-signed, time-limited; "free for academic use" means no fee, not unrestricted — redistribution and likely commercial/ML terms are constrained. Board review required.

name: HBV-related Hepatocellular Carcinoma Proteogenomics (Gao et al., Chinese cohort)
description: Integrated proteogenomic characterization of 159 paired tumor/non-tumor liver tissues from HBV-related HCC patients in a Chinese cohort (a CPTAC/ICPC partner study). Genome, transcriptome, proteome and phosphoproteome define metabolic subtypes and candidate therapeutic targets. Organ-specific, non-TCGA Asian proteogenomic resource.
scale: 159 HBV-related HCC patients (paired tumor/non-tumor)
license: custom — National Omics Data Encyclopedia (NODE) terms for genomics; proteomics via iProX/ProteomeXchange

provenance.maintainer: Fudan University / CPTAC-China (ICPC partner)

relevance.why: HBV-driven HCC in an Asian cohort with matched proteome — expands antigen models beyond Western cohorts and gives protein-level evidence for virally-associated tumor antigens.

agent_access: Proteomics mirrored to iProX/ProteomeXchange (openly fetchable). Genomic data hosted in NODE (biosino.org) under application/registration — not a simple anonymous bulk download.
caveats: LICENSE/ACCESS RED FLAG: individual-level genetic data are subject to China's Human Genetic Resources regulations — genomics are application-gated via NODE, not openly redistributable. Confirm the exact NODE accession and terms before reuse.

name: Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN) Data Portal
description: NCI-funded multi-institution atlas of human tumors across the pre-cancer-to-advanced continuum, with single-cell, spatial, imaging, bulk and clinical data under a common data model. Open-access derived/Level-3+ data plus controlled-access lower-level and identifiable data.
scale: 20+ atlases, millions of cells + spatial/imaging across cancer types

provenance.maintainer: NCI Human Tumor Atlas Network / Sage Bionetworks (Synapse)

relevance.why: Multi-modal, deeply clinically annotated human tumor data spanning single-cell and spatial — high-value for linking antigen-presentation state to tumor progression.

agent_access: Open-access files downloadable (free Synapse account for Synapse-hosted files). Programmatic access via Synapse REST API / CLI / R client, and ISB-CGC BigQuery for clinical/metadata queries; portal generates DRS manifests for cloud (SB-CGC). Controlled files require approved dbGaP application (phs002371) — not agent-automatable.
caveats: Controlled tier needs institutional dbGaP DUA; cannot be auto-ingested. Explicit reuse license for open-access files not clearly stated per-file — check portal terms. Third-party `htan` PyPI wrapper exists (MIT) but is unofficial.

name: Hugo et al. 2016 — anti-PD-1 melanoma (WES/RNA-seq + response)
description: Metastatic melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab/nivolumab); whole-exome and transcriptome of pretreatment tumors with response annotation. Defined the "IPRES" innate anti-PD-1 resistance transcriptional signature.
scale: ~38 patients (WES); 28 RNA-seq (GSE78220)
license: GEO/SRA public submission (open); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Lo / Ribas labs, UCLA

relevance.why: Open anti-PD-1 melanoma expression + mutation cohort for benchmarking expression-based and neoantigen-based response models.

agent_access: RNA-seq openly downloadable from GEO GSE78220; raw reads in SRA SRP067938 (UCLA) and SRP090294 (Vanderbilt) via fasterq-dump — no auth, fully automatable.
caveats: Small, melanoma-only. WES access route less uniform than the RNA-seq; confirm per-sample.

name: Hugo 2016 anti-PD-1 melanoma (GEO GSE78220 + SRA SRP067938/SRP090294)
description: Genomic + transcriptomic profiling of metastatic melanoma on anti-PD-1 therapy, with response annotation. RNA-seq in GEO (GSE78220); whole-exome in SRA. Widely reused for response/neoantigen and expression-signature modeling.
scale: 38 WES samples; 28 with RNA-seq (15 responders / 13 non-responders, pre-treatment)

provenance.maintainer: Hugo/Ribas/Lo labs, UCLA

relevance.why: OPENLY accessible response-annotated melanoma RNA-seq (GEO) — rare for ICB cohorts (most are dbGaP); good for expression/neoantigen-context modeling without a DUA.

agent_access: GEO RNA-seq (GSE78220) openly downloadable, no auth; WES in SRA (SRP067938 UCLA, SRP090294 Vanderbilt) openly accessible. Fully automatable.
caveats: Open, but SRA raw WES is large. Small cohort. GEO processed data = FPKM tables; raw reads via SRA.

name: ICDC OSA01
description: Multi-platform sequencing (WGS/WES/RNA-seq) of canine appendicular osteosarcoma.
scale: osteosarcoma cohort (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: Osteosarcoma somatic landscape for neoantigen candidate generation.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No MHC typing/immunopeptidome; counts via API.

name: ICDC OSA03
description: Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (methylation) of human and canine osteosarcoma — rare public canine tumor methylome.
scale: human + canine OSA WGBS (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: One of the few public canine tumor methylomes; epigenetic context for antigen expression.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Methylation only; counts via API.

name: ICDC TCL01 — Canine Cancer Cell-Line WES
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine cancer cell lines (osteosarcoma, lymphoma, melanoma, hemangiosarcoma and others) for druggable-target discovery. Overlaps SRA BioProject PRJNA503864 (33 canine cancer cell lines).
scale: ~33 canine cancer cell lines

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC; original: Das et al.

relevance.why: Cell lines are candidate substrates for in-house DLA-restricted immunopeptidomics (MHC-I elution) to begin closing the canine presentation gap.

agent_access: FASTQ/BAM via SRA (prefetch/fasterq-dump, no auth); calls via ICDC.
caveats: No native MHC-ligand data; DLA typing of lines not standardized.

name: ICDC UBC02
description: Molecular subtypes of canine urothelial carcinoma with tumor immune signatures (genomics/transcriptomics). One of the few ICDC studies with an explicit immune-signature focus.
scale: urothelial cohort (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: Tumor immune-signature transcriptomics — closest ICDC study to immune context, but still no MHC-ligand/TCR data.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Immune "signatures" are expression deconvolution only, not antigen-level data.

name: ICDC UC01
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine urothelial carcinomas lacking BRAF V595E; identifies in-frame BRAF/MAP2K1 deletions as alternative MAPK activation.
scale: WES cohort (BRAF V595E-negative)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: Somatic variants for neoantigen candidate generation in bladder cancer.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Exome variants only; no MHC data.

name: ICGC 25K (legacy International Cancer Genome Consortium)
description: The original ICGC data release: ~24,000 donors across ~80 projects and 20+ tumor types. Simple somatic mutations, structural variants, expression and methylation are available in two tiers — open-access aggregated/somatic summaries, and controlled-access raw and germline data in EGA.
scale: 24,289 donors (22,330 with molecular data), ~80 projects
license: ICGC data-access policy (open tier) / DACO + EGA DUA (controlled tier)

provenance.maintainer: ICGC / OICR (legacy DCC, partially migrated to AWS/Collaboratory and EGA)

relevance.why: Large, diverse open somatic mutation corpus for neoantigen enumeration without a DUA, spanning tumor types and populations complementary to TCGA.

agent_access: Open somatic/aggregated files downloadable programmatically from the legacy DCC/mirrors (no auth). Raw and germline data require DACO approval plus EGA dataset-level access and the EGA download client (ega-fuse / pyega3) with credentials.
caveats: Legacy portal partially deprecated; some endpoints moved to AWS Collaboratory / EGA. Controlled tier is doubly gated (DACO then EGA). Build-hg19 calls predominate.

name: ICGC ARGO (Accelerating Research in Genomic Oncology)
description: Successor to ICGC, aiming to uniformly analyze tumor genomes with harmonized, deep clinical data across international programs. Clinical data on the ARGO Data Platform are open to any registered user; molecular (sequence/variant) data are controlled and gated by the ICGC Data Access Compliance Office (DACO).
scale: ~7,000+ donors, 9 programs, ~180,000 files (Release 15)
license: ICGC ARGO data-use / DACO terms (not an open license)

provenance.maintainer: ICGC ARGO (OICR-hosted Data Coordination Centre)

relevance.why: International, prospectively collected tumors with uniform processing extend antigen-discovery beyond US cohorts and add populations/cancer types underrepresented in TCGA.

agent_access: Clinical data downloadable by any registered platform user (programmatic via platform API). Controlled molecular data require DACO approval (2-year term), after which a download client / API token is issued. Not scrape-able; auth-gated end to end for molecular files.
caveats: DACO application is institution-signed and project-scoped; approval can take weeks. Some raw data mirrored in EGA with separate per-dataset access (up to 48h provisioning).

name: IMbrave150 / GO30140 HCC atezolizumab + bevacizumab transcriptomic cohort
description: Tumor gene-expression data from the IMbrave150 phase 3 and GO30140 phase 1b trials of atezolizumab + bevacizumab in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, used to derive and validate ICB-response signatures (e.g., ABRS, ISS). An HCC immunotherapy-outcome cohort beyond the melanoma/RCC/urothelial sets, with controlled-access expression data in EGA.
scale: advanced HCC; expression from IMbrave150 (phase 3) + GO30140 (phase 1b) arms
license: EGA controlled-access data access agreement (Roche/Genentech DAC)

provenance.maintainer: Genentech/Roche; analyses by multiple academic groups

relevance.why: HCC ICB-outcome expression at trial scale — links immune/antigen-presentation signatures to combination-immunotherapy benefit in a tumor type absent from the usual ICB cohorts.

agent_access: Expression data require an EGA controlled-access DAR (EGAD00001008128) through the sponsor's data access committee + DTA; no open download. Derived signatures are published in the papers.
caveats: Industry-sponsored, EGA-controlled (sponsor DAC approval, DTA). Access is to gene-expression data; raw clinical/genomic depth is limited. Confirm current dataset/accession on EGA.

name: Gabriella Miller Kids First Data Resource
description: NIH Common Fund pediatric resource spanning childhood cancers and structural birth defects, with WGS/WES and RNA-seq plus clinical data. Summary data are browsable in the Portal; individual-level genomic data are controlled via dbGaP and analyzed through the integrated CAVATICA cloud platform.
scale: ~30,000+ participants with WGS or RNA data (cancer + congenital)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; dbGaP DUA via Kids First Data Access Committee

provenance.maintainer: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (DRC) + NIH Common Fund

relevance.why: Pediatric tumors (fusion-driven, low-TMB) stress-test antigen pipelines built on adult cancers and add fusion-neoantigen and germline-predisposition context.

agent_access: Summary/metadata browsable openly via the Portal (and its API). Individual-level data require a dbGaP Data Access Request approved by the Kids First DAC; approved data are pushed to CAVATICA (Seven Bridges) for in-cloud analysis rather than local download.
caveats: Controlled tier under pediatric dbGaP DUA; analysis is cloud-native (CAVATICA), not a simple download. Separate proposal/submission step beyond the dbGaP request.

name: Gabriella Miller Kids First Data Resource Center (DRC)
description: NIH Common Fund cloud platform harmonizing genomic + clinical data across many pediatric cancer and structural-birth-defect cohorts (including CBTN/PBTA, pediatric solid and hematologic tumors). WGS/WXS/RNA-seq with matched germline across dozens of studies, with a registration tier and a dbGaP-gated controlled tier; integrates with CAVATICA for in-cloud analysis. The umbrella resource that aggregates many of the pediatric subprojects.
scale: >110,000 data files; ~15 cancer + 22 birth-defect cohorts, >28,500 participants
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; per-study dbGaP DUAs

provenance.maintainer: NIH Common Fund; DRC led by Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (D3b) + partners

relevance.why: One access path to many pediatric tumor genomes with germline — lets antigen pipelines span histologies and calibrate against pediatric HLA/mutation backgrounds rather than adult-only data.

agent_access: Portal browsing + API with a free account for registration-tier files; controlled files require dbGaP approval (eRA Commons ID) per study (phs accessions), then detected by the portal. CAVATICA for in-cloud compute.
caveats: Controlled tier is per-study dbGaP (not one blanket DUA). Pediatric consent sensitivity. File/participant counts are point-in-time — verify on the portal.

name: Liu et al. 2019 — metastatic melanoma anti-PD-1 integrative (WES/RNA-seq)
description: Large integrative anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort (including prior-CTLA-4-treated patients) with WES and RNA-seq and clinical modeling; showed TMB's predictive value is confounded by melanoma subtype and prior therapy.
scale: 144 patients WES; 121 RNA-seq
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP DUA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen lab, Dana-Farber / Broad; Schadendorf (Essen)

relevance.why: One of the larger single anti-PD-1 melanoma cohorts with matched WES+RNA — good power for antigen/expression response modeling and for studying TMB confounders.

agent_access: Reads controlled via dbGaP phs000452.v3.p1; supplementary clinical/mutation tables and a companion GitHub repo (vanallenlab/schadendorf-pd1) hold processed data and code (open).
caveats: Shares the phs000452 accession with Van Allen 2015 — overlapping patients; dedupe before pooling. Controlled DUA for reads.

name: Canine Lymphoma Exomes, 3 Breeds (Elvers 2015)
description: Matched tumor-normal exome sequencing of lymphomas from boxer (T-cell), cocker spaniel (B-cell), and golden retriever (mixed); Roche custom 50 Mb canine exome; Broad-sequenced. Showed breed-specific somatic patterns.
scale: tumor-normal exomes across 3 breeds

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA (Broad/UMN)

relevance.why: Breed-stratified lymphoma mutation sets; germline-background effect on somatic patterns.

agent_access: SRA; accession in paper supplement (not surfaced in search — VERIFY exact PRJNA).
caveats: Accession VERIFY (check supp http://genome.cshlp.org/content/suppl/2015/09/16/gr.194449.115.DC1). CanFam3.1-era.

name: Mariathasan et al. 2018 — IMvigor210 urothelial atezolizumab (RNA-seq/WES)
description: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma treated with atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1) in the IMvigor210 trial, with RNA-seq, mutation data and response; linked TGF-beta signaling in fibroblasts to immune exclusion and non-response.
scale: ~348 patients with RNA-seq (298-348 depending on modality)
license: Processed data: Genentech IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package (custom terms); raw: EGA DUA

provenance.maintainer: Genentech

relevance.why: Widely used urothelial ICI benchmark; the processed expression+clinical R package is a near-open resource for validating response/expression models outside melanoma.

agent_access: Processed gene-expression + clinical data distributed as the IMvigor210CoreBiologies R package (download + install, scriptable). Raw sequence data controlled in EGA EGAS00001002556 (DAC approval + pyega3).
caveats: R-package terms are custom (academic reuse widely practiced). EGA accession appears with some variation across re-analyses (EGAS00001002556 vs others) — verify the intended modality/accession.

name: GSE122590 / GSE50433 — Canine Cutaneous MCT Expression Arrays (metastasis; prognosis)
description: Two MCT microarray cohorts. GSE122590 (PRJNA505684, 34 arrays, Affymetrix CEL) compares primary cutaneous MCTs that later metastasised with those that did not. GSE50433 (PRJNA217482, 51 biopsies, Agilent Canine V2 4x44k) profiles MCT for classification and prognosis by differentiation grade.
scale: 34 + 51 arrays

provenance.maintainer: (see papers — PLoS ONE 2018; PLoS ONE 2014)

relevance.why: Outcome-annotated MCT expression (metastasis, grade) that complements the domain-14 MCT exome and LCM RNA-seq entries.

caveats: Array platforms differ from each other and from RNA-seq; batch-correct before combining. No explicit reuse license.

name: GSE306319 / PRJNA1310467 — Canine MCT Laser-Capture-Microdissection RNA-seq (Sci Rep 2026)
description: RNA sequencing of neoplastic mast cells isolated by laser-capture microdissection from FFPE biopsies of 32 canine cutaneous mast cell tumours across grades, reporting grade-associated molecular alterations with reduced stromal contamination. GEO series GSE306319 (BioProject PRJNA1310467) provides processed RDS/TXT supplementary files.
scale: 32 canine cutaneous MCTs (LCM RNA-seq); GEO lists 1 sample record

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Scientific Reports 2026)

relevance.why: Cleanest primary-MCT expression signal available (tumour cells only), suited to MCT-specific marker and antigen discovery.

caveats: Accession resolved in pass 14b via GEO search (title matches the paper). Raw reads are NOT public: on 2026-11-15, NCBI SRA had 0 experiments and ENA had 0 runs under PRJNA1310467, and GEO shows a single sample record carrying processed RDS/TXT files. Expect a count/expression object, not FASTQ, and confirm it covers all 32 tumours.

name: MET500 metastatic cancer cohort (Robinson et al.)
description: Integrative clinical genomics of 500 adult patients with metastatic solid tumors of ~30 types: whole-exome plus whole-transcriptome sequencing across diverse metastatic sites, with somatic mutation and CNV calls. An early, widely reused metastatic pan-cancer reference distinct from primary-tumor TCGA.
scale: 500 metastatic tumors, ~30 cancer types (WXS + RNA-seq)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs000673)

provenance.maintainer: Michigan Center for Translational Pathology (MCTP), University of Michigan

relevance.why: Metastatic WXS + RNA-seq across many tumor types — expands antigen-candidate discovery into advanced disease and provides a cross-site expression reference.

agent_access: Somatic mutation/CNV summaries downloadable from the MET500 web portal; raw reads require a dbGaP DAR (phs000673.v2.p1) with institutional signing.
caveats: Raw data controlled (dbGaP DUA). Mixed RNA-seq protocols (PolyA vs capture) require batch care. Older cohort (2017); GRCh37-era processing.

name: Miao 2018 clear-cell renal carcinoma ICB cohort
description: Whole-exome (+ clinical) profiling of metastatic clear-cell RCC treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, linking PBRM1 loss and genomic features to response. Response-annotated; processed data mirrored on cBioPortal.
scale: WES; validation cohort ~63 ccRCC patients on PD-1/PD-L1 +/- CTLA-4 blockade
license: cBioPortal data: open (ODC-ODbL / free reuse); dbGaP raw: controlled

provenance.maintainer: Miao/Van Allen et al., Dana-Farber / Broad

relevance.why: Non-melanoma (RCC) ICB response cohort broadens tumor-type coverage for neoantigen/response modeling.

agent_access: Processed mutations/clinical openly on cBioPortal datahub (GitHub) — agent-fetchable, no auth. Raw sequence via dbGaP (controlled). Prefer cBioPortal for open reuse.
caveats: Raw reads controlled; cBioPortal copy is processed-level and openly reusable. Confirm the exact cBioPortal study id.

name: Miao et al. 2018 — immune checkpoint response in clear-cell RCC (WES)
description: Whole-exome sequencing of clear-cell (and other) renal-cell carcinoma treated with PD-1/ PD-L1 or CTLA-4 blockade, with response annotation; identified truncating PBRM1 mutations associated with ICI benefit in ccRCC.
scale: ~35 ccRCC (plus additional non-ccRCC); WES + matched normal
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP DUA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen lab, Dana-Farber / Broad

relevance.why: Extends antigen/response modeling to a low-TMB cancer (RCC) where response is driven more by specific driver loss than by bulk neoantigen load.

agent_access: Reads controlled via dbGaP phs001493 (approved DAR + token). Summary MAF/clinical in supplement. Cite v3.p1 for the live record.
caveats: Controlled DUA. Low-TMB disease — a useful negative/edge case for TMB-centric predictors.

name: MMRF CoMMpass (Relating Clinical Outcomes in MM to Personal Assessment of Genetic Profile)
description: Longitudinal multiple-myeloma cohort from the Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation: ~1,150 newly diagnosed patients followed over ≥8 years with serial sampling at diagnosis and relapse. Tumor/normal whole-exome, whole-genome and RNA-seq are paired with deep clinical annotation (treatment, response, survival). The flagship rare-cancer genomics resource not covered by TCGA, widely used for myeloma subtype and progression analysis.
scale: ~1,150 patients (995 cases with controlled seq in GDC MMRF-COMMPASS); serial timepoints
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs000748); MMRF Gateway registration terms for processed tier

provenance.maintainer: Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation (MMRF); sequencing by TGen; served via NCI GDC

last_updated: staged 6-monthly interim releases; public release 12 months after each interim

relevance.why: Rare-cancer cohort with paired WGS/WXS/RNA-seq and longitudinal relapse sampling — a clean substrate for enumerating expressed somatic variants and watching how the antigen landscape shifts under therapy in a non-TCGA tumor type.

agent_access: Open-tier derivatives and the controlled tier are both GDC API-addressable (gdc-client, manifests). Raw reads need an approved dbGaP DAR (phs000748) + GDC token. Processed/ clinical tables need a free MMRF Researcher Gateway account (research.themmrf.org); a newer MMRF Virtual Lab also hosts the data (terms unverified).
caveats: Staged release embargo: data reach the public ~12 months after each interim release, with sponsors/sites getting earlier access — expect the newest timepoints to be withheld. Raw reads are controlled (dbGaP DUA, institutional signing). Gateway registration terms govern redistribution of the processed tier.

name: MSK-IMPACT Clinical Sequencing Cohort (public release)
description: Public, de-identified release of Memorial Sloan Kettering's targeted panel sequencing of >10,000 advanced-cancer patients (Zehir et al. 2017), with mutation, copy-number and structural-variant calls plus clinical annotation. Hosted openly on cBioPortal (msk_impact_2017); larger MSK-MET and later releases also public.
scale: 10,336 patients / 10,945 tumors (2017 release); larger in later MSK releases
license: Open for scientific use via cBioPortal (ODbL-governed hosting); cite Zehir et al.

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; hosted on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Very large real-world advanced/metastatic cohort with hotspot-focused calls — good for recurrence priors on actionable/shared antigens, though panel-limited for exome-wide neoantigen discovery.

agent_access: Fully open via the cBioPortal API and study ZIP — no auth. Programmatic and bulk-friendly.
caveats: Targeted panel (341–505 genes), NOT whole-exome — captures only panel-covered variants, so it under-counts the neoantigen space. De-identified; redistribution follows cBioPortal (ODbL) + citation of the source paper.

name: MSK-MET (Nguyen et al. 2022) — pan-cancer metastasis genomics
description: Very large pan-cancer cohort (~25,000 patients) integrating MSK-IMPACT tumor genomics with detailed metastatic-site annotation to map organotropism and genomic correlates of metastatic spread; de-identified data released publicly on cBioPortal.
scale: ~25,000 patients across 50+ cancer types (targeted panel)
license: Open via cBioPortal (ODbL-governed hosting); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering; hosted on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Massive real-world cohort tying tumor genotype to metastatic behavior — useful for recurrence priors on actionable/shared antigens and for stage/site-aware target prioritization.

agent_access: Open via cBioPortal (API + study ZIP), no auth, automatable.
caveats: Targeted panel (not WES/WGS) — no neoantigen-level or expression data. Confirm the exact cBioPortal study id (expected msk_met_2021) on the datasets page before scripting.

name: NCI Mesothelioma Clinical Genomics / Clinomics cohort (Hmeljak/Thorsson et al.)
description: NCI mesothelioma resource combining expression and clinical data for ~100 patients, including a subset (16) treated with anti-PD-1 therapy (pembrolizumab/nivolumab) and outcome. Served via the NCI Clinomics site with controlled-access raw data in dbGaP; an organ-specific rare-cancer cohort with ICB-treated patients.
scale: ~100 patients with expression; 16 anti-PD-1 treated
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs002207)

provenance.maintainer: National Cancer Institute (CCR)

relevance.why: Rare-cancer cohort with ICB-treated patients and expression — supports immunotherapy- response modeling in mesothelioma, complementing PrE0505.

agent_access: Some expression/summary data via the NCI Clinomics portal; raw reads require dbGaP authorization (phs002207). Individual transcriptomic data for ICB-treated patients may be limited.
caveats: Only 16 ICB-treated patients, and per-patient transcriptomic data for the trial subset were reported as not individually available — verify granularity before response modeling. Raw data dbGaP-controlled.

name: Open Pediatric Brain Tumor Atlas (OpenPBTA) — open processed analysis layer
description: Open, reproducible analysis of the PBTA: harmonized processed somatic mutations, fusions, copy-number, expression matrices and derived subtype calls for 1,074 tumors and 22 cell lines from 943 patients, released openly on GitHub/CAVATICA/PedcBioPortal with a download script. Successor project "Open Pediatric Cancer (OpenPedCan)" extends it across pediatric cancers. The open counterpart to the controlled PBTA raw data.
scale: 1,074 tumors + 22 cell lines, 943 patients (processed)
license: code BSD-3-Clause; processed data under CC-BY-style release (CBTN) — confirm per file

provenance.maintainer: Alex's Lemonade Stand Foundation Childhood Cancer Data Lab + CBTN

relevance.why: Ready-to-use expressed-mutation, fusion and expression matrices for pediatric brain tumors — immediately usable for antigen-candidate enumeration without clearing a DUA, with the controlled raw tier available when read-level evidence is needed.

agent_access: Fully scriptable: a single download-data.sh pulls the current release from S3; no auth. PedcBioPortal gives web/API access to processed calls.
caveats: Processed-only; read-level validation still needs the controlled PBTA tier. Confirm the per-file data license (code is BSD-3; data release terms derive from CBTN) before redistribution or ML training. Pin the release tag for reproducibility.

name: Open Targets Platform
description: Not a neoantigen DB per se: a target-identification/prioritization platform integrating genetics, genomics, expression, and cancer evidence (e.g. Project Score CRISPR screens, Cancer Gene Census, Cancer Genome Interpreter). Relevant to this domain for antigen/target gene prioritization (tumor-associated antigen genes, expression specificity) rather than peptide-level neoantigens.
scale: Whole-genome target-disease evidence; quarterly releases (tens of GB bulk)
license: CC0 1.0 (platform data); code Apache-2.0; some source datasets carry own terms

provenance.maintainer: Open Targets consortium (EMBL-EBI, Wellcome Sanger, GSK, et al.)

relevance.why: Best-licensed (CC0) route to tumor-antigen TARGET prioritization — expression specificity, tractability and cancer evidence to rank candidate antigen genes before descending to peptide level.

agent_access: Fully automatable: GraphQL + REST API, EMBL-EBI FTP, Google Cloud/BigQuery, and an AWS S3 bucket (open-targets-public-data-releases) listable without an account. No auth for public data.
caveats: Platform data are CC0 (excellent for reuse/ML), but the licence page notes individual source datasets have their own terms — e.g. Cancer Gene Census is "commercial use for Open Targets" (NOT free commercial reuse); check per-source terms before commercial use. Gene/target level, not peptide/neoantigen level.

name: PCAWG (Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes)
description: Uniform whole-genome analysis of 2,658 cancers (tumor + matched normal) across 38 tumor types, jointly from ICGC and TCGA. Deep catalog of coding and non-coding somatic drivers, structural variants, mutational signatures and whole-genome expression. Most molecular, clinical and specimen summaries are open; identifying data (germline alleles, raw reads) are controlled via both TCGA (dbGaP) and ICGC (DACO).
scale: 2,658 donors / whole genomes, 38 tumor types

provenance.maintainer: ICGC/TCGA PCAWG Consortium (DCC at OICR/EBI)

relevance.why: Only large uniform WGS cohort covering non-coding and structural variants — essential for antigens arising outside the exome (SV junctions, non-coding drivers, retained introns) that WES-only cohorts miss.

agent_access: Open molecular/consensus files (VCF/MAF) via ICGC DCC and mirrors (UCSC Xena PCAWG hub is fully open, no auth). Controlled germline/reads need dbGaP (TCGA portion) AND DACO (ICGC portion) plus token/EGA clients.
caveats: Somatic SNVs from TCGA donors require separate dbGaP authorization even within the open workflow. Dual-consortium access is the main automation barrier for read-level data.

name: PetDx OncoK9 — Canine cfDNA Liquid Biopsy (NOT public)
description: Commercial multi-cancer early-detection liquid biopsy using plasma cell-free DNA NGS in dogs (CLASSiC prospective screening study; >1,100-dog clinical validation). Catalogued for completeness; underlying data are proprietary and there is conflicting evidence the product/company may have wound down in 2024.
scale: >1,100 dogs (validation); CLASSiC prospective cohort

provenance.maintainer: PetDx, Inc.

relevance.why: Demonstrates canine cfDNA feasibility; relevant to monitoring, not to presentation/recognition modeling. No usable public data.

agent_access: No public dataset, no API. Publications only.
caveats: Proprietary and NOT redistributable; reports of 2024 discontinuation conflict with 2026 pubs — verify company status before relying on it. Included only to mark the boundary of what is public.

name: Personalized OncoGenomics POG570 (advanced/metastatic pan-cancer)
description: 570 patients with advanced and metastatic cancers of many types, profiled at BC Cancer by tumor whole-genome and RNA sequencing with matched germline. A real-world metastatic cohort (not primary-tumor, unlike TCGA) that captures treatment-resistant disease and structural variation; a long-read subset was later added. Raw reads are in EGA; processed small-mutation calls and expression TPMs are openly downloadable from the GSC.
scale: 570 advanced/metastatic tumors (WGS + RNA-seq, matched normal)
license: custom — POG data-use guidelines/restrictions; processed tier terms per GSC download page

provenance.maintainer: Canada's Michael Smith Genome Sciences Centre, BC Cancer

relevance.why: Metastatic, heavily pretreated tumors with WGS + expression — useful for seeing which antigen-generating variants persist in advanced disease and for structural-variant- derived neoantigens that exome-only cohorts miss.

agent_access: Processed small-mutation and expression files are a direct HTTPS download from the GSC (no auth, scriptable). Raw WGS/RNA-seq reads require an EGA controlled-access DAR (EGAS00001001159) negotiated with the POG data access committee.
caveats: Raw reads are EGA-controlled under POG's own data-use restrictions (not a standard open license). Confirm redistribution/ML-training terms of the processed tier on the GSC page before reuse; the download page states no explicit SPDX license.

name: PrE0505 durvalumab + platinum-pemetrexed pleural mesothelioma trial
description: Phase 2 trial (NCT02899195) of first-line durvalumab (anti-PD-L1) plus chemotherapy in 55 patients with unresectable pleural mesothelioma, with germline/somatic whole-exome and immunologic analyses correlating mutation burden and HLA with survival. A rare-cancer ICB- outcome cohort beyond the usual melanoma/RCC/urothelial sets.
scale: 55 patients (germline evaluable 44, somatic 40)

provenance.maintainer: PrECOG LLC / Johns Hopkins (Forde, Anagnostou et al.)

relevance.why: ICB-outcome mesothelioma with WXS + HLA — a low-TMB tumor where the mutation-to-response link is subtle, useful for calibrating immunogenicity models outside high-TMB cancers.

agent_access: Figure source data are open with the paper; individual-level genomics require an EGA controlled-access DAR (EGAS00001005426) with a data access committee + DTA.
caveats: Small single-arm cohort. Raw genomics EGA-controlled. A dbGaP id (phs000452) cited in the paper refers to re-analyzed prior data, not PrE0505's own deposit — do not conflate.

name: PRJDB10211 / PRJDB11462 — Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma WES + RNA-seq (Sci Rep 2023)
description: Whole-exome sequencing (SureSelect Canine All Exon V2) of 5 canine HS tumour/normal pairs (PRJDB10211) and RNA-seq of 4 HS samples (PRJDB11462). The study shows ERK and Akt pathway activation. The paper cites DRA runs DRA010452, DRA013421 and DRA013450.
scale: WES: 5 tumour + 5 normal (10 runs); RNA-seq: 4 runs

provenance.maintainer: Laboratory of Veterinary Internal Medicine, The University of Tokyo

relevance.why: Matched tumour/normal exomes allow somatic calling in HS. The domain-14 HS entry (GSE288068) is RNA-only.

caveats: The paper's RNA comparator was CD14+ monocytes from one healthy beagle, whose data are not in PRJDB11462 as far as we verified. Run-to-DRA mapping was inferred from run counts. Small n. No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJEB12081 — Canine Oral Melanoma (ENA; Hendricks)
description: ENA-hosted canine oral melanoma sequencing used in pan-tumor TMB/TP53 reanalyses; part of the canonical reusable canine WES/WGS set.
scale: oral melanoma cohort

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI ENA

relevance.why: Reusable melanoma WES/WGS for mutation/neoantigen pipelines.

agent_access: ENA bulk FASTQ (Aspera/FTP); no auth.
caveats: Reanalysis paper notes missing patient info (breed). Older reference build.

name: PRJEB24200 — Canine Mast Cell Tumours Sequencing (Sanger, Arendt; 2019)
description: Fifty canine mast cell tumour libraries (ENA strategy WXS) deposited by the Wellcome Sanger Institute. The project text frames the work around tumour behaviour and detecting metastatic versus reactive mast cells.
scale: 50 runs / 50 samples

provenance.maintainer: Wellcome Sanger Institute (with M. Arendt)

relevance.why: A further open MCT exome/capture cohort, roughly the size of PRJNA518003 (domain-14).

caveats: No linked publication found. Tumour/normal pairing and capture design are unverified. May overlap PRJEB56233 (FUR MCT). No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJEB36828 — Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma RNA-seq vs Healthy Tissue (Univ Rennes/CNRS 2020)
description: RNA-seq of canine histiocytic sarcoma compared with healthy tissue to identify dysregulated pathways, deposited by the CNRS / University of Rennes canine genetics group (7 runs).
scale: 7 samples

provenance.maintainer: Université de Rennes / CNRS (BioProject submitter)

relevance.why: An independent European HS transcriptome for cross-cohort validation against the US (GSE288068) and Japanese (PRJDB11462) sets.

caveats: No linked publication identified; this group's HS papers (e.g. PTPN11, Int J Cancer 2020) are genetic, not this RNA-seq. No explicit reuse license (INSDC).

name: PRJNA1090544 — Canine Oral Mucosal Melanoma Exomes
description: Exome sequencing of canine oral mucosal melanomas compared with human melanoma mutation spectra.
scale: oral mucosal melanoma exome cohort

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Melanoma mutation landscape; canine oral melanoma is a lead immunotherapy indication (cf. Oncept vaccine) — high-value for presentation/neoantigen work.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: VERIFY accession; mucosal (not UV-driven) melanoma — lower TMB than human cutaneous.

name: PRJNA1154710 — Canine Oral Osteosarcoma Genomics
