description: Genomic landscape of canine oral osteosarcoma; confirms SETD2 and DMD among genes mutated in ~half of samples, paralleling appendicular OSA (Gardner et al.).
scale: oral OSA tumor-normal set

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Somatic OSA variants for neoantigen candidates; recurrent SETD2/DMD biology.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ (prefetch); no auth.
caveats: Gardner et al. (2019) SETD2/DMD appendicular-OSA genome accession not confirmed here — check that paper's data-availability directly.

name: PRJNA1294405 — Canine Pulmonary Adenocarcinoma WGS/WES/RNA-seq (Vet Comp Oncol 2026) — NOT YET RELEASED
description: A genomic landscape study of 46 dogs with pulmonary adenocarcinoma (cPAC), a model for never-smoker human NSCLC: WGS on 8 tumour/normal pairs, WES on 5, and tumour-only RNA-seq on 36. It reports candidate targetable gene fusions and HER2 V659E. The paper states the data are in SRA under BioProject PRJNA1294405.
scale: 46 dogs; WGS n=8, WES n=5, RNA-seq n=36 (per paper)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Veterinary and Comparative Oncology 2026)

relevance.why: The only multi-modal canine lung cancer genomics cohort we found. Fusions and HER2 hotspot calls would give canine lung neoantigen candidates once the data are released.

caveats: Not available yet: the BioProject is registered (2025-07-21), but on 2026-11-15 NCBI SRA had 0 experiments and ENA had 0 public runs under it, so the paper's availability claim does not yet match the archive. Re-check later or contact the authors. "access: request" reflects the current practical state, not a stated policy.

name: PRJNA1354447 / PRJNA1354253 — Canine Histiocytic Sarcoma Low-pass WGS + Cell Lines (Rennes 2025)
description: Two companion BioProjects from CNRS / University of Rennes. PRJNA1354447 holds low-pass WGS of blood and tumour tissue from 10 dogs with HS (10 runs). PRJNA1354253 holds deeper WGS of 3 HS cell lines and matched blood from two affected dogs (3 runs, ~226 GB).
scale: PRJNA1354447: 10 runs; PRJNA1354253: 3 runs

provenance.maintainer: CNRS / Université de Rennes

relevance.why: Adds copy-number and structural genomic data to the HS cluster. Copy-number change is a known hallmark of HS (e.g. CDKN2A loss).

caveats: No publication yet. size_bytes is the sum of ENA FASTQ sizes (13,241,806,713 + 226,199,191,613). The low-pass data suit copy-number analysis, not SNV calling. No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJNA1399620 — Canine Hemangiosarcoma Organoid RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of 5 HSA and 5 nodular-hyperplasia patient-derived 2.5D organoid lines (orthotopic xenograft study).
scale: 10 organoid lines (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Organoid models as functional antigen-presentation substrates.

agent_access: SRA; no auth. BioSamples SAMN54501156+.
caveats: Organoid (not primary tumor) expression. VERIFY.

name: PRJNA1438806 — Canine Pulmonary Adenocarcinoma Small RNA-seq + RNA-seq (Kagoshima 2026)
description: Small RNA-seq (miRNA) and whole-transcriptome RNA-seq (mRNA and lncRNA) of lung tissue from 5 dogs with pulmonary adenocarcinoma and 6 healthy control dogs, deposited as a comparative resource.
scale: 11 dogs; 22 runs (11 RNA-seq + 11 miRNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Kagoshima University

relevance.why: This is the only public canine lung adenocarcinoma expression data we found with healthy-lung controls.

caveats: No linked publication found. Small n. No explicit reuse license (INSDC).

name: PRJNA268531 / SRP050276 — TRAF3 in Canine+Human B-cell Lymphoma
description: Sequencing from a study of TRAF3 genetic inactivation in canine and human B-cell lymphoma.
scale: canine + human lymphoma samples

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Cross-species shared driver (TRAF3) evidence.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: DOI VERIFY; older CanFam3.1-era data.

name: PRJNA376380 / PRJNA562916 / GSE95183 — Canine HSA RNA-seq Subtypes
description: RNA-seq/microarray defining canine hemangiosarcoma molecular subtypes (angiogenic, inflammatory, adipogenic); basis for ML gene-signature work.
scale: multi-cohort HSA transcriptomes

provenance.maintainer: NCBI GEO/SRA

relevance.why: Subtype-resolved HSA expression; immune (inflammatory) subtype relevant to recognition.

agent_access: GEO + SRA; no auth.
caveats: Mixed platforms; batch effects. VERIFY per-accession mapping.

name: PRJNA418842 — Canine Extreme Intestinal Polyposis WGS + RNA-seq (Oncotarget 2018)
description: Whole-genome sequencing (17 runs) and RNA-seq (28 runs) of canine intestinal tumours and normal tissue from a case of extreme intestinal polyposis. The study integrated genomic, transcriptomic and microbiome changes. A later canine colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma transcriptome study (Front Vet Sci 2023) re-analysed this project together with PRJNA396033 (Dog Genomics Resources normal tissue).
scale: 45 runs (17 WGS + 28 RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Oncotarget 2018)

relevance.why: The only open canine intestinal-tumour WGS+RNA set we found; it gives a colorectal comparator to human CRC.

caveats: Unusual phenotype (extreme polyposis), so it may not represent sporadic canine CRC. PRJNA396033 is a general dog genomics resource of normal tissues, not a tumour dataset. No explicit reuse license (INSDC).

name: PRJNA421895 — Canine Oral Melanoma Whole-Transcriptome
description: RNA-seq whole-transcriptome profiling of canine oral melanoma (radiotherapy effect + outcome gene signature).
scale: oral melanoma RNA-seq cohort

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Expression context for melanoma antigens and immune signatures.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Expression only. VERIFY accession.

name: PRJNA448733 / PRJNA685036 / PRJNA1007700 — Shetland Sheepdog iUC Genomes
description: Whole-genome (PRJNA448733, PRJNA685036) and whole-tumor (PRJNA1007700) sequencing from the Shetland-sheepdog invasive urothelial carcinoma GWAS/NIPAL1 study; arrays GSE241367, ChIP-seq GSE254079.
scale: iUC WGS + arrays + ChIP-seq

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA/GEO (NC State)

relevance.why: Germline + somatic + regulatory layers for bladder cancer; breed-predisposition genetics.

agent_access: SRA + GEO; no auth.
caveats: Spread across multiple accessions; join carefully.

name: PRJNA489159 / SRP159481 — Canine Mammary Tumor WES + WTS
description: Whole-exome (197 dogs) and whole-transcriptome (158 dogs) sequencing of canine mammary gland tumors with matched controls (185/197 WES and 64/158 WTS matched). Scientific Data resource.
scale: WES 197 dogs; WTS 158 dogs

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Large matched WES+RNA-seq mammary resource; strong substrate for neoantigen + expression pipelines.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth. Single-sample example SRX4636206.
caveats: WES and RNA-seq sample sets differ; partial matched normals.

name: PRJNA503864 / PRJNA503860 — Canine Cancer Cell-Line WES
description: Whole-exome sequencing of ~33 canine cancer cell lines (osteosarcoma, lymphoma, melanoma, hemangiosarcoma, others) for druggable-target discovery; matched normal/stroma under PRJNA503860. Underlies ICDC TCL01.
scale: ~33 cell lines (WES)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Cell lines are the most practical substrate for generating canine immunopeptidome data in-house.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: No DLA typing; cell-line genotypes drift.

name: PRJNA518003 / PRJNA576344 — Canine Mast Cell Tumour Exomes + Gene Panel (Vozdova 2020)
description: Whole-exome sequencing of canine cutaneous mast cell tumours identifying recurrent somatic mutations in 87 genes, including 10 recognized human cancer drivers (Vozdova et al., Vet Comp Oncol 2020). Exome reads are under BioProject PRJNA518003; targeted gene-panel NGS under PRJNA576344. Beyond the well-known KIT, the study flags additional recurrently mutated genes.
scale: canine MCT exomes + targeted panel

provenance.maintainer: Institute of Animal Genetics and Biotechnology / Veterinary Research Institute, Czechia

relevance.why: Mast cell tumour is one of the most common canine skin cancers and a priority under-covered tumour type; the somatic mutation set supplies candidate canine neoantigen loci beyond KIT.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (INSDC/NCBI open). Exome, not RNA — pair with MCT expression data for neoantigen prioritization. Confirm sample-vs-run counts on NCBI.

name: PRJNA552034 — Canine Hemangiosarcoma Exome (Megquier, 47 GR)
description: WES of 47 golden retriever hemangiosarcomas (+ RNA-seq of 74 multi-breed HSA) showing shared mutational landscape with human angiosarcoma (TP53, PIK3CA/PIK3R1). BioSamples SAMN12173468-561.
scale: 47 WES (GR); 74 RNA-seq (multi-breed)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA (Broad/UMN)

relevance.why: Strong dog<->human (angiosarcoma) comparative mutation set for neoantigen modeling.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Separate RNA-seq accession may exist — check paper data-availability. VERIFY.

name: PRJNA559406 / PRJNA308949 — Canine Invasive Urothelial Carcinoma RNA-seq
description: RNA-seq of 15 canine iUC tumors defining two expression clusters by BRAF V595E status (PRJNA559406); earlier iUC RNA-seq under PRJNA308949.
scale: 15 iUC tumors (+ earlier cohort)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Bladder-cancer expression clusters; BRAF-driven biology shared with human.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Small n; expression only.

name: PRJNA574196 — Canine Insulinoma Malignant-Progression RNA-seq (Sci Rep 2020)
description: Bulk RNA-seq characterizing malignant progression of canine insulinoma from normal pancreatic tissue through primary tumour to metastatic disease (Sci Rep 2020). Canine insulinoma is a spontaneous model of functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour.
scale: normal + primary + metastatic insulinoma (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Scientific Reports 2020)

relevance.why: Covers a previously uncatalogued endocrine tumour type with a stage-progression axis (normal→primary→met) useful for progression-associated antigen/expression analysis.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Accession from paper data statement; the Nature article page is access-gated — reconfirm run counts on the NCBI record.

name: PRJNA579792 — Canine Glioma WES/WGS
description: Canine glioma WES/WGS deposited in SRA; part of the reusable canine tumor sequence set (distinct from ICDC GLIOMA01's integrated multi-omic release).
scale: glioma tumor-normal set (count VERIFY)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Glioma somatic variants; cross-reference with ICDC GLIOMA01.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: Study details/sample counts VERIFY at NCBI.

name: PRJNA648932 — Canine Multicentric B-cell Lymphoma WGS (Sparks 2020)
description: Whole-genome sequencing of six dogs with multicentric B-cell lymphoma treated with CHOP — first canine lymphoma WGS cohort.
scale: 6 cases (WGS)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Genome-wide somatic variant discovery for B-cell lymphoma neoantigens.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Only 6 cases. VERIFY accession at NCBI.

name: PRJNA667767 — Australian Canine MCT KIT Mutation Amplicon Survey (Univ. Adelaide 2020)
description: Ion AmpliSeq sequencing of KIT exons and non-coding regions (upstream, downstream, splice sites, UTRs) in 67 cutaneous and 14 subcutaneous FFPE canine MCTs, linked to clinical and survival data.
scale: 81 tumours (amplicon)

provenance.maintainer: The University of Adelaide

relevance.why: A KIT variant prevalence reference, including non-coding variants, in an independent geographic cohort.

caveats: Single-gene panel. Paper DOI not located via PubMed. No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJNA677995 / PRJNA417727 — Canine Splenic HSA Exome (heterogeneity + actionable mutations)
description: Exome/deep sequencing of canine splenic hemangiosarcoma documenting extensive intra/inter-patient heterogeneity (PRJNA677995) and actionable mutations (PRJNA417727; PIK3CA, TP53, NRAS etc.).
scale: splenic HSA tumor sets

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Druggable/actionable HSA mutations; heterogeneity caution for neoantigen calling.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: High heterogeneity complicates clonal neoantigen inference. VERIFY accessions.

name: PRJNA805123 — Canine DLBCL WGS (Fanelli 2025)
description: Whole-genome sequencing of 10 canine DLBCL cases expanding the aberration spectrum.
scale: 10 cases (WGS)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Recent canine DLBCL genomes for variant/neoantigen work.

agent_access: SRA FASTQ; no auth.
caveats: Methods noted a publication-tied embargo — confirm current release status at NCBI before use.

name: PRJNA808112 — Golden Retriever B-cell Lymphoma Methylome
description: Genome-wide methylome of aggressive B-cell lymphoma in golden retrievers; reveals a conserved hypermethylome. Rare canine tumor methylation dataset.
scale: golden retriever DLBCL methylome cohort

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Epigenetic context for antigen/gene expression in lymphoma.

agent_access: SRA; no auth.
caveats: Methylation only. VERIFY accession.

name: Riaz et al. 2017 — nivolumab melanoma (pre/on-treatment WES/RNA-seq)
description: Melanoma treated with nivolumab, with paired pre- and on-treatment whole-exome and RNA-seq, enabling analysis of mutational/neoantigen dynamics and transcriptional change under PD-1 blockade.
scale: ~65-68 patients; 49 with RNA-seq (GSE91061)
license: GEO/SRA public submission (open); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Chan / Wolchok labs, Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: On-treatment timepoints capture immune-editing of the antigen landscape — valuable for modeling which presented antigens are under selection during therapy.

agent_access: RNA-seq via GEO GSE91061 (open); raw reads via the linked SRA project (SRA Run Selector), scriptable with no auth. Mutation/neoantigen tables in supplement.
caveats: Melanoma-only, modest size. SRP project ID not stated in-paper — resolve via the GEO series' SRA link.

name: Riaz 2017 nivolumab melanoma (GEO GSE91061)
description: Pre- and on-treatment tumor RNA-seq (and exome) of melanoma treated with nivolumab (anti-PD-1), response-annotated. Captures treatment-induced transcriptional change; a standard ICB response benchmark.
scale: RNA-seq: ~51 pre-treatment + ~58 on-treatment samples from ~65 patients on nivolumab

provenance.maintainer: Riaz/Chan/Wolchok et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Openly accessible paired pre/on-treatment ICB transcriptomes — useful for modeling response dynamics and neoantigen context without controlled access.

agent_access: GEO openly downloadable (GSE91061), no auth; raw reads via linked SRA. Automatable.
caveats: Open. Exome component may require SRA/dbGaP — verify if WES raw is needed. Count-per-patient vs sample differs (paired samples).

name: Rizvi et al. 2015 — NSCLC pembrolizumab (WES + neoantigen/response)
description: Non-small-cell lung cancer treated with pembrolizumab; whole-exome sequencing linking nonsynonymous mutation burden and candidate neoantigens to durable clinical benefit. One of the first demonstrations of TMB as a checkpoint-response biomarker.
scale: ~34 patients (two independent cohorts; WES)

provenance.maintainer: Chan / Rizvi labs, Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Canonical TMB/neoantigen-vs-response NSCLC dataset for benchmarking neoantigen callers against clinical benefit outside melanoma.

agent_access: Mutation annotation files (MAF), clinical and neoantigen tables are in the paper's supplementary materials (downloadable). No confirmed raw-read repository deposit.
caveats: Very small. License for the supplementary data is not explicitly stated (mark unknown); reuse likely requires citing the paper. Confirm whether raw reads were later deposited to dbGaP before relying on read-level data.

name: Rizvi 2015 NSCLC anti-PD-1 mutational landscape
description: Whole-exome sequencing of non-small-cell lung cancer treated with pembrolizumab across two cohorts, establishing nonsynonymous TMB / neoantigen burden as a correlate of PD-1 blockade benefit. Response-annotated tumor exomes.
scale: WES, discovery n=16 + validation n=18 NSCLC; nonsyn-TMB threshold ~178

provenance.maintainer: Rizvi/Chan et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Landmark TMB/neoantigen-vs-ICB-response dataset in NSCLC — a key cross-tumor-type benchmark beyond melanoma.

agent_access: UNRESOLVED: no public repository accession located in the Data Availability (dbGaP/ENA not confirmed). Likely controlled or on-request. Mutation tables are in the paper's supplement (openly readable).
caveats: download_url + license unknown; raw-data location unverified — treat as controlled/on-request until confirmed. Small cohort. Use the supplementary mutation tables for open reuse.

name: Samstein 2019 MSK-IMPACT pan-cancer TMB/ICB cohort (cBioPortal)
description: Targeted-panel (MSK-IMPACT) mutation + TMB + survival data across many cancer types, including ~1,661 checkpoint-inhibitor-treated patients, establishing TMB as a pan-cancer survival correlate after ICB. Openly released via cBioPortal / MSK data catalog.
scale: ~1,661 ICB-treated patients (+ untreated comparators); genomic + TMB + survival (MSK-IMPACT panel)
license: cBioPortal/MSK open release (free reuse; verify terms)

provenance.maintainer: Samstein/Morris/Chan et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Large OPEN pan-cancer TMB-vs-ICB-survival dataset — benchmark for TMB/neoantigen-burden signals across tumor types without controlled access.

agent_access: Open via cBioPortal (study id ~'tmb_mskcc_2018') and MSK data catalog (dataset 10452): download or REST/API. Agent-fetchable, no auth.
caveats: Panel (not WES) — TMB is panel-estimated, not full neoantigen calls. Confirm the exact cBioPortal study id before programmatic pull. License is an open release; verify specific reuse terms.

name: Samstein et al. 2019 — pan-cancer TMB & ICI survival (MSK-IMPACT)
description: ~1,660 ICI-treated patients across multiple cancer types profiled with the MSK-IMPACT targeted panel, with overall survival; established cancer-type-specific TMB cut-points for checkpoint-blockade benefit.
scale: ~1,661-1,662 ICI-treated tumors (targeted panel)
license: Open via cBioPortal (ODbL-governed hosting); cite source paper

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering; hosted on cBioPortal

relevance.why: Large real-world ICI outcome cohort for TMB priors and for calibrating per-cancer-type antigen-burden thresholds — fully open via cBioPortal API.

agent_access: Open via cBioPortal study tmb_mskcc_2018 (API + ZIP), no auth. Fully automatable.
caveats: Targeted panel (MSK-IMPACT), not WES — TMB is panel-derived; no neoantigen-level or expression data. A companion NSCLC study (nsclc_pd1_msk_2018) is separate.

name: Wellcome Sanger "FUR" Canine Tumour/Germline Targeted-Sequencing Programme (16 ENA projects)
description: Sixteen ENA projects deposited by the Wellcome Sanger Institute (2023-09 to 2024-05), each titled "FUR__Canine_<tumour>_TGS", sequencing tumour/germline pairs of common canine cancers with a targeted capture panel. The stated aim, modelled on MSK-IMPACT, is to define driver genes in companion-animal cancers. Tumour types: pancreatic carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, mast cell tumour, thyroid carcinoma, osteosarcoma, cholangiocarcinoma, colorectal carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, lymphoma, cutaneous melanoma, splenic haemangiosarcoma, histiocytic sarcoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, mammary gland carcinoma, seminoma and Sertoli cell tumour.
scale: 3,010 runs / 1,851 samples across 16 tumour types (tumour + germline); ~3.80 TB FASTQ

provenance.maintainer: Wellcome Sanger Institute

relevance.why: The largest open set of canine tumour/germline pairs we have found, covering several tumour types that have no other public genomics (cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic, basal cell, seminoma, Sertoli, gastric, hepatocellular). Matched germline allows somatic calling, and therefore canine neoantigen candidate generation, across tumour types.

agent_access: Public ENA FASTQ over FTP/HTTPS/Aspera, no auth; ENA portal filereport gives per-run URLs and sizes. Bulk size is ~3.8 TB, so plan egress and storage.
caveats: We found no canine publication describing these projects. ENA library_strategy is "WXS", but the project text describes targeted sequencing (TGS): panel content and gene list are unverified, so do not assume whole-exome coverage. Tumour/normal pairing must be rebuilt from sample metadata. No explicit reuse license (INSDC policy). Some samples may overlap with the earlier Sanger Arendt MCT project (PRJEB24200); de-duplicate by biosample. Sample counts are ENA biosamples (tumour + normal), not dogs.

name: Snyder 2014 CTLA-4 melanoma neoantigen exomes
description: Whole-exome sequencing of melanoma treated with CTLA-4 blockade, one of the first studies linking neoantigen landscape to checkpoint response. Response-annotated tumor exomes; neoantigen predictions in the paper.
scale: WES of melanoma from 64 CTLA-4-treated patients (discovery + validation)

provenance.maintainer: Chan/Snyder et al., Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Early response-annotated neoantigen cohort for CTLA-4 blockade; cross-reference with Van Allen for anti-CTLA-4 neoantigen-vs-response modeling.

agent_access: CONTROLLED: raw sequence via dbGaP (secondary sources report phs000452.v2.p1 — VERIFY the exact Snyder accession on dbGaP/NEJM supplement, as phs000452 is primarily the Van Allen study). DAR/DUA required.
caveats: Accession attribution uncertain (reported phs000452.v2.p1 from a secondary source) — confirm before relying. Controlled-access. Mutation/neoantigen summary tables are in the NEJM supplement (openly readable).

name: Snyder et al. 2017 — urothelial anti-PD-L1 multi-omic (WES/RNA-seq/TCR)
description: Exploratory multi-omic analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma treated with atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1): WES, RNA-seq and TCR sequencing with clinical response; examined systemic and somatic factors in PD-L1-blockade response/resistance.
scale: ~29-30 patients (multi-omic)
license: dbGaP DUA (reads); cBioPortal open (processed calls); Adaptive immuneACCESS (TCR)

provenance.maintainer: Chan / Hellmann labs, Memorial Sloan Kettering

relevance.why: Rare cohort pairing tumor genomics with TCR repertoire and ICI outcome — bridges antigen presentation to T-cell recognition in a non-melanoma cancer.

agent_access: Reads controlled via dbGaP phs001783. Somatic calls + CNA + clinical open on cBioPortal (blca_cmo_06155_2016, API). TCR data on Adaptive Biotechnologies immuneACCESS (snyder-2017-plosmedicine), free registration.
caveats: Accession/study-id from a secondary source — verify against the PLoS Medicine statement. Very small cohort. TCR data under Adaptive's immuneACCESS terms.

name: SRP137798 — Canine DLBCL Genomic Landscape (77 cases)
description: Genomic landscape of canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: RNA-seq + exome + genome across ~77 cases, defining clinically relevant subtypes.
scale: ~77 cases (multi-modal)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI SRA

relevance.why: Largest multi-modal canine DLBCL resource; subtype-resolved mutations and expression.

agent_access: SRA; no auth. Reused by lncRNA follow-up studies.
caveats: DOI VERIFY; mixed data types need demultiplexing by sample.

name: St. Jude Cloud (Genomics Platform + PeCan knowledgebase)
description: The largest pediatric-cancer genomic ecosystem: paired tumor/normal WGS, WXS and RNA-seq across pediatric cancers and long-term survivors, plus germline. Two front doors — the controlled-access Genomics Platform (request raw data, analyzed in-cloud without download) and the open PeCan knowledgebase of curated somatic variants from published pediatric genomes. ~1.25 PB total across open/registered/controlled tiers.
scale: ~12,000 WGS, ~7,700 WES, ~2,200 RNA-seq samples (2020); ~12,000 total in portal
license: St. Jude Cloud Data Access Agreement (committee-reviewed; no redistribution)

provenance.maintainer: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital

relevance.why: Deep pediatric tumor genomes with matched germline — a distinct mutational and HLA context from adult TCGA, important for not over-fitting antigen models to adult cancers and for pediatric-specific neoantigen candidates.

agent_access: PeCan variant pages and some summary data are open to browse/export. Raw genomics are controlled: a one-time DAC request (DocuSign for US requesters), then data are "vended" into a private cloud workspace — analysis happens in-cloud rather than by bulk download, so a pure local-fetch agent cannot pull reads.
caveats: In-cloud analysis model limits conventional bulk download of the controlled tier. DAA governs use; terms and data volumes change — verify at platform.stjude.cloud. Pediatric data carry heightened consent/redistribution sensitivity.

name: TARGET (Therapeutically Applicable Research to Generate Effective Treatments)
description: NCI pediatric cancer genomics program covering high-risk childhood malignancies (ALL, AML, neuroblastoma, Wilms tumor, osteosarcoma, kidney tumors). Multi-omic tumor/normal profiling with clinical outcomes, served through the GDC alongside TCGA.
scale: ~5,000 cases across ~6 pediatric cancer types
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs000218 for controlled data)

provenance.maintainer: NCI Office of Cancer Genomics; served via GDC

relevance.why: Pediatric tumors have low mutational burden and distinct driver landscapes; useful for testing whether antigen-discovery pipelines generalize beyond adult, high-TMB cancers and for fusion-derived neoantigen work (fusion-rich pediatric sarcomas).

agent_access: Same mechanics as TCGA via the GDC API: open derivatives tokenless; controlled reads via dbGaP phs000218 + GDC token.
caveats: Controlled data under pediatric dbGaP DUA; additional privacy sensitivity for minors. Smaller per-disease cohorts limit statistical power.

name: The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)
description: Landmark multi-omic atlas of ~11,000 patients across 33 cancer types, jointly run by NCI and NHGRI. Provides matched tumor/normal WXS, WGS (subset), RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, DNA methylation, copy-number and reverse-phase protein arrays with clinical follow-up. Now served through the GDC (harmonized) and the legacy portal; summary derivatives are openly downloadable, read-level and germline data are controlled.
scale: ~11,315 cases, 33 tumor types
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP phs000178 for controlled data)

provenance.maintainer: NCI/NHGRI; served via GDC

last_updated: project complete 2018; harmonized releases ongoing via GDC

relevance.why: The best-characterized pan-cancer cohort for linking somatic variants to expression and immune context — foundational for antigen-discovery benchmarks and for training expression/immunogenicity models on diverse tumor types.

agent_access: Open derivatives (MAF, expression matrices, clinical) via GDC API, no auth. Controlled reads/germline need dbGaP phs000178 approval + GDC token. UCSC Xena / cBioPortal mirror processed subsets with simpler bulk access (see those entries).
caveats: Must cite per TCGA publication guidelines; controlled data under dbGaP DUA with institutional signing authority and study-specific terms. Batch effects across tissue source sites are documented and need correction.

name: TCGA Breast Phenotype Research Group — breast radiogenomics (TCIA)
description: Breast MRI (DCE-MRI) and mammography imaging for TCGA-BRCA subjects together with quantitative computer-extracted image-phenotype features and their mappings to molecular/genomic data (the TCGA Breast Phenotype Research Group datasets). A reference human breast imaging-genomics resource linking radiology phenotype to transcriptomic/clinical subtype.
scale: ~84–139 TCGA-BRCA subjects with MR/MG; corresponding original DICOM ~52 GB; phenotype feature tables
license: CC BY 3.0 (corresponding original TCGA-BRCA images and feature tables)

provenance.maintainer: TCIA / TCGA Breast Phenotype Research Group (Giger, Gillies et al.)

relevance.why: Human breast imaging phenotypes mapped to TCGA molecular subtype — a model problem for multimodal radiology-to-molecular inference.

agent_access: Feature spreadsheets and corresponding original DICOM (CC BY 3.0, ~52 GB) downloadable via the TCIA wiki/NBIA API, no auth. Scriptable.
caveats: Breast collections remain CC BY 3.0 (not restricted like brain). Subject counts vary by filter (84 radiogenomics subset vs. 139 in the full TCGA-BRCA imaging collection); cite the specific subset and DOI.

name: TCGA-GBM / TCGA-LGG glioma radiogenomics (TCIA, incl. BraTS-TCGA)
description: Pre-operative brain MRI (T1, T1c, T2, FLAIR) for TCGA glioblastoma (TCGA-GBM) and lower-grade glioma (TCGA-LGG) subjects, linked to TCGA molecular data, plus derived expert tumor-segmentation labels and radiomic features (the BraTS-TCGA sets) and radiogenomic feature analyses. Core resource for imaging-genomics of glioma.
scale: ~262 glioma subjects (135 GBM + 108 LGG) with multiparametric MRI; derived segmentations/radiomics
license: Derived segmentations/radiomics CC BY 3.0; original TCGA-GBM/LGG DICOM now TCIA Restricted/Limited-Access

provenance.maintainer: TCIA / University of Pennsylvania (Bakas et al.); images from TCGA

relevance.why: Canonical imaging-genomics glioma cohort; template for relating radiology phenotype to molecular subtype, extensible to immune-microenvironment modeling.

agent_access: Derived CC BY 3.0 segmentations/radiomics downloadable via DOI/NBIA, no auth. The original TCGA-GBM/LGG DICOM images require a signed TCIA Restricted/Limited-Access License (brain collections moved off Creative Commons on 2022-01-06) — not agent-fetchable.
caveats: ACCESS RED FLAG — raw brain-MRI DICOM is NOW RESTRICTED (TCIA Limited/Restricted License, email agreement) even though derived labels remain CC BY 3.0. Do not assume open access to the images.

name: TCGA MC3 somatic mutation calls (Multi-Center Mutation Calling)
description: The consensus, reproducible somatic-mutation call set for TCGA, produced by an ensemble of seven callers with artifact filtering (~3.5M variants across ~10,000 exomes). The de facto standard TCGA mutation table for pan-cancer analyses.
scale: ~3.5M somatic variants, ~10,000 tumor exomes (33 cancer types)
license: NIH GDS Policy; PUBLIC MAF open, CONTROLLED MAF via dbGaP (phs000178)

provenance.maintainer: TCGA MC3 working group / GDC; Ellrott et al.

relevance.why: The cleanest open pan-cancer somatic-variant table for enumerating candidate neoantigens across all 33 TCGA cancer types in one harmonized file.

agent_access: Public MAF (mc3.v0.2.8.PUBLIC.maf.gz) is a single open download from the GDC publication page / GDC API — trivially automatable. CONTROLLED and validation MAFs need dbGaP phs000178 + token.
caveats: Public MAF is filtered (some low-confidence/germline-risk calls removed) — the CONTROLLED MAF has the full set. hg19-based. Confirm the exact GDC file UUID at download time.

name: TCGA PanCanAtlas harmonized derived data
description: The curated bundle of batch-corrected pan-cancer matrices released with the 2018 PanCanAtlas papers: RNA-seq expression (EB++ adjusted), RPPA protein, 27K/450K methylation, miRNA, SNP6 copy-number segments, ABSOLUTE purity/ploidy and segmented CN, PARADIGM pathway activities, and the TCGA Clinical Data Resource (CDR) survival endpoints.
scale: ~11,000 tumors, 33 cancer types (multi-omic matrices)
license: NIH GDS Policy; listed derived files open, ABSOLUTE MAF controlled

provenance.maintainer: TCGA PanCanAtlas consortium / GDC

relevance.why: One-stop harmonized expression + copy-number + purity + survival for all TCGA tumors — the substrate for antigen-expression filtering and outcome association without per-study wrangling.

agent_access: Individual files downloadable via direct GDC API links from the publication page (no auth) plus an ISB-CGC BigQuery mirror for SQL access. The ABSOLUTE somatic MAF is controlled (dbGaP). Fully automatable except that one file.
caveats: Files are release-frozen (2018); expression is EB++ batch-adjusted (document the normalization when combining with GDC current releases). Purity correction matters for variant-allele-frequency / expression interpretation.

name: The Cancer Immunome Atlas (TCIA) / Immunophenoscore
description: Pan-cancer immunogenomic resource derived from TCGA (>8,000 samples, 20 solid cancers): precomputed immune infiltrates, immune-subset expression, cancer-germline antigens, HLA alleles, PREDICTED neoantigens, tumor heterogeneity, immunophenoscore (IPS), and clinical data. Free download. Predicted/derived, not experimentally validated.
scale: >8,000 TCGA samples across 20 solid cancers; per-sample HLA, neoantigen, IPS, infiltrate tables
license: unknown (portal terms not stated; data derived from TCGA)

provenance.maintainer: Trajanoski lab, Medical University of Innsbruck

relevance.why: Ready-made pan-cancer predicted-neoantigen + HLA + immune-context tables tied to TCGA outcomes — fast substrate for target triage and immune-context modeling without running the pipeline.

agent_access: Normally a web portal with downloadable per-tumor tables (no auth). As of 2026 the portal is paused for redesign; urgent dataset/validation-file requests go to icbi@i-med.ac.at. Supplementary data also distributed with the Cell Reports paper.
caveats: Portal currently offline — availability intermittent; cannot be relied on for an automated pipeline until restored. License/terms not explicitly stated (mark unknown). Predictions are tool-dependent; re-derive with current callers for production use.

name: Thorsson et al. 2018 — The Immune Landscape of Cancer (TCGA PanImmune)
description: Immunogenomic characterization of >10,000 TCGA tumors across 33 cancer types, defining six immune subtypes and releasing a large per-sample immune feature matrix (immune cell fractions, cytolytic activity, TCR/BCR diversity, neoantigen load, signatures).
scale: >10,000 tumors, 33 cancer types; ~160 immune features per sample
license: NIH GDS Policy; feature matrix open (derived); underlying controlled data via dbGaP

provenance.maintainer: TCGA PanImmune working group / GDC; Thorsson et al.

relevance.why: Directly provides per-tumor neoantigen load, immune-cell composition and TCR/BCR diversity alongside subtype labels — a ready-made immune context layer for prioritizing antigen targets and for recognition modeling.

agent_access: The per-sample immune feature matrix is an open download (GDC PanImmune page) and is mirrored/queryable via CRI iAtlas; no auth. Automatable.
caveats: Features are derived (deconvolution/signature estimates), not direct measurements — document the methods. Raw inputs remain under TCGA access tiers.

name: TUPAC16 — Tumor Proliferation Assessment Challenge (breast WSIs)
description: Breast-cancer whole-slide-image challenge for predicting tumor proliferation from histology. 821 TCGA H&E WSIs (500 train / 321 test) with molecular proliferation ground truth derived from PAM50/RNA expression, plus auxiliary mitosis-detection and ROI tasks. A reference imaging-to-molecular (proliferation) prediction benchmark.
scale: 821 TCGA breast WSIs (500 train / 321 test); molecular proliferation scores + mitosis ROIs

provenance.maintainer: Eindhoven Univ. of Technology / consortium (Veta et al.); images from TCGA

relevance.why: Directly pairs human tumor histology with a molecular (proliferation) readout — a template task for multimodal models linking tissue morphology to transcriptomic phenotype.

agent_access: Images are TCGA-derived WSIs; access via the grand-challenge portal (registration). Underlying slides also retrievable from GDC under TCGA terms. Scriptable after registration.
caveats: No explicit dataset license located on the challenge site or journal page (marked unknown per schema; do not guess). Underlying slides inherit TCGA/GDC open-access research-use terms. Test proliferation labels are sequestered for scoring.

name: Van Allen et al. 2015 — anti-CTLA-4 melanoma (WES/RNA-seq + response)
description: Pretreatment metastatic melanoma biopsies with matched germline from 110 patients treated with ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4), with whole-exome and RNA-seq and annotated clinical benefit. A foundational cohort linking mutational/neoantigen load to checkpoint-blockade response.
scale: 110 patients (pretreatment tumor + germline WES; RNA-seq subset)
license: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (dbGaP DUA)

provenance.maintainer: Van Allen / Garraway labs, Dana-Farber / Broad

last_updated: 2015 (phs000452; later extended by Liu 2019 to v3.p1)

relevance.why: Ground-truth cohort for training/validating neoantigen-based response predictors: somatic variants + expression paired with real checkpoint-blockade outcomes.

agent_access: Raw reads (WES SAM/BAM, RNA-seq FASTQ) controlled via dbGaP phs000452; needs an approved DAR + download token. Mutation/neoantigen summary tables are in the paper's supplement (open, directly downloadable).
caveats: Controlled DUA for reads. Small cohort; melanoma-only. v2.p1 vs v3.p1 (Liu 2019) overlap — dedupe patients if combining with Liu.

name: Canine DLA-DR15/DR12 class II immunopeptidomics
description: First immunopeptidomics-derived MHC class II binding motifs for two common canine DR alleles (DLA-DRB1*015:01 / DR15 and DLA-DRB1*012:01 / DR12), the only direct canine class II ligand data available.
scale: 838 DLA-DR15-associated + 644 DLA-DR12-associated peptides

provenance.maintainer: Academic (canine immunology group); J Immunol

relevance.why: The only canine class II presentation data - essential and currently almost unique for any DLA class II modeling.

agent_access: Peptide lists in paper supplementary files; raw MS likely in PRIDE (accession not confirmed at catalog time - search PRIDE for "DLA-DR" / Canis familiaris). Partly publisher-gated.
caveats: PRIDE accession and data license UNCONFIRMED - verify in the paper's data availability statement. Only two alleles. Extremely sparse (the canine class II gap).

name: Canine DLA immunopeptidomics (primary studies)
description: The small set of primary studies that experimentally define canine MHC (DLA) peptide-binding motifs via MS elution - essentially the only direct canine immunopeptidomics data available. Includes class I (DLA-88*50101) and the first class II motifs (DLA-DRB1*015:01, DLA-DRB1*012:01), plus a canine tumor-antigen presentation set deposited in PRIDE.
scale: DLA-88*50101: ~3,720 eluted peptides (~2,436 nonamers); DLA-DR15: 838; DLA-DR12: 644; tumor set under PXD074485

provenance.maintainer: Multiple academic labs; raw data via PRIDE/ProteomeXchange

relevance.why: The core experimental substrate for canine presentation modeling. Directly enables (and bounds) Veritope's dog immuno-oncology work; everything else canine is sequence-only.

agent_access: Raw MS via PRIDE (bulk, CC0); motif/peptide lists via paper supplementary files (per-publisher access). Fetchable but scattered across papers - requires assembly.
caveats: SPARSE by design: only a handful of DLA alleles characterized, mostly class I and a couple class II. No consolidated canine atlas exists. This gap is the key comparative-oncology constraint - likely a build-it-ourselves opportunity.

name: Canine & feline lymphoma H&E nuclei-segmentation datasets
description: Publicly released canine and feline lymphoma histology (H&E) image datasets with manual nuclei segmentation, supporting a modular deep-learning pipeline for histological lymphoma classification across both species.
scale: canine + feline lymphoma H&E image sets with manual nuclei annotations (counts per repo)

provenance.maintainer: University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria group (data via a public Git repository)

relevance.why: Paired canine and feline lymphoma histology with cell-level annotation; a two-species comparative resource for hematopoietic-tumor morphology and nuclei modeling.

agent_access: Datasets stated to be publicly available through a Git link in the paper; resolve the exact repo URL and clone. No single-archive DOI located.
caveats: License not stated in the search-visible text — mark unknown and confirm at the repo. Exact image counts/format require reading the repository.

name: Canine Mammary Carcinoma (CMC) completely annotated WSI dataset
description: 21 H&E whole slide images of canine mammary (breast) carcinoma, completely annotated for mitotic figures by two expert pathologists, plus tumor-region outlines and a defined region of interest of highest mitotic count. Positioned as a canine model for human breast cancer digital pathology. Cell annotations provided in a SQLite3 database.
scale: 21 WSIs; 13,907–13,937 mitotic figures; 36,346 hard negatives

provenance.maintainer: FAU Erlangen / FU Berlin (Aubreville, Bertram, Donovan, Marzahl, Maier, Klopfleisch)

relevance.why: Explicit dog-as-human-breast-cancer-model WSI resource; comparative digital-pathology substrate linking canine mammary tumors to human breast cancer biology.

agent_access: Springer Nature figshare collection; a paper notebook auto-downloads the data from figshare. Direct download, no auth.
caveats: Mitotic-figure counts differ slightly between the paper and figshare (versioning). Confirm the CC BY 4.0 license field on the collection. Scanner: Aperio ScanScope CS2 at 0.25 um/px (file format not stated explicitly — expect SVS). Shares authorship with CATCH/MIDOG/MITOS sets.

name: Canine marginal zone lymphoma single-cell + spatial atlas (GSE343505)
description: Longitudinal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of canine marginal zone lymphoma presented as a comparative-oncology model; deposited in GEO. TCR V(D)J content not confirmed from metadata.
scale: longitudinal scRNA + spatial cohort (GSE343505)

relevance.why: Adds canine tumor immune single-cell data for the dog comparative arm; candidate source if it includes V(D)J reads.

agent_access: Open GEO series GSE343505; matrices via GEO FTP/HTTPS, automatable.
caveats: TCR V(D)J inclusion NOT confirmed — verify in the GEO record before relying on it for TCR work. DOI not located. Dog.

name: PRJNA742469 / SRP326193 — Canine Single-cell TCR + scRNA (Hoang 2024)
description: First dedicated single-cell (10x) canine TRA/TRB V(D)J + scRNA profiling, covering healthy PBMC, healthy lymph node, melanoma PBMC and lymphoma lymph node — the strongest purpose-built public canine TCR dataset found.
scale: 16 samples / 11 dogs; 77,809 V(D)J-expressing cells; 5 samples with scRNA-seq

provenance.maintainer: Griffith labs, Washington University / University of Missouri

relevance.why: THE key public canine TCR resource for a comparative-oncology (dog) arm — includes canine melanoma and lymphoma samples and custom CanFam3.1 10x references.

agent_access: Raw scRNA/scTCR FASTQs open in SRA (SRP326193) under BioProject PRJNA742469; SRA Toolkit/ENA for programmatic bulk download. Custom canine reference at genomedata.org/10X_canine_ref/.
caveats: Not antigen-labeled (no canine epitope specificity). Small cohort. No canine VDJdb/McPAS equivalent exists; this plus SRA RNA-seq reanalysis is essentially the entire public canine TCR landscape.

name: Canine TCR repertoires from public RNA-seq (SRA)
description: Canine TCR repertoires reconstructed from public dog RNA-seq in the SRA using TRUST4/MiXCR with IMGT canine references, spanning blood, lymphoid, solid tissue and tumor samples; plus companion single-cell canine TCR V(D)J atlases of healthy dogs.
scale: ~1,808 RNA-seq samples (1,361 PE + 447 SE) from ~1,063 dogs; 613 tumor samples

provenance.maintainer: various (reanalysis preprint 2024; Frontiers scRNA atlas 2023)

relevance.why: The only meaningful public canine TCR coverage found — essential for any comparative-oncology (dog) arm; raw reads are reprocessable with canine IMGT references.

agent_access: Underlying reads are public in SRA (programmatic via SRA Toolkit/ENA); derived repertoire tables depend on authors' supplements. Reprocessing is compute-heavy but fully automatable.
caveats: No single curated canine TCR database — this is reanalysis of scattered RNA-seq, so quality and annotation vary. NOT antigen-labeled. No canine equivalent of VDJdb/McPAS exists; canine coverage across all other resources in this domain is effectively zero. This is the key comparative-oncology gap.

name: Canine TCR repertoires reconstructed from public RNA-seq (SRA reanalysis)
description: Computational reconstruction of canine TCR repertoires from existing public dog RNA-seq in the SRA using TRUST4/MiXCR with IMGT canine references, across blood, lymphoid, solid tissue and tumors — the broadest (if indirect) canine TCR coverage.
scale: ~1,808 RNA-seq samples (1,361 PE + 447 SE) from ~1,063 dogs; 613 tumor samples

provenance.maintainer: (bioRxiv 2024 reanalysis)

relevance.why: Largest-breadth canine TCR coverage (incl. 613 tumor samples) for the dog comparative arm; reprocessable from open reads with canine IMGT refs.

agent_access: Underlying reads open in SRA/ENA (programmatic via SRA Toolkit); derived repertoire tables depend on the preprint's supplements. Reprocessing is compute-heavy but automatable.
caveats: Preprint (verify peer-review status). Reconstructed from bulk RNA-seq (not targeted TCR-seq); quality/annotation varies. Not antigen-labeled. Dog.

name: 7 Common Canine Tumours Cytology Dataset + Background Tiles
description: Tile-based canine cytology image dataset for CNN training to recognize seven common canine tumor types in veterinary cytology samples, plus background tiles. Inferred tumor classes from archive names: carcinoma, histiocytoma, lymphoma, melanoma, MCT (mast cell tumor), PCT (plasma cell tumor), STS (soft tissue sarcoma); includes MATLAB training code.
scale: ~1.7 GB of image tiles across 7 tumor classes + background; count not stated

provenance.maintainer: Dataset authors (deposited on Zenodo)

relevance.why: Broad-coverage (7-class) canine cytology tile set for classification; useful comparative substrate for tumor-type recognition and pretraining in companion-animal pathology.

agent_access: Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19493409), CC BY 4.0; direct download of ZIP archives (per-class: BG 236.5 MB, Carcinoma 176.2 MB, Histiocytoma 187.7 MB, Lymphoma 187.0 MB, MCT 259.6 MB, Melanoma 272.4 MB, PCT 199.9 MB, STS 201.5 MB), no auth.
caveats: Tiles are pre-processed for CNN training (not raw WSIs/FNAs); total image count and per-slide provenance not stated on the record. Class abbreviations (MCT/PCT/STS) inferred from file names.

name: Canine thoracic radiographs for VHS determination (Mendeley Data)
description: Open dataset of canine latero-lateral thoracic radiographs curated as an educational/research resource for vertebral heart score (VHS) determination, from a veterinary teaching hospital. Anonymized images with associated VHS learning materials. The main openly published canine thoracic radiograph image set with a formal data descriptor.
scale: ~152–156 anonymized radiographs (PNG)

provenance.maintainer: Flores Duenas et al., Small Animal Veterinary Teaching Hospital, Autonomous University of Baja California (Mendeley Data)

relevance.why: A rare openly licensed canine radiology dataset; seeds comparative veterinary imaging capability (cardiac/thoracic) adjacent to oncology imaging workflows.

agent_access: Mendeley Data record (DOI 10.17632/ktx4cj55pn.1), CC BY 4.0; direct download of PNG images, no auth.
caveats: Small (~152 images) and cardiology/VHS-focused, not oncology-specific. Image counts differ between the Data-in-Brief article (153) and the Mendeley record (152/156). (Note: the separate "DogHeart" cardiomegaly set exists but its repository/license were not verified and it is not catalogued here.)

name: CAnine CuTaneous Cancer Histology (CATCH) dataset
description: Pan-tumor canine cutaneous histology WSI dataset: 350 H&E whole slide images spanning seven cutaneous tumor subtypes (e.g., mast cell tumor, melanoma, histiocytoma, squamous cell carcinoma, plasmacytoma, peripheral nerve sheath tumor, trichoblastoma) with 12,424 polygon annotations across 13 histologic classes. Train/val/test split of 245/35/70 slides. Mirrored to the NCI Imaging Data Commons as DICOM.
scale: 350 WSIs; 12,424 polygon annotations; 13 classes; 522.1 GB

provenance.maintainer: Flinders/FAU group (Wilm, Aubreville, Bertram et al.); hosted by The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) and NCI Imaging Data Commons

relevance.why: Large annotated canine tumor digital-pathology resource spanning multiple skin-cancer subtypes; a substrate for comparative tumor-microenvironment and morphology models relevant to immuno-oncology.

agent_access: Open, no registration. Primary SVS images (522 GB) download via IBM Aspera Faspex (browser plugin required); annotations as JSON/SQLite. IDC DICOM mirror fetchable with the idc-index Python package ("idc download catch"). A Zenodo copy of the original data also exists (10.5281/zenodo.18526942).
caveats: Very large (522 GB) — plan storage/bandwidth. Aspera plugin complicates headless automation; prefer the IDC idc-index route for programmatic access. CC BY 4.0 requires attribution + TCIA data citation.

name: NCI Comparative Oncology Program (COP) / COTC Trials
description: NIH/NCI Center for Cancer Research program running clinical trials in pet dogs with spontaneous cancer across a ~19-site academic network (COTC). NCI provides trial design, oversight and data management (C3D real-time capture); public correlative data flow into ICDC.
scale: ~19 sites; ~10 completed studies; ~450 dogs enrolled across recent trials
license: custom (data ownership often with drug sponsor; public subset via ICDC)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CCR Comparative Oncology Program

relevance.why: The institutional backbone of U.S. comparative oncology; a partnership/data channel, not a bulk dataset. Public outputs are already in ICDC.

agent_access: Program is not itself a downloadable dataset; raw trial data ownership often sits with the drug sponsor. Access public correlatives through ICDC; trial-level data by agreement.
caveats: Sponsor-owned data not redistributable; public access is the ICDC subset only.

name: PRJEB7734-PRJEB7736 / PRJNA288568 — CTVT + 186 Canid Whole Genomes (Decker 2015)
description: Whole-genome sequencing of CTVT tumours alongside 186 canid reference genomes (dogs, wolves, coyotes) used to reconstruct the CTVT somatic mutation landscape and evolutionary history (Decker et al., Genome Research 2015). Reads are split across ENA BioProjects PRJEB7734-PRJEB7736 (submitter deposits) and NCBI PRJNA288568.
scale: CTVT genomes + 186 canid WGS

provenance.maintainer: Transmissible Cancer Group, University of Cambridge; Wellcome Sanger Institute

relevance.why: Deepest somatic-mutation characterization of a transmissible canine cancer plus a large canid germline panel — a somatic/germline contrast useful for canine variant filtering and for understanding long-term tumour-genome evolution.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (INSDC open-access). Reads span multiple projects across ENA and NCBI; de-duplicate samples before combining. Large WGS — plan storage/egress.

name: SAMEA2358413 / SAMEA2358415 — Original CTVT Founder Genomes (Murchison 2014)
description: The two CTVT genomes first sequenced by Murchison et al. (Science 2014), which established the ~11,000-year origin and ~1.9M somatic substitutions of the CTVT clone (Australia and Brazil tumours). Deposited as ENA biosamples SAMEA2358413 (genome 1) and SAMEA2358415 (genome 2); reused by downstream CTVT studies.
scale: 2 CTVT tumour genomes (WGS)

provenance.maintainer: Wellcome Sanger Institute; Transmissible Cancer Group, Cambridge

relevance.why: Foundational CTVT genomes; anchor for mutational-signature and clonal-cancer comparisons across the canine oncology dataset.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (INSDC). These are sample accessions, not a BioProject — resolve to runs via ENA before download. Only two genomes; use with Decker 2015 panel.

name: Dog Aging Project (DAP) Curated Open Data
description: Large prospective longitudinal cohort of US companion dogs (the "Pack") with annual owner surveys (Health and Life Experience Survey), electronic veterinary medical records, environmental data, and a multi-omic "precision" sub-cohort. Disease-outcome fields include cancer diagnoses, making it a population-scale resource for canine cancer epidemiology and healthy-aging baselines. Annual Curated Data releases are shared with outside researchers at a ~one-year lag.
scale: ~50,188 dogs in the 2024 Curated Data Open Access Release v1.1; tens of thousands enrolled

provenance.maintainer: Dog Aging Project consortium (University of Washington, Texas A&M; data curated/hosted on Terra, Broad Institute); NIH/NIA U19 funded

last_updated: 2024 (Curated Data Open Access Release v1.1; annual March releases)

relevance.why: Population-scale canine health and cancer-incidence data to anchor comparative-oncology epidemiology and to define healthy companion-dog baselines against which tumor cohorts are read.

agent_access: Not directly fetchable. Requires an online Application for Data Access plus a signed DAP Data Use Agreement; approved users get Terra credentials and work in the Terra workspace. Codebooks are public (Terra workspace and the DAP public GitHub). Commercial use is negotiated separately.
caveats: Access is gated by a DUA (nonprofit/research use); no SPDX license stated — flag before any redistribution or ML-training use. One-year access lag behind internal releases. Cancer outcomes are owner/clinic-reported, not centrally pathology-verified.

name: Golden Retriever Lifetime Study (GRLS) — Bette M. Morris Data Commons
description: Prospective lifetime cohort of ~3,000 US Golden Retrievers followed since 2012 with annual owner and veterinary questionnaires, physical exams, clinicopathology, and a biorepository (blood, serum, DNA, urine, feces, hair, toenails). Cancer is a primary study endpoint (Goldens have high lifetime cancer risk). Eleven subject areas: activity, behavior, dental, disease diagnoses, diet, environment, grooming, geography, medications, physical exams, reproduction.
scale: ~3,000 dogs, 10+ years of annual follow-up

provenance.maintainer: Morris Animal Foundation

relevance.why: Deep single-breed longitudinal phenotyping with a matched biorepository; a controlled model for cancer-incidence and risk-factor analysis and for linking phenotype to future biosample assays.

agent_access: Not agent-fetchable. Data Commons access requires credentialed academic/nonprofit/government affiliation, account creation, and agreement to a data use agreement; samples require a separate call-for-proposals. Commercial requests are case-by-case.
caveats: Single-breed (Golden Retriever) — limits generalizability. DUA-gated; no SPDX license published. Samples are not downloadable (physical biorepository, proposal-based).

name: GSE250310 — Canine Meningioma Molecular Classes / Human MenG C Counterpart (Acta Neuropathol 2024)
description: RNA-seq of 62 canine meningiomas. The tumours separate into molecular classes, and an aggressive class (chromosomal instability, cell-cycle activation, high MKI67) mirrors the aggressive human MenG C group. BioProject PRJNA1053343.
scale: 62 tumours, 62 runs

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — Acta Neuropathologica 2024)

relevance.why: Largest open canine meningioma cohort, with an explicit mapping to a human molecular class. It supports cross-species validity arguments for brain tumours beyond glioma.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI). The same group registered DNA-methylation BioProjects (PRJNA1046409, PRJNA1045298) that we did not verify; check them separately.

name: NCI Integrated Canine Data Commons (ICDC)
description: NCI Cancer Research Data Commons (CRDC) node aggregating harmonized canine cancer data — clinical/biospecimen metadata, bulk RNA-seq, WGS, WES, genotyping arrays and DNA methylation — across spontaneous companion-dog tumors. Data come from the Comparative Oncology Program/COTC, PRECINCT, and individual canine researchers, structured to the ICDC data model and queryable by cohort. Current studies (12): COTC007B, COTC022 (appendicular osteosarcoma SOC), GLIOMA01 (comparative glioma), MGT01 (mammary/breast), NCATS-COP01 (canine-human transcriptomics), ORGANOIDS01 (urothelial organoids), OSA01 (osteosarcoma multi-platform), OSA03 (human+canine osteosarcoma WGBS), TCL01 (canine cancer cell-line WES), UBC01 (vemurafenib in BRAF-mutant bladder cancer), UBC02 (urothelial subtypes + immune signatures), UC01 (urothelial WES, BRAF-V595E-negative).
scale: ~35 TB; ~11-12 studies, ~678 cases, ~937 samples (figures vary by release)
license: custom (open access; use with attribution; no named SPDX license)

provenance.maintainer: NCI Center for Biomedical Informatics & Information Technology (CBIIT) / CRDC

last_updated: 2026-06 (CRDC update: +44 COTC022 files, Data Model Navigator refresh)

relevance.why: Primary open canine oncology multi-omics resource; anchors Veritope's comparative strategy. Rich on genomics/transcriptomics but carries NO MHC-ligand, immunopeptidome or TCR data — a gap we must fill from elsewhere or generate ourselves.

agent_access: REST API + web portal; cohort building then analysis in CRDC Cloud (Seven Bridges Cancer Genomics Cloud). Metadata queryable programmatically; large sequence files (BAM/VCF) are cloud-hosted. No login for open data; no documented hard rate limits but prefer the API over scraping the Angular SPA (the HTML is JS-rendered and returns no content to plain fetchers).
caveats: No explicit SPDX license — "open access with attribution" only; confirm redistribution terms per study. Per-study case/sample counts not exposed on static pages (need API/portal). Portal is a single-page app, so direct curl of /#/explore yields no data — use the API.

name: ICDC COTC007B
description: COTC preclinical trial comparing three indenoisoquinoline (topoisomerase-I inhibitor) drug candidates in tumor-bearing dogs, with pharmacodynamic/correlative data. Early ICDC clinical-trial study.
scale: small trial cohort (tumor-bearing dogs)

provenance.maintainer: NCI Comparative Oncology Program / CRDC

relevance.why: Demonstrates the COTC->ICDC data pipeline for PK/PD; no omics presentation layer.

agent_access: ICDC API / portal; open, no auth.
caveats: Clinical/PK only; no genomics or immune data.

name: ICDC COTC022 — Appendicular Osteosarcoma Standard-of-Care
description: Prospective COTC trial of standard-of-care in dogs with appendicular osteosarcoma; genomics + transcriptomics correlatives. Transcriptomes mirrored in GEO GSE238110 (see below). Actively updated.
scale: trial cohort (dozens of dogs); +44 files added 2026-06

provenance.maintainer: NCI Comparative Oncology Program / CRDC

relevance.why: Osteosarcoma is a flagship comparative (dog<->pediatric human) indication; clean trial-linked genomics for modeling tumor genetics, though no antigen-presentation layer.

agent_access: Via ICDC API / CGC; same access model as parent ICDC.
caveats: No immune/MHC data. Counts only via API.

name: ICDC GLIOMA01 — Comparative Canine/Human Glioma Genomics
description: Multi-omic molecular life-history study of spontaneous canine (and matched human) gliomas; the TCIA companion collection (ICDC-Glioma) holds imaging for the same subjects.
scale: ~81 subjects (multi-omic)
license: custom (ICDC open access); TCIA imaging CC BY 4.0

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC / The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA)

relevance.why: Paired cross-species omics + imaging; strong template for comparative tumor-biology modeling.

agent_access: Genomics via ICDC API; imaging via TCIA REST API (NBIA) — bulk DICOM download supported.
caveats: No MHC/immunopeptidome/TCR layer; glioma is immunologically cold.

name: ICDC MGT01
description: Molecular comparison of canine mammary gland tumors and human breast cancer (genomics).
scale: genomics cohort (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: Breast/mammary cross-species comparison; hormone-driven tumor biology.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No immune/MHC data. Counts only via API.

name: ICDC NCATS-COP01
description: NCATS/Comparative Oncology Program canine-human transcriptomics study for diagnosing/treating cancers.
scale: transcriptomics cohort (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC / NCATS

relevance.why: Cross-species transcriptomic reference for drug repurposing.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No MHC/immune layer; counts via API.

name: ICDC ORGANOIDS01
description: Healthy and urothelial-carcinoma canine organoids for personalized-medicine modeling (genomics).
scale: organoid panel (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: Organoids are candidate substrates for functional presentation assays.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: No native immune data; counts via API.

name: ICDC UBC01
description: Clinical trial of vemurafenib activity in dogs with BRAF-mutant bladder (urothelial) carcinoma.
scale: trial cohort (count via API)

provenance.maintainer: NCI CRDC

relevance.why: BRAF-targeted therapy response in dogs; translational to human BRAF cancers.

agent_access: ICDC API; open.
caveats: Counts via API; no immune layer.

name: Kaabinejadian/Yari 2026 canine & human tumor DLA/HLA immunopeptidome
description: The most substantial canine (DLA) class I immunopeptidomics release to date: DLA-bound peptides eluted from canine tumors (osteosarcoma, anal sac carcinoma, oral melanoma) and DLA-transduced mono-allelic cells, with matched human HLA data showing shared tumor antigen peptides across species.
scale: Canine tumors: e.g. 7,520 (oral melanoma, DLA-88*003:02/*006:01/*017:01), 1,335 (anal sac, DLA-88*004:02), plus DLA-88*501:01/*501:02; mono-allelic DLA cells
license: MS: CC0 1.0 (PRIDE default); RNA-seq: SRA BioProject terms

provenance.maintainer: University of Oklahoma HSC (Hildebrand lab); PRIDE + SRA

relevance.why: THE anchor canine presentation dataset for Veritope: real DLA-eluted tumor peptides across multiple DLA-88 allotypes, and direct evidence of canine/human shared tumor antigens - the cross-species bridge the thesis depends on.

agent_access: MS: PRIDE/ProteomeXchange PXD074485 (open, bulk-downloadable). Canine tumor RNA-seq: SRA BioProject PRJNA1428288. No auth.
caveats: Still only a handful of DLA-88 allotypes and almost entirely class I; DLA class II barely covered. Raw MS needs reprocessing. Nonetheless the richest canine source - directly addresses the canine data gap flagged across this domain.

name: MIDOG++ multi-domain mitotic figure dataset
description: Comprehensive multi-domain mitotic-figure detection dataset spanning seven tumor types from human and canine cases (breast carcinoma, lung carcinoma, lymphosarcoma, neuroendocrine tumor, cutaneous mast cell tumor, cutaneous melanoma, (sub)cutaneous soft tissue sarcoma), across multiple scanners. Underpins the MIDOG challenge series on domain-robust mitosis detection.
scale: 11,937 mitotic figures (vs 14,351 imposter cells) across 503 tumor specimens, 7 tumor types

provenance.maintainer: DeepMicroscopy / FAU Erlangen & collaborators (Aubreville, Bertram et al.)

relevance.why: Mixed human+canine annotated mitosis benchmark; directly supports cross-species digital-pathology model development where canine tumors serve as comparative models of human cancers.

agent_access: figshare collection (DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.6615571), CC BY 4.0, direct download no auth.
caveats: ROI images rather than full WSIs; file format not stated on the landing page — confirm on figshare. Challenge test sets may carry separate terms. Overlaps in provenance with CATCH/MITOS_WSI_CCMCT (shared authors) — dedup on specimen identity if combining.

name: MITOS_WSI_CCMCT — canine cutaneous mast cell tumor mitotic-figure WSI dataset
description: Large-scale, completely annotated whole-slide dataset of canine cutaneous mast cell tumor for mitotic-figure assessment: 32 H&E WSIs selected across low- and high-grade cases, with 44,880 mitotic-figure annotations plus secondary annotations for neoplastic mast cells, granulocytes, and mitotic look-alikes. Cell annotations provided as a SQLite database.
scale: 32 WSIs; 44,880 mitotic figure annotations

provenance.maintainer: DeepMicroscopy group (Bertram, Aubreville et al.), FAU Erlangen; data on Springer Nature figshare

relevance.why: Deeply annotated single-tumor-type canine WSI set for mitosis and cell-level modeling; a building block for canine tumor-grading and TME-adjacent digital-pathology work.

agent_access: Code/notebooks on GitHub (DeepMicroscopy); individual WSIs (~1 GB each) and annotation DB on Springer Nature figshare, CC BY 4.0, direct download. No single-archive bulk link — fetch per-slide.
caveats: Large per-slide SVS files. Confirm the CC BY 4.0 license on each figshare item. Shares authorship with MIDOG++/CMC — potential specimen overlap; dedup before pooling.

name: PetHIS — pet histopathological image database
description: Histopathological image database for training CNNs to classify cancer in pets, labeled benign vs malignant. Built from 82 original images expanded by augmentation (flips, random crop) to 592 labeled images; sourced from a Brazilian veterinary pathology laboratory.
scale: 82 original images augmented to 592 labeled (benign/malignant) images; 942 MB

provenance.maintainer: Laboratory of Veterinary Medicine, State University of Maranhao / Federal Institute of Maranhao (Brazil)

relevance.why: Small, clean benign/malignant companion-animal histopathology set; a lightweight comparative classification resource and augmentation reference.

agent_access: Single ~942 MB ZIP ("Base de dados PetsHI.zip") on Zenodo, CC BY 4.0, direct download no auth.
caveats: Very small base (82 originals); the 592 count is augmentation-inflated — do not treat augmented copies as independent samples. Binary labels only (no tumor subtype).

name: PRJEB10386 — Golden Retriever Mast Cell Tumour Germline Risk Resequencing (Uppsala; PLoS Genet 2015)
description: Pooled targeted resequencing (ENA strategy POOLCLONE; 17 pools, 62 runs) of GWAS-associated regions in MCT-affected and control Golden Retrievers, used to fine-map germline risk loci for mast cell tumours.
scale: 17 pooled samples, 62 runs

provenance.maintainer: Uppsala University

relevance.why: Germline risk architecture for a common canine cancer; the background needed to interpret breed effects in MCT somatic data.

caveats: Pooled DNA, so the data give no individual genotypes. Matched to the 2015 GWAS paper by submitter, date and design; the paper's accession statement was not read. No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJEB19508 — CTVT Regression RNA-seq (Frampton 2018)
description: Bulk RNA-seq of serial biopsies from canine transmissible venereal tumours (CTVT) undergoing vincristine-induced and natural regression vs. non-regressing tumours. The study (Frampton et al., Cancer Cell 2018) identified immune/inflammatory regression signatures and proposed CCL5 as a candidate driver of tumour rejection. CTVT is a naturally transmissible clonal cancer — a unique model of allogeneic tumour rejection and immune escape in an outbred canine host.
scale: serial biopsies, regressing + non-regressing CTVT (RNA-seq)

provenance.maintainer: Transmissible Cancer Group, University of Cambridge (Murchison lab)

relevance.why: Rare in vivo transcriptomic record of spontaneous immune-mediated tumour regression against an allogeneic (foreign-genotype) tumour; directly informs what a successful anti-tumour immune response looks like at the expression level.

agent_access: ENA bulk FASTQ over HTTPS/FTP via Browser API or Aspera, no auth. Programmatic filereport endpoint (result=read_run) returns run accessions and download paths.
caveats: No explicit reuse license (ENA/INSDC open-access policy applies; cite the paper). CTVT is clonal — tumour genotype differs from the host dog, so host-matched analyses require care. Confirm run-level accessions on the ENA record before bulk pull.

name: SRP046723 — Canine Oral / Head-and-Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (PLoS Genet 2015)
description: Sequencing of canine spontaneous head-and-neck / oral squamous cell carcinomas shown to recapitulate their human counterparts at the molecular level (PLoS Genetics 2015). SRA study SRP046723.
scale: canine HNSCC/OSCC cohort

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — PLoS Genetics 2015)

relevance.why: Explicit canine-human HNSCC molecular-equivalence dataset; a template for the cross-species validity argument central to the comparative-oncology thesis.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Confirm exact assay/sample composition on the SRA study record; accession taken from downstream citation.

name: Swiss Canine Cancer Registry (SCCR) data 2008–2020
description: Registry extract of canine tumor cases in Switzerland (2008–2020) diagnosed by histology (biopsy and necropsy) and cytology at four veterinary pathology laboratories, coded with Vet-ICD-O-canine-1. Supports incidence-rate estimation per 100,000 dog-years overall and by breed and tumor morphology.
scale: 54,986 tumors; 7,135,182 dog-years at risk

provenance.maintainer: Institute of Veterinary Pathology, Vetsuisse Faculty, University of Zurich (Guscetti, Dhein et al.)

relevance.why: Breed- and morphology-resolved canine cancer incidence from a defined pathology-confirmed registry; a reference for tumor-type prevalence weighting and breed-risk comparison.

agent_access: Single 15.0 MB Excel workbook ("Dataset SCCR, 2008-2020.xlsx") on Zenodo; direct download, no auth.
caveats: Zenodo shows "Open" access but no explicit SPDX license is displayed — mark license unknown and confirm before redistribution. Some sensitive fields withheld under local law. Diagnoses coded in Vet-ICD-O-canine-1 (needs mapping to other oncology ontologies).

name: Veterinary Cytological Images segmentation dataset (CYFROVET)
description: Annotated veterinary cytology image dataset for neoplastic-tumor diagnosis: ~1,206 images across four categories — three round-cell tumor types (lymphoma, histiocytoma, mastocytoma) plus inflammation — with per-cell annotations (tumor cells, neutrophils, damaged cells) supporting segmentation and detection. (A detection variant lists 1,219 images / 28,149 objects.)
scale: ~1,206 images, 4 categories (detection variant: 1,219 images, 28,149 objects)

provenance.maintainer: Grzeszczyk et al. (Warsaw University of Technology / Sano Centre); hosted on PLGrid GitLab

relevance.why: Canine cytology (not histology) image resource for round-cell tumors; complements WSI datasets with fine-needle-aspirate morphology relevant to practical comparative diagnostics.

agent_access: Hosted on a PLGrid GitLab instance (git.plgrid.pl); repository access/clone method and rate limits unverified — may require navigating the GitLab UI. No Zenodo mirror found.
caveats: No explicit license located — mark license unknown and confirm before reuse/ML training. Image count differs between segmentation (1,206) and detection (1,219) variants (versioning).

name: Veterinary Medical Database (VMDB)
description: National database of standardized veterinary clinical records (demographics, dates, diagnoses, procedures) contributed by North American university teaching hospitals since 1964; diagnoses coded in SNOMED. Widely used for retrospective cancer-demographics and disease-frequency studies across species, though skewed toward referral-hospital caseloads.
scale: >7 million records from 26 US/Canadian university teaching hospitals

provenance.maintainer: Veterinary Medical Database, housed at Purdue University since 1988

relevance.why: Long-running, SNOMED-coded multi-species diagnosis corpus; a historical denominator and tumor-demographics source for comparative oncology across dogs and cats.

agent_access: Not agent-fetchable. Data are provided on request for a fee (fee waived for researchers at participating institutions). No public bulk download or API.
caveats: Strong referral bias (teaching-hospital caseloads over-represent rare/severe disease). Fee/request gated; no public license. Confirm the site is live before relying on access terms.

name: AB-Bind (antibody binding mutational database)
description: Curated set of experimental binding free-energy changes (ddG) for point and multiple mutations in antibody-antigen (and related) complexes, each mapped to a solved PDB structure. Built as a benchmark for computational affinity- change prediction.
scale: 1,101 mutational variants across 32 antibody-antigen complexes, each with measured ddG

provenance.maintainer: Keating Lab, MIT (Sirin, Apgar, Bennett, Keating)

relevance.why: A focused antibody-antigen ddG benchmark for affinity-maturation / binder-optimization models — smaller and more antibody-specific than SKEMPI, and routinely paired with it for evaluation.

agent_access: Dataset lives in the Protein Science article's supplementary files; copies are widely mirrored on GitHub by reusers. No API; fetch the SI tables.
caveats: No explicit data license on the SI (mark unknown; confirm before redistribution). Small and well-trodden — risk of train/test leakage with SKEMPI 2.0 (overlapping complexes). Some entries are non-antibody PPIs.

name: AbRank — antibody-antigen affinity ranking benchmark
description: A large aggregated antibody-antigen binding benchmark reframing affinity prediction as pairwise ranking, pooling >380,000 binding assays from nine public sources with a fold-difference filter to form robust train/test pairs. Ships a metric-learning framework and standard splits.
scale: >380,000 binding assays aggregated from 9 sources; main CSV ~296 MB

provenance.maintainer: Plissier et al. (AbRank)

relevance.why: A ready-made, de-leaked ranking benchmark across many antibody-antigen affinity sources — directly usable to evaluate binder affinity-ranking models without rebuilding the aggregation.

agent_access: Dataset on Kaggle (Kaggle account/registration to download); code + splits on GitHub (biochunan/AbRank-WALLE-Affinity).
caveats: Aggregates sources ALREADY in or overlapping this catalog (AlphaSeq, SAbDab, SKEMPI-v2, HER2-binders, CATNAP, RBD-escape, Ab-CoV, AIntibody) — major dedup/leakage risk if combined with their primary entries. Kaggle download requires registration. Per-source licenses are inherited and mixed; the aggregate has no single stated data license (mark unknown).

name: Absci de novo anti-HER2 antibody binders (Shanehsazzadeh 2023)
description: Open-sourced experimental results from a generative de novo antibody-design campaign: >400,000 HER2-targeted variants screened, with 421 SPR-validated binders and their measured affinities (KD), including Fab/mAb affinities and cross-species (cyno/mouse/canine) HER2 binding. A rare released wet-lab output of a real binder-design pipeline.
scale: >400,000 designed variants screened; 421 SPR-characterised binders with KD

provenance.maintainer: Absci Corporation (Shanehsazzadeh et al.)

relevance.why: Direct precedent and benchmark for the binder-design program: real generative-design outputs with experimental SPR validation against a defined target, exactly the task Veritope aims to do for its targets.

agent_access: CSV files in the AbSciBio GitHub repo (zero-shot-binders.csv etc.); clone to fetch. No API/auth.
caveats: Single target (HER2). Repo license not explicitly stated (mark unknown; confirm reuse terms). Preprint, not peer-reviewed; selection pipeline biases the released positives.

name: Absolut! in silico antibody-antigen binding database
description: A large synthetic (in silico) antibody-antigen binding dataset: CDR-H3 sequences docked against lattice representations of real PDB-derived antigens with an exhaustive, deterministic binding energy for every pose. Designed to give unconstrained, fully-labelled ground truth for benchmarking antibody specificity / binding-prediction ML without experimental noise.
scale: ~159 lattice antigens; ~6.9M murine CDR-H3 sequences; on the order of ~1 billion antibody-antigen binding pairs

provenance.maintainer: Greiff lab (University of Oslo) and collaborators; hosted on Norstore/Sigma2

relevance.why: Fully-labelled, noise-free antibody-antigen binding ground truth at scale — a controlled benchmark for the recognition models and generative-design scoring that underpin the binder program, complementing noisy real assays.

agent_access: Pre-generated files downloadable over HTTPS from the Sigma2/Norstore mirror (no auth); the Absolut! C++ code (csi-greifflab/Absolut) can regenerate or extend data but generation can take days. Large; pull selectively.
caveats: Explicit reuse license not clearly stated on the mirror (license: unknown) — confirm via the Norstore DOI before redistribution; attribute Robert et al. 2022. SYNTHETIC/lattice data — a proxy for real binding, useful for method development but not a substitute for experimental affinities.

name: AlphaSeq antibody-affinity dataset (anti-SARS-CoV-2 scFv)
description: A large quantitative antibody-antigen affinity dataset: scFv-format antibodies assayed by the AlphaSeq yeast-mating platform against a SARS-CoV-2 HR2 peptide, with predicted KD values spanning ~37 pM to ~22 mM. One of the largest single-target experimental affinity datasets released.
scale: 104,972 scFv designs built into the library; ~71,384 with an affinity value (triplicate)

provenance.maintainer: MIT Lincoln Laboratory / A-Alpha Bio (Engelhart et al.)

relevance.why: A dense, quantitative affinity landscape against one target — ideal for training/benchmarking affinity-prediction and affinity-maturation models central to binder design.

agent_access: Single CSV on Zenodo (plus GitHub mit-ll/AlphaSeq_Antibody_Dataset), no auth. Trivial to automate.
caveats: Affinities are platform-"predicted" (AlphaSeq normalized scores), not SPR KD; single antigen/epitope. Minor count discrepancies between the paper and downstream benchmarks (~71.4k vs ~71.8k) — verify against the Zenodo file.

name: AlphaSeq antibody-antigen binding dataset (SARS-CoV-2 peptide)
description: A large quantitative antibody-antigen binding dataset: ~105,000 scFv antibody variants assayed by the AlphaSeq yeast mating-based platform against a SARS-CoV-2 spike HR2 peptide, giving sequence-resolved, replicate, predicted affinity values. Built explicitly as a public ML benchmark pairing antibody sequence, antigen sequence and quantitative binding.
scale: ~104,972 antibodies vs a SARS-CoV-2 peptide; affinities ~37 pM to ~22 mM; 3 phage-display seed sequences with ~30k variants per library set

provenance.maintainer: MIT Lincoln Laboratory; data from A-Alpha Bio (Engelhart et al.)

relevance.why: One of the largest public datasets with real quantitative antibody binding affinities tied to sequence — a direct supervised benchmark for the recognition/affinity-prediction models behind binder design.

agent_access: Two public releases hosted by MIT Lincoln Laboratory (Dataset 1: original AlphaSeq set; Dataset 2: ML-designed antibodies measured experimentally). CSV with sequences, CDRs, replicate IDs and log-scale nM affinity. Download via the MIT LL page.
caveats: Each release subdirectory carries its own license (overall license: unknown until checked per subdir) — read before reuse; attribute Engelhart et al. 2022. Affinities are platform-predicted (AlphaSeq), replicate-averaged; blanks denote poor/non-binders. Single antigen (SARS-CoV-2 HR2 peptide).
