relevance.why: Population allele frequencies decide which HLA alleles to prioritize for population coverage in presentation/design (shared-antigen vaccine or TCR design).

agent_access: Native access is paginated HTML tables (scrape-only, no clean bulk API) - a real friction point for agents. Community mirrors exist: slowkow/allelefrequencies (single afnd.tsv, MIT-licensed repo) and the HLAfreq Python package automate download/combination. Prefer those for bulk pulls.
caveats: AFND's own site has "Licensing" and "Disclaimer" pages that were not retrievable at catalog time - data license marked unknown; confirm before redistribution. AFND asks you to also cite the ORIGINAL publication of each dataset used. Community mirror's MIT license covers the repo/code, not the underlying frequencies.

name: AntiRef (reference clusters of human antibody sequences)
description: Non-redundant reference clusters of human antibody sequences derived by clustering large public repertoire data at multiple identity thresholds, analogous to UniRef for antibodies. Provides representative sequences that collapse the massive redundancy of raw repertoires into tractable, deduplicated reference sets for search and model training.
scale: Clustered sets at several identity thresholds (e.g. 100/90/.../50% id); tens of millions of representatives depending on threshold

provenance.maintainer: Briney lab, The Scripps Research Institute

relevance.why: Deduplicated antibody reference sets give cleaner training/search corpora than raw repertoires, reducing sampling bias when pretraining antibody models or searching for natural analogues of a designed binder.

agent_access: Distributed via GitHub with downloadable FASTA cluster files (hosted on public object storage per the repo). No auth. Scriptable.
caveats: No explicit data license surfaced — treat as unconfirmed (license: unknown) and attribute Briney 2023. Human only; derived product (clustering choices affect downstream stats). Unpaired.

name: BarkBase — Canine Epigenomic Annotation
description: Epigenomic reference for the dog: RNA-seq, WGS and ATAC-seq across 27 adult tissues (with replicates) plus staged embryonic timepoints, with a download portal. Foundational for regulatory annotation of the canine genome.
scale: 27 adult tissues + embryonic timepoints; 37/46 ATAC-seq libraries passed QC
license: unknown (portal download; SRA raw reads public-domain norms)

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute / UMass Chan (Karlsson/Megquier)

relevance.why: Tissue-level regulatory annotation helps interpret expression context of tumor antigens; a baseline for "self" expression used in neoantigen filtering.

agent_access: Portal downloads + SRA raw reads (project IDs in supp. Table S1); no auth.
caveats: ATAC-seq quality limited (many samples FRiP <0.3, below ENCODE threshold); not ENCODE-depth. No MHC/immune-specific layer. License not explicitly stated.

name: Big Fantastic Database (BFD)
description: One of the largest publicly available clustered protein-sequence databases, built for deep MSA generation in AlphaFold2. Contains 65,983,866 protein families as MSAs and profile HMMs covering ~2.2 billion sequences, clustered at 30% identity / 90% coverage from UniProt, Metaclust, the Soil Reference Catalog and the Marine Eukaryotic Reference Catalog (~2.5B input sequences).
scale: 65,983,866 families / clusters; ~2,204,359,010 clustered sequences (~2.5B input)

provenance.maintainer: Steinegger / Mirdita / Söding (Söding Lab, MMseqs2 ecosystem); produced for AlphaFold

relevance.why: Massive clustered metagenome-inclusive corpus for deep MSA construction and large-scale PLM pretraining; reaches far beyond UniProt into environmental sequence space relevant to novel-fold and representation learning.

agent_access: Direct HTTP(S) bulk download (Google Cloud and GWDG mirrors); ~272 GiB tarball, aria2c recommended. No auth. Plan for very large disk/RAM footprint.
caveats: Frozen 2021 build (not updated). Enormous download. Derived inputs include Metaclust, which is CC BY-NC-SA (see metaclust entry) — BFD itself is released CC BY 4.0, but confirm downstream terms if redistributing derivatives. Clusters with <3 sequences removed.

name: BioGRID (Biological General Repository for Interaction Datasets)
description: Manually curated database of physical and genetic protein/gene interactions, plus chemical and post-translational-modification interactions, drawn from the primary literature and high-throughput datasets. Interactions are evidence-typed and experiment- attributed.
scale: >2.9M protein/genetic interactions, >1M chemical interactions, ~80k publications

provenance.maintainer: BioGRID team (Princeton, Mount Sinai Toronto, others)

relevance.why: MIT-licensed (commercially usable) curated physical/genetic interaction edges for building interaction features around antigen-processing and immune-signaling proteins; PTM interactions add regulatory detail.

agent_access: Open bulk downloads (TAB2/MITAB/PSI-MI, monthly archives) under MIT; REST API with a free access key. Fully automatable and redistributable with attribution.
caveats: Data are MIT (free for commercial + academic, cite Stark 2006 + Oughtred 2021); the article text is CC BY 4.0 — keep separate. Curation is literature-driven, so coverage is biased toward well-studied proteins; dog interactions are sparse.

name: BV-BRC viral/bacterial epitope features (ex-ViPR / ex-IRD)
description: The epitope feature data within the Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center (BV-BRC), which consolidated the legacy Virus Pathogen Resource (ViPR), Influenza Research Database (IRD) and PATRIC. Epitope records (originally sourced from IEDB and mapped onto BV-BRC pathogen proteins/genomes) link experimentally characterized T- and B-cell epitopes to viral strains, surface glycoproteins and genome coordinates — useful for infectious-disease and vaccine epitope selection (influenza, flaviviruses, coronaviruses, etc.).
scale: Epitope features across thousands of viral/bacterial pathogen genomes; IEDB-sourced, strain-mapped
license: custom (all public data freely available without restriction; code MIT)

provenance.maintainer: BV-BRC (NIAID-funded; University of Chicago / Argonne / J. Craig Venter Institute et al.)

relevance.why: Strain- and structure-mapped infectious-disease/vaccine epitope context not readily available from IEDB alone; useful for pathogen-mimicry analyses and vaccine-antigen selection.

agent_access: Public data "freely available without restriction"; access via website, data API, CLI and FTP. No auth for public data. Fully agent-fetchable.
caveats: The epitope records are IEDB-derived (already-catalogued IEDB is the upstream source) — BV-BRC adds pathogen/strain mapping, not new assays. Any downstream reuse of the epitope evidence should respect IEDB's own terms. Code is MIT; "data freely available" is BV-BRC's own statement (no SPDX tag) — verify for commercial redistribution.

name: cAb-Rep (Curated Antibody Repertoires)
description: A curated database of full-length, IgBLAST-annotated human antibody variable (IGH, IGK, IGL) repertoires assembled to study antibody diversity and to estimate the prevalence of a given antibody lineage across donors. Each transcript carries V/D/J gene usage, isotype and somatic-hypermutation annotation. Useful for asking how "public"/recurrent a designed or isolated antibody is.
scale: 306 Ig repertoires from 121 human donors; ~267.9M heavy-chain and ~72.9M light-chain transcripts

provenance.maintainer: Shapiro lab, Columbia University (C2B2)

relevance.why: Donor-resolved human repertoires let you score the natural prevalence and germline plausibility of candidate antibody sequences, a useful prior for the design program and for interpreting recognition breadth.

agent_access: Web resource; repertoires provided as FASTA. No documented API; expect to download per-donor/per-repertoire FASTA files. No auth.
caveats: No explicit license found on the site/paper — treat redistribution as unconfirmed (license: unknown) and attribute Guo et al. 2019. Human only; static (2019) and not updated. Unpaired chains only.

name: CAID (Critical Assessment of Intrinsic Disorder)
description: CASP-style blind benchmark for intrinsic disorder and disordered-binding-region prediction, built on community-curated DisProt annotations (plus DisProt-PDB / DisProt-Binding reference sets). Defines where a sequence does NOT adopt a single stable 3D structure — an important complement/caveat to folding models.
scale: CAID1: 646 proteins, 43 methods; CAID2: expanded DisProt-based sets (e.g. 210-protein NOX subset)

provenance.maintainer: Tosatto group / DisProt consortium; OpenEBench

relevance.why: Disorder labels mark regions where sequence->single-structure assumptions break down (low-pLDDT regions in AFDB often coincide); useful for masking/ confidence modelling and for antigen-flexibility reasoning.

agent_access: Reference datasets and predictions downloadable from the CAID portal / OpenEBench; DisProt has a REST API and flat-file downloads. No auth.
caveats: Tangential to 3D coordinate learning (disorder, not folds) — included as a boundary/negative-signal resource. Datasets are small (benchmark scale). Cite DisProt/CAID.

name: CAMEO (Continuous Automated Model EvaluatiOn)
description: Weekly, fully automated blind benchmark that evaluates structure (and other) prediction servers on soon-to-be-released PDB targets. Provides continuous, ongoing held-out assessment data complementing the biennial CASP.
scale: Weekly targets since 2012 (rolling archive of predictions + scores)

provenance.maintainer: Schwede group, SIB / Biozentrum Basel

relevance.why: Continuous, low-leakage evaluation stream for monitoring folding-model performance on fresh structures — useful for tracking model drift between CASP rounds.

agent_access: Per-window "Raw Data" downloads over HTTPS; no auth. Some older category pages frozen. Agent can fetch snapshots.
caveats: RED FLAG: CC BY-SA 4.0 share-alike — derivatives inherit the license. Primarily an evaluation resource, not a bulk training corpus; download layout can change.

name: CanFam3.1 Reference Assembly (Boxer "Tasha")
description: The long-standing Boxer-derived dog reference genome (Sep 2011, Broad). Still the most widely used coordinate system for legacy canine GEO/SRA studies and most published tumor variant calls.
scale: ~2.4 Gb; 39 chromosomes (38 autosomes + X)
license: public (INSDC / Ensembl — no restriction on use)

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute; Ensembl/UCSC/NCBI

relevance.why: Default coordinate space for historical canine cancer datasets; needed for liftover and to interpret legacy mutation calls.

agent_access: Bulk FASTA/GTF from Ensembl/UCSC/NCBI FTP; no auth. UCSC canFam3.
caveats: Fragmented vs newer long-read assemblies; coordinate mismatch with CanFam4/ROS/Tasha1.0 — liftover required. Aging annotation.

name: CATH / CATH-Gene3D
description: Hierarchical structural classification of protein domains (Class, Architecture, Topology/fold, Homologous superfamily) derived from PDB, extended to sequence space via Gene3D (HMM-based assignment to UniProt). Provides domain boundaries, fold labels and representative/non-redundant sets used to build leakage-free ML train/test splits.
scale: v4.3.0: 500,238 classified structural domains, 5,481 superfamilies; ~151M predicted sequence domains (Gene3D)
license: custom (Gene3D copyright; research use, no resale, attribution)

provenance.maintainer: Orengo group, UCL (Global Biodata Core Resource)

relevance.why: Standard source of fold/superfamily labels and non-redundant domain sets for structure-aware pretraining and for defining clustered data splits that prevent homology leakage between train and test.

agent_access: Open FTP/HTTPS bulk download and FunFam/sequence search APIs; no auth. Agent-mirrorable.
caveats: RED FLAG: data files are Gene3D copyright with a research-use policy that forbids resale and requires acknowledgement — NOT a CC licence. Confirm terms before redistribution or commercial product use. Classification lags PDB.

name: Cell Ontology (CL)
description: Structured, species-neutral ontology of cell types (including immune cell types) used as the controlled vocabulary for annotating single-cell datasets (e.g. CELLxGENE, Tabula Sapiens). The backbone for harmonizing cell-type labels across sources.
scale: thousands of cell-type classes

provenance.maintainer: OBO Foundry / obophenotype (GitHub)

relevance.why: Required controlled vocabulary to merge cell-type annotations across atlases and to query cells by type programmatically (e.g. in the Census).

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: download OWL/OBO/JSON from persistent PURLs (versioned for reproducibility); query via EBI OLS API; GitHub source. Fully automatable, no auth.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 (attribution). One name annotation imported from OBO Foundry is CC0 — negligible. Do not confuse CL with CLO (Cell Line Ontology), which has its own (disputed) license.

name: ColabFoldDB
description: A merged environmental + reference protein database built for fast MMseqs2-based MSA generation in ColabFold. Combines BFD/MGnify clusters with additional metagenomic protein catalogs (eukaryotic, phage, updated MetaClust), clustered at 30% identity / 90% coverage. Final database: 209,335,865 representative sequences and 738,695,580 members.
scale: 209,335,865 representatives; 738,695,580 members (~182M env clusters merged with BFD)
license: CC BY 4.0 (follows BFD/MGnify; verify component terms)

provenance.maintainer: Mirdita / Steinegger / Söding (ColabFold / MMseqs2)

relevance.why: Ready-made large environmental corpus for MSA generation and as an alternative/augmenting pretraining corpus beyond UniRef; the practical database behind ColabFold MSAs.

agent_access: HTTP(S) bulk download of MMseqs2-formatted database via setup_databases.sh. Searching it requires a machine with ~768 GB RAM; bulk download only for infra-heavy users.
caveats: Aggregates multiple sources with differing provenance (MGnify, Metaclust-derived, phage/euk catalogs) — redistribution terms should be checked per component; Metaclust lineage carries NC-SA. Very large; impractical without large-RAM infrastructure.

name: CookHLA 1000 Genomes HLA imputation reference panels (five super-populations)
description: HLA imputation reference panels distributed with CookHLA, built from 1000 Genomes Project SNP and HLA data for five super-populations (AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, SAS). Each panel pairs ~225,194 MHC-region SNPs (chr6:28-35 Mb) with four-digit classical HLA types for HLA-A, -B, -C, -DQB1 and -DRB1, enabling reference-based imputation; CookHLA adds adaptive genetic-map and overlapping-window refinement.
scale: ~225,194 MHC SNPs + 4-digit HLA (A/B/C/DQB1/DRB1); 5 super-populations from 1000 Genomes

provenance.maintainer: Choi, Han et al. (Seoul National University)

relevance.why: Openly bundled multi-super-population HLA reference built on the public 1000 Genomes data — a download-and-run alternative to restricted panels for imputing HLA across ancestries.

agent_access: git clone of the repo brings down the panels; software DOI on Zenodo. No DUA for the 1000G-derived panels themselves. Agent-fetchable.
caveats: RED FLAG: the paper states the software is for noncommercial academic research use — confirm whether the panel files inherit that restriction before commercial deployment. Panels cover only 5 classical loci (no DPB1/DRB3-5). Built on 1000 Genomes sample sizes (modest per-population counts for rare alleles).

name: CORUM (Comprehensive Resource of Mammalian protein complexes)
description: Manually curated database of experimentally characterized mammalian protein complexes, with subunit composition, function, and literature evidence. The reference resource for known stable protein-complex membership (including immune-relevant complexes such as the immunoproteasome and MHC-associated assemblies).
license: custom — CC BY-NC 4.0 per site; CC BY 4.0 per 2022/2024 papers (CONFLICT)

provenance.maintainer: Helmholtz Munich (Ruepp / Institute for Bioinformatics and Systems Biology)

relevance.why: Ground-truth protein-complex membership for features and interpretation — e.g. grouping proteasome/immunoproteasome and antigen-processing machinery subunits as functional units rather than isolated proteins.

agent_access: Open bulk download (complete complex table as TXT/CSV/JSON), no auth. Small, fully script-ingestible. No formal REST API.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG / CONFLICT. The Helmholtz CORUM site states CC BY-NC 4.0 (NON- COMMERCIAL) for copyrightable parts, while the 2022 and 2024 NAR papers describe downloads as CC BY 4.0, and one older note mentions CC0. Treat the most restrictive (CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial) as governing until confirmed with the maintainer before any commercial/product use. Mammalian-focused; mostly human/mouse evidence.

name: COSMIC (Catalogue Of Somatic Mutations In Cancer)
description: The largest expert-curated catalogue of somatic mutations in human cancer, aggregating point mutations, CNVs, fusions, drug-resistance variants and the Cancer Gene Census from literature and large screens. Core reference for annotating which tumor variants are recurrent/driver and for mutational-signature analysis.
scale: tens of millions of coding mutations; v104+ (May 2026)
license: Custom — free for academic/non-profit (registration); commercial via QIAGEN; redistribution prohibited

provenance.maintainer: Wellcome Sanger Institute (Genome Research Limited)

relevance.why: Recurrence and driver annotation for candidate neoantigens — distinguishing recurrent hotspot mutations (shared-antigen opportunities) from private passengers, and sourcing curated fusion/resistance variants.

agent_access: Bulk downloads require a registered COSMIC account; files are fetched via authenticated HTTPS (email+password → download token/URL). Scriptable with stored credentials but NOT anonymous. Commercial automated use needs a QIAGEN license.
caveats: REDISTRIBUTION FORBIDDEN — COSMIC data may not be re-packaged or passed to third parties without a commercial licence; flag for any product that would ship derived COSMIC content. Academic licence is royalty-free but still a contract. Commercial pipelines need paid QIAGEN licensing.

name: CoV-AbDab — Coronavirus Antibody Database
description: A curated database of antibodies and nanobodies known to bind coronaviruses (SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV-1, MERS and others), each with heavy/light sequences where available, binding/neutralisation evidence, epitope/antigen target, origin and links to source publications and any PDB structures. A compact, antigen-labelled benchmark set for binder recognition.
scale: ~12,900 unique antibody/nanobody entries (Feb 2024 release); 1,402 at 2020 launch

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

relevance.why: Sequence-paired, antigen- and epitope-labelled antibodies with binding and neutralisation outcomes — a clean supervised set for antibody-antigen recognition models and for validating binder-design pipelines against a well-characterised antigen family.

agent_access: Full database downloadable as CSV without registration; no auth. Community submissions accepted by email. Trivially scriptable.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 (attribute Raybould et al. 2021 and original studies). Scope limited to coronaviruses; update cadence is intermittent (last site update Feb 2024). Binding/neutralisation evidence is aggregated from heterogeneous assays — read per-entry provenance before treating labels as uniform.

name: CTdatabase — cancer-testis antigen knowledge base
description: Curated knowledge base of cancer-testis antigens (CTAs): gene aliases, RefSeq accessions, genomic locations, splice variants and family members, plus manually curated mRNA/protein expression and antigen-specific immune-response data in cancer patients. The reference catalogue for the classic shared tumor-antigen class (MAGE, NY-ESO-1, SSX, etc.).
scale: Hundreds of curated CTA genes/families with expression + immunogenicity annotation

provenance.maintainer: Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research / LNCC (Brazil)

relevance.why: The canonical CTA reference for shared tumor antigens — a baseline antigen list to cross- check non-canonical/TE/ERV candidates against established cancer-germline antigens.

agent_access: Web interface (cta.lncc.br); no documented bulk-download API — may require scraping. Verify the site resolves before relying on it.
caveats: NO explicit license stated (flag before redistribution/ML training). Site is legacy (core content ~2009) and availability can be intermittent. Human only.

name: Darwin's Ark — Companion-Animal Citizen-Science Genomics
description: Open citizen-science cohort (co-founded by E. Karlsson) linking owner-reported phenotype questionnaires to low-pass WGS in tens of thousands of dogs. Phenotype + genotype data released openly (e.g., Dryad) alongside behavior-genetics publications.
scale: ~48,500+ dogs registered; sequenced subset in the thousands

provenance.maintainer: Darwin's Ark Foundation / UMass Chan (Karlsson)

relevance.why: Large open germline + phenotype resource; breed-structure and germline background useful for population-aware variant interpretation. Minimal direct oncology/immune content.

agent_access: Dryad bulk downloads (CC0); surveys as CSV. No auth.
caveats: Behavior/morphology focus, not cancer; low-pass depth limits somatic/immune uses.

name: Dog10K / CanFam canine reference genome & variation
description: Canine reference genome assemblies and a large multi-omics variation resource for dogs and wild canids. Centers on the UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0 (canFam4, German Shepherd) assembly with GFF annotation, plus the Dog10K consortium SNV/structural-variant panel from ~2000 canids. The primary dog reference for the comparative-oncology program.
scale: SNPs from ~2,075 individuals; VCF from 1,987 samples (phase-1 from 1,929)
license: unknown (freely available online; no explicit license posted)

provenance.maintainer: Dog10K Consortium (incl. Kunming Inst. Zoology CAS; Kidd lab, U Michigan; iDog/NGDC)

relevance.why: The canine reference genome + variation baseline needed to translate human target/antigen concepts into dog (naturally occurring canine cancers as comparative-oncology models) and to distinguish germline canine variation from tumor-specific changes.

agent_access: Genome FASTA (GCF_011100685.1_UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0), GFF, aliases, and SNV VCFs download from the Dog10K site; variant files/annotations mirrored on the Kidd lab share (kiddlabshare.med.umich.edu/dog10K/) and Zenodo (record 8084059). UCSC canFam4 and NCBI Datasets also serve the assembly. No auth.
caveats: Dog10K portal does not state an explicit license — treat as unknown and rely on the NCBI/UCSC assembly (unrestricted) + cite the papers; verify terms for the variant panel before redistribution. Multiple canine assemblies in circulation (canFam3.1/4/5/6, ROS_Cfam_1.0) — fix one and be consistent. Canine gene annotation is less mature than human.

name: Dog10K_Boxer_Tasha_1.0 (Long-read Boxer assembly)
description: Long-read (PacBio) reassembly of the original Boxer "Tasha", scaffolded against CanFam3.1. NCBI GCF_000002285.5; UCSC canFam6. Higher contiguity on the historical Boxer background.
scale: chromosome-level; ~2.4 Gb

provenance.maintainer: Dog10K Consortium; NCBI

relevance.why: Bridges legacy Boxer-based (CanFam3.1) resources with long-read quality; useful for DLA-region assembly comparisons.

agent_access: NCBI Datasets / FTP; no auth. UCSC canFam6.
caveats: A third coordinate system — adds to the dog-reference fragmentation problem. Note: ROS_Cfam_1.0 (GCF_014441545.1, canFam5) is the current NCBI RefSeq reference for Canis lupus familiaris.

name: DoGA — Dog Genome Annotation (Integrative Epigenome Map)
description: Integrative dog epigenome reference annotation (RNA-seq + regulatory marks) across many tissues for comparative inter-tissue and cross-species studies; complements BarkBase.
scale: multi-tissue epigenome (dozens of tissues/samples)
license: CC BY 4.0 (article); data via SRA/GEO public norms

provenance.maintainer: DoGA consortium (incl. University of Helsinki / Lohi, Broad)

relevance.why: Stronger regulatory/expression annotation than BarkBase; supports gene-model and self-expression references for the dog.

agent_access: Processed tracks + raw reads via GEO/SRA/EGA (check paper data-availability for exact accession and any controlled-access splits); no auth for public parts.
caveats: Not tied to Darwin's Ark/Karlsson despite overlap of people; confirm exact accessions. ENCODE-level canine functional data still does not exist.

name: ECOD (Evolutionary Classification of protein Domains)
description: Classification of PDB domains emphasising distant evolutionary (homologous) relationships, with an automatically updated hierarchy (X/H/T/F groups). Recent releases extend classification to AlphaFold DB models (AFDB-ECOD), giving domain labels over predicted structures too.
scale: >500,000 PDB domains (~3,400 homologous groups); plus AFDB-derived domains

provenance.maintainer: Grishin lab, UT Southwestern

relevance.why: Evolution-aware domain boundaries and remote-homology groupings help define challenging, leakage-controlled splits and augment fold-label coverage, including over predicted (AFDB) structures.

agent_access: Flat-file distributions downloadable over HTTP; no auth. Agent-mirrorable. No documented bulk API.
caveats: RED FLAG: no explicit license found on the site — treat as unknown and confirm reuse terms before redistribution. Served over plain HTTP; verify integrity.

name: eggNOG (evolutionary genealogy of genes: Non-supervised Orthologous Groups)
description: A hierarchical catalog of orthologous groups with functional and phylogenetic annotation, built on reference proteomes across all domains of life. eggNOG 6.0 covers 12,535 organisms (1,322 eukaryotes, 10,756 bacteria, 457 archaea) with >17M orthologous groups at 1,601 taxonomic levels. Supplies orthology-structured sequence/annotation sets and powers eggNOG-mapper functional annotation.
scale: 12,535 organisms; >17M orthologous groups (incl. 17,011,080 NOGs) at 1,601 tax levels

provenance.maintainer: Bork Lab (EMBL) / Huerta-Cepas et al.

relevance.why: Orthology-grouped protein sequences and HMMs for building evolution-aware corpora, functional labels for representation-learning tasks, and comparative-genomics context.

agent_access: Bulk download (per-level members, FASTA, HMMs) from eggNOG website; eggNOG-mapper tool separate. No auth.
caveats: LICENSE UNVERIFIED — the 6.0 paper is CC BY 4.0 but no explicit data license is stated on the download page (eggNOG 2008 release used CC BY 3.0 for data). Do not assume terms; confirm on the download page before redistribution/ML use. Marked unknown per cataloguing rules.

name: Ensembl (genomes, gene models, comparative genomics)
description: Reference genome assemblies with automated + manually integrated gene annotation, variation, regulation, and comparative genomics for vertebrates. Provides human (GRCh38, with GENCODE as the human gene set) and multiple dog assemblies (incl. ROS_Cfam_1.0, UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0/canFam4, Boxer Tasha), with cross-species orthology.
scale: Hundreds of vertebrate genomes; human GRCh38 + GRCh37; multiple dog assemblies

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI & Wellcome Sanger Institute

relevance.why: Supplies the human and dog reference genomes + gene models underpinning transcript/protein references and variant interpretation. Cross-species orthology directly serves the comparative-oncology (canine) program (mapping human targets to the dog genome).

agent_access: REST API (rest.ensembl.org; GRCh37 mirror grch37.rest.ensembl.org), Perl API, BioMart, and FTP for FASTA/GTF/GFF3/VCF. No auth. Highly scriptable; per-release archive hosts for pinning.
caveats: Multiple dog assemblies exist — pick one deliberately (ROS_Cfam_1.0 vs UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0/canFam4) and keep human/dog coordinate systems consistent. Release-versioned; pin releases for reproducibility.

name: GENCODE (reference gene annotation)
description: The reference gene annotation for the human (and mouse) genome: comprehensive, manually curated + computationally supported models of protein-coding genes, lncRNAs, pseudogenes, and alternative splicing on GRCh38. Adopted as the human gene set in Ensembl and (via MANE) aligned with RefSeq.
scale: Human ~63,000 genes, ~20,000 protein-coding, ~250,000 transcripts (recent releases)

provenance.maintainer: GENCODE consortium (EMBL-EBI/HAVANA + collaborators), part of ENCODE

relevance.why: The authoritative transcript/ORF catalog defining the canonical human proteome coordinate space. Alternative-splice and ORF annotation is the substrate for enumerating normal protein products vs. candidate tumor-specific transcripts/ORFs.

agent_access: Direct HTTPS/FTP download of GTF/GFF3 and transcript/translation FASTA per release; small, scriptable, versioned. No auth, no API needed (static files).
caveats: No explicit standalone license document — data is free/open but cite the GENCODE paper; verify terms if redistributing. Human + mouse only (no dog — use Ensembl/RefSeq for canine annotation). Pin release number (annotation changes between releases).

name: Gene Ontology (GO) & GO Annotations (GOA)
description: The authoritative structured vocabulary of gene/gene-product function across three aspects (molecular function, biological process, cellular component), plus the GO Annotation (GOA) corpus that links specific gene products to GO terms with evidence codes. The de facto standard for functional annotation and gene-set / enrichment analysis. Dog (Canis familiaris) annotations are available through GOA and Ensembl orthology projection.
scale: ~43,000 GO terms; hundreds of millions of annotations across species (GOA)

provenance.maintainer: Gene Ontology Consortium (EMBL-EBI, others; NIH/NHGRI funded)

last_updated: 2026 (monthly releases; GO knowledgebase in 2026 paper published)

relevance.why: Core annotation layer for turning gene/protein identifiers into interpretable functional features (e.g. tagging antigen-processing, MHC, cytokine-signaling genes) and for enrichment interpretation of model outputs across human and canine programs.

agent_access: Open bulk download (OBO/OWL ontology + GAF/GPAD annotation files) over HTTPS, no auth. REST API (api.geneontology.org) and the GOlr Solr endpoint for programmatic queries. Fully automatable; pin a release date for reproducibility.
caveats: GO ontology/annotation data are CC BY 4.0; GO software is BSD-3-Clause (keep separate). Evidence codes vary in reliability (IEA electronic vs. experimental) — filter by evidence for high-confidence features. Canine annotations are sparser and partly orthology-projected; verify per gene.

name: Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB)
description: A standardized, phylogenetically consistent taxonomy and reference genome set for bacteria and archaea, with representative genomes, aligned marker genes, and full genome sequences. A clean, taxonomically balanced prokaryotic genomic corpus widely used to sample sequence diversity for training and benchmarking.
scale: R10 (RS226): ~732,475 genomes (715,230 bacterial + 17,245 archaeal); R232 ~901,341 genomes

provenance.maintainer: Australian Centre for Ecogenomics (University of Queensland)

last_updated: R232 (2026-04-15); R10/RS226 is the DOI-cited release

relevance.why: Taxonomically de-biased prokaryotic genome/protein source for sampling sequence diversity in PLM pretraining and for phylogenetically aware benchmarking.

agent_access: HTTP(S)/FTP bulk download across Europe/Asia-Pacific/worldwide mirrors plus academic torrent; no auth. Large genome archives.
caveats: CC BY-SA (ShareAlike) — derivatives inherit the license (differs from CC BY). Some third-party listings mislabel as CC BY or GPL (GPL = software). Release numbering changes counts frequently.

name: HIBAG pre-fit HLA imputation classifiers (multi-ethnic model sets)
description: Pre-trained HLA imputation models ("classifiers") for the HIBAG attribute-bagging method, distributed so users can impute classical HLA alleles from SNP-array genotypes without owning raw reference individual-level data. Pre-fit models cover European, Asian, Hispanic and African ancestries and are provided per SNP-array platform; a later multi-ethnic panel (Degenhardt et al. 2019) extends class I and II coverage. Models are distributed as R objects (no individual genotypes exposed).
scale: Pre-fit classifiers for 4 ancestries x multiple SNP platforms; HLA class I + II loci

provenance.maintainer: Xiuwen Zheng et al.; distributed via Bioconductor + author S3/GitHub-Pages mirrors

relevance.why: Privacy-preserving, openly downloadable alternative to raw reference panels for HLA imputation across ancestries; lets an automated pipeline call HLA from arrays with no DUA for the pre-fit models.

agent_access: Pre-fit model files are direct HTTPS downloads from the S3 mirror / GitHub Pages, no auth; HIBAG package installs from Bioconductor (GPL-3). Fully agent-fetchable for the open pre-fit sets.
caveats: RED FLAG (partial): the GPL-3 covers the software, not necessarily every model set. The Zheng 2014 pre-fit classifiers are freely distributed, but the 2019 multi-ethnic panel (Degenhardt) is described as CC BY-NC 4.0 and/or available on request / only via outsourced imputation services — NonCommercial and request terms conflict across sources, so verify per-model license before commercial use. Imputation accuracy drops for rare alleles and under-represented ancestries.

name: HIV Molecular Immunology Database (Los Alamos; CTL/Th epitope maps)
description: A curated, annotated database of HIV-1 cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL/CD8), T-helper (CD4) and antibody epitopes maintained by Los Alamos National Laboratory (Group T-10), with HLA restriction, sequence, protein location, escape-mutation and literature annotations. Includes the "best-characterized CTL/Th epitope" summary sets. Sister LANL resources exist for HCV and (historically) Ebola immunology.
scale: Thousands of annotated HIV-1 CTL/Th/antibody epitopes with HLA restriction + escape annotation
license: custom (US Govt; public release, distribution unlimited)

provenance.maintainer: Los Alamos National Laboratory, Theoretical Biology & Biophysics (Group T-10; Korber, Yusim et al.)

relevance.why: Deeply annotated infectious-disease T-cell epitope set with HLA restriction and immune-escape data — a gold-standard non-cancer epitope corpus for benchmarking immunogenicity/recognition models and for cross-pathogen transfer.

agent_access: Web search interface with CSV/JSON export per query; downloadable summary tables. No auth. Agent- fetchable via the export endpoints (not a single bulk dump — iterate queries).
caveats: No explicit reuse LICENSE beyond the US-government "approved for public release; distribution unlimited" statement on compendium PDFs — that is a distribution statement, not a CC license; confirm reuse terms for the live database. Some epitope records ultimately overlap with IEDB (already catalogued). The DOI given is for a LANL compendium report; the live DB has no single journal DOI.

name: Immunogenicity Database Collaborative (IDC) — therapeutic-protein ADA / deimmunization dataset
description: A curated, publicly accessible clinical-immunogenicity dataset linking anti-drug-antibody (ADA) outcomes for therapeutic proteins/antibodies with predicted CD4+ T-cell epitope content and molecule features — assembled to study and benchmark immunogenicity (deimmunization) prediction. Reports weak but positive correlation between predicted epitope counts and observed ADA rates. Part of a growing set of public ADA/deimmunization resources (alongside curated therapeutic-antibody ADA collections).
scale: Curated clinical ADA outcomes across therapeutic proteins linked to CD4 epitope predictions

provenance.maintainer: Immunogenicity Database Collaborative (IDC) consortium

relevance.why: Clinical ADA-linked immunogenicity labels for *therapeutic proteins* are exactly the deimmunization signal missing from epitope databases; directly relevant to designing low-immunogenicity biologics and validating class II / deimmunization predictors.

agent_access: Dataset distributed via preprint supplements (bioRxiv) — downloadable, no auth. Agent-fetchable once the supplement URLs are confirmed.
caveats: PREPRINT (2025) — not yet peer-reviewed; the DOI prefix (10.64898) is unusual for bioRxiv (normally 10.1101), so VERIFY the DOI/landing URL before citing. No dataset license established yet — mark unknown. Clinical immunogenicity is confounded (dose, route, assay, indication); correlations are weak. Some comparable clinical datasets (e.g. Roche/Genentech arms) remain proprietary/non-public.

name: IMGT Dog (Canis lupus familiaris) IG/TR Germline Reference
description: IMGT's curated germline annotation of the canine immunoglobulin (IGH, IGK, IGL) and T-cell-receptor (TRA/TRB/TRG/TRD) loci — gene tables, allele sequences, locus maps and gene order — the canine analogue of the human IMGT germline sets used for V(D)J assignment. Underlying comprehensive annotation from Martin et al. (Immunogenetics 2017).
scale: canine IG + TR germline V/D/J/C gene tables and alleles

provenance.maintainer: IMGT, the international ImMunoGeneTics information system (Montpellier/CNRS)

relevance.why: The germline backbone for canine TCR/BCR repertoire analysis (V(D)J assignment, CDR3 calling) — essential canine-specific infrastructure where human IMGT cannot substitute. Enables canine recognition-arm work analogous to human IMGT pipelines.

agent_access: IMGT/GENE-DB and IMGT/V-QUEST provide canine reference sets; web and FASTA export. No bulk API; scraping is restricted by terms of use — prefer the provided export tools.
caveats: IMGT terms of use are restrictive (academic use, mandatory citation, redistribution limited) — verify license_url before redistributing or using for ML training. Canine TRA/TRD and light-chain annotation historically lagged; coverage still improving.

name: IMGT Canine IGK Locus Annotation (NAR Genom Bioinform 2026)
description: Dedicated IMGT annotation of the canine immunoglobulin kappa (IGK) light-chain locus on chromosome 17 (~317-349 kb; 31 genes: 25 V, 5 J, 1 C), built from Boxer (CanFam3.1) and Basenji assemblies with cross-breed insights. Fills a long-standing light-chain gap in canine immunogenetics.
scale: canine IGK locus — 31 genes (25V/5J/1C)

provenance.maintainer: IMGT (Montpellier/CNRS)

relevance.why: Completes the canine light-chain germline reference needed for full BCR (IGK) V(D)J analysis in the recognition program.

caveats: IMGT terms of use apply (see license_url). Breed-specific allele variation noted — confirm which reference breed matches the study samples.

name: IMGT/GENE-DB (IG & TR reference genes)
description: The international reference for immunoglobulin (IG) and T-cell receptor (TR) gene and allele nomenclature and germline reference sequences; supplies the reference directories used by IMGT/V-QUEST and most AIRR annotation tools.
scale: ~8,500 IG/TR genes across species (human + mouse core)
license: conflicting: site states CC BY 4.0; NAR 2025 states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

provenance.maintainer: IMGT / CNRS, Montpellier

relevance.why: Canonical germline reference for TCR/IG gene naming and sequences — required to standardize V/D/J gene calls across all recognition datasets.

agent_access: Germline FASTA reference sets downloadable from the site; query interface for genes. No open REST API — fetch reference directories as files. IMGT/V-QUEST has a web API but with usage terms (contact IMGT).
caveats: LICENSE CONFLICT: imgt.org states CC BY 4.0 while the NAR 2025 overview states academic CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 with commercial use requiring a CNRS financial arrangement — resolve with IMGT (contact-imgt@igh.cnrs.fr) before any commercial use. Scraping discouraged; prefer the provided reference files.

name: ImmPort (Immunology Database and Analysis Portal)
description: NIAID/DAIT-funded repository of curated immunology research data from clinical and mechanistic studies (flow/CyTOF, ELISA, gene expression, HAI, clinical metadata), plus reference gene lists (e.g. ImmPort immune gene categories) and analysis tools. The 'Shared Data' tier is open to any registered researcher.
scale: Hundreds of curated studies; standardized immunology assay + clinical data
license: custom (NIAID-DAIT Data Sharing Use Agreement; cite study accessions)

provenance.maintainer: ImmPort (NIAID/DAIT; UCSF, University at Buffalo, Northrop Grumman)

relevance.why: Standardized human immunology assay data and the ImmPort immune gene category lists provide immune-feature annotations and real immune-cell/clinical datasets for grounding and benchmarking immune models.

agent_access: Shared Data downloadable via web and Aspera/API after a one-step free registration (DSUA acceptance). Private Data tier is provider-controlled (not open). Automatable after obtaining credentials; cite study accession + title per use.
caveats: Not pure open-access: requires registration and acceptance of the NIAID-DAIT Data Sharing Use Agreement; redistribution of raw study data is constrained by the DSUA and per-study citation requirements. Human-focused (plus some mouse); no dog.

name: ImmuneSigDB (MSigDB C7 immunologic signatures)
description: The immunologic-signature collection within MSigDB (collection C7): thousands of gene sets derived from manually curated comparisons of immune-cell states, perturbations and conditions (activation, differentiation, infection, vaccination). Purpose-built for scoring and interpreting immune transcriptional programs.
scale: ~5,200 immunologic gene sets (ImmuneSigDB subset of C7)

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute (Godec, Haining et al.) within MSigDB

relevance.why: The most immune-specific curated gene-set resource for Veritope — directly provides features for immune-cell-state and immune-program scoring in antigen/immune modeling, and interpretable labels for recognition-program signatures.

agent_access: Delivered as the C7 collection within the MSigDB GMT/XML bulk downloads (email registration requested). Script-ingestible.
caveats: Subset of MSigDB; dedup against the parent 'msigdb' entry (do not double-count). Under the CC BY 4.0 portion of MSigDB terms, but confirm when bundling with other MSigDB collections that may carry third-party restrictions. Human/mouse only (no dog).

name: INDI — Integrated Nanobody Database for Immunoinformatics
description: An integrated database of camelid single-domain antibody (VHH / nanobody) sequences and metadata aggregated from all major public outlets: patents, GenBank, next-generation sequencing repositories, deposited structures and the scientific literature. Entries are filtered to contain all three CDRs and only canonical amino acids, with provenance and annotation.
scale: >11 million nanobody sequences (2021 preprint figure)

provenance.maintainer: NaturalAntibody (Poland), with Harvard Medical School, Abterra Biosciences, Alector

relevance.why: Nanobodies are a primary scaffold for the binder-design program (small, stable, single-domain). INDI is the largest aggregation of natural VHH sequence space for pretraining and for sampling realistic CDR-H3 loops.

agent_access: Web portal with sequence / CDR-H3 / text search. Bulk-download availability and any API are not clearly documented — confirm on the portal before assuming programmatic bulk access; may require contacting maintainers.
caveats: No explicit reuse license found (license: unknown) — confirm terms with NaturalAntibody before redistribution or ML training. Aggregated from mixed sources (patents, NGS) with heterogeneous quality; dedup needed. Camelid single-domain only.

name: IntAct Molecular Interaction Database
description: EMBL-EBI's open database of molecular interaction data (primarily protein-protein), curated to deep detail from the literature and direct depositions, and the common curation platform for the IMEx consortium (MIntAct). Interactions carry PSI-MI controlled-vocabulary evidence and confidence scoring.
scale: >1.1M binary interactions, >20k publications curated

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (Orchard/Hermjakob) / IMEx Consortium

relevance.why: Deeply curated, PSI-MI-detailed protein interaction evidence (binding regions, methods, confidence) for high-quality interaction features and for grounding antigen/immune protein complexes and binding partners.

agent_access: Open bulk downloads (MITAB, PSI-MI XML) and PSICQUIC/REST web services, no auth. CC BY 4.0 — redistributable with attribution. Automatable.
caveats: Data are CC BY 4.0 and software Apache-2.0 (do not conflate; CC0 appears only on third-party registry metadata, not on IntAct data). Human-heavy; dog interactions limited. Deduplicate against BioGRID/STRING (shared IMEx curation overlaps).

name: InterPro
description: Integrative classification of proteins into families, domains and sites by combining 13+ member databases (Pfam, CATH-Gene3D, PANTHER, PROSITE, SMART, SUPERFAMILY, NCBIfam, CDD, etc.). Provides domain architectures and residue annotations across 200M+ UniProt sequences, with structural member databases (CATH-Gene3D, SUPERFAMILY) linking families to folds.
scale: Release 10x.0: 45,899 InterPro entries from 84,588 member signatures; >200M sequences
license: CC0 1.0 for InterPro-produced data; InterProScan Apache-2.0; member DBs vary

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI InterPro consortium

relevance.why: Domain-architecture and structural-family labels across all of UniProt provide weak supervision and conditioning signals for sequence->structure models, and a route to propagate structural family labels onto unlabelled sequences.

agent_access: Open FTP bulk download and a comprehensive REST API; no auth. Agent-mirrorable. New releases every ~8 weeks.
caveats: Member databases carry their own licenses (e.g. CATH-Gene3D research-use/no- resale; PANTHER, SMART have terms). InterPro's own aggregation is CC0 but check a member DB's terms before redistributing that portion.

name: IPD-IMGT/HLA Database
description: The authoritative reference of human HLA allele sequences and official HLA nomenclature. Provides genomic/cDNA/protein sequences, alignments, and a flat-file database. The canonical source for HLA allele definitions used by every typing and prediction pipeline.
scale: ~43,758 HLA alleles (release 3.63, Jan 2026); 47 genes; 44,876 total sequences

provenance.maintainer: Anthony Nolan Research Institute + EMBL-EBI (IPD), UK

relevance.why: Required reference to standardize HLA alleles when joining pMHC/presentation data with TCR-recognition datasets. Cross-ref the presentation agent for MHC/HLA depth — do not duplicate deeply.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: EBI FTP/HTTP file download (latest release) and GitHub (ANHIG/IMGTHLA) with a branch per release + compressed archives — ideal for version-pinned ingestion. No auth.
caveats: CC BY-ND - RED FLAG: NoDerivs means you may redistribute verbatim with attribution (commercial OK) but distributing a MODIFIED version requires prior written permission. Deriving and re-publishing altered sequence sets, or shipping a reformatted subset, needs permission. Internal use/derived features generally fine; redistribution of derivatives is the constraint. Human only.

name: IPD-KIR Database (Killer-cell Immunoglobulin-like Receptors)
description: The official reference database of allelic sequences for the human Killer-cell Immunoglobulin-like Receptor (KIR) genes, part of the IPD (Immuno Polymorphism Database) at EMBL-EBI and the sister resource to IPD-IMGT/HLA. Provides curated KIR allele nomenclature, genomic and cDNA reference sequences, alignments and gene-content/haplotype context for the NK-cell receptor locus that pairs with HLA class I ligands.
scale: All named KIR alleles across ~15 KIR genes/pseudogenes; release 2.15 (2025-12)

provenance.maintainer: Anthony Nolan Research Institute + EMBL-EBI (Robinson, Barker, Marsh et al.)

relevance.why: Canonical KIR allele reference needed to model NK-cell recognition of HLA class I and KIR-ligand (e.g. HLA-C C1/C2, Bw4) interactions — the receptor side of the innate arm complementing TCR work.

agent_access: EBI web + FTP; reference sequences/alignments versioned on the ANHIG/IPDKIR GitHub (git-cloneable). No auth. Agent-fetchable.
caveats: RED FLAG (partial): IPD databases carry Creative Commons terms that may include NoDerivatives (ND) — confirm the exact current licence on the IPD-KIR licence page before redistributing modified data. KIR gene-content/copy-number is not a simple allele table (structural complexity). For KIR allele/ genotype *frequencies* across populations, cross-reference the Allele Frequency Net Database (AFND, catalogued in domain-1) rather than this sequence reference.

name: IPD-MHC Database (non-human, incl. canine DLA)
description: The inter-species sister database to IPD-IMGT/HLA: curated MHC allele sequences and nomenclature for non-human species, including canine DLA. The authoritative source for DLA allele definitions (DLA-88, DLA-DRB1, etc.).
scale: >7,000 alleles across ~70 species; canine (DLA) subset is comparatively small

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (IPD) + species nomenclature committees

relevance.why: The canine DLA reference needed for any dog immuno-oncology work: pseudo-sequences and allele definitions for DLA-restricted presentation modeling. Core to Veritope's comparative-oncology angle.

agent_access: Downloadable per-species flat files + GitHub. No auth; bulk-fetchable.
caveats: CC BY-ND (same NoDerivs constraint as IPD-IMGT/HLA). Canine coverage is SPARSE relative to human - few alleles, and sequence-only (no binding/elution data here). This is the central canine gap for Veritope.

name: JGI IMG/M (Integrated Microbial Genomes & Microbiomes)
description: DOE JGI's data-management and comparative-analysis system for microbial genomes and metagenomes, with gene/protein predictions and functional annotation over a very large public holding of isolate genomes and metagenomes. A major genomic/metagenomic sequence source for building microbial protein corpora.
scale: Very large (tens of thousands of metagenomes + isolate genomes); counts grow continuously
license: JGI Data Utilization/Release Policy (NCBI-imported genomes public domain)

provenance.maintainer: DOE Joint Genome Institute (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)

relevance.why: Large microbial genome/metagenome corpus and gene-prediction source for expanding protein sequence space and comparative microbial analyses.

agent_access: Public data downloadable via JGI Data Portal; many bulk downloads require a (free) JGI/ORCID account login. Private submissions embargoed (18 mo genomes / 24 mo metagenomes). Not a no-auth bulk FTP like UniProt.
caveats: Access is registration-gated for bulk download and ~16% of isolate genomes / ~30% of metagenomes are private. Terms follow the JGI Data Policy rather than a single CC license — review before redistribution/ML use. Large, heterogeneous holdings need careful dedup.

name: KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes)
description: Reference knowledgebase of molecular pathways (KEGG PATHWAY), functional orthology (KEGG ORTHOLOGY/KO), modules, diseases and drugs. Widely used as a pathway-membership and ortholog-grouping annotation source. Includes immune-system and signaling maps.
scale: ~570 reference pathway maps; ~26,000 KO groups; thousands of organisms

provenance.maintainer: Kanehisa Laboratories; licensing via Pathway Solutions Inc.

relevance.why: KEGG pathway and KO annotations are a standard feature source for pathway membership and cross-species ortholog grouping — but licensing severely constrains programmatic and commercial use (see caveats).

agent_access: Free KEGG REST API (rest.kegg.jp) for academic use with rate limits; free website. BULK download (FTP) requires a PAID academic FTP subscription; the API is not intended for mass harvesting. Agent-scale ingestion effectively needs a subscription.
caveats: MAJOR LICENSE RED FLAG. KEGG is NOT a free/open database. Academic WEB and limited REST use is free, but bulk FTP download requires a paid academic subscription and ANY commercial use (including for-profit research or embedding in a product/service) requires a commercial End-User or Service-Provider license from Pathway Solutions. Redistribution and large-scale extraction are prohibited under the FTP terms. Do NOT treat KEGG data as redistributable or ML-trainable without an appropriate license. Prefer Reactome/WikiPathways (CC0) or KEGG-MEDICUS-derived MSigDB sets where possible.

name: KIR*IMP — KIR gene-content imputation reference panel
description: A reference-based method and panel for imputing KIR gene content (presence/absence copy number of KIR genes) from SNP genotype data in the surrounding region. The UK reference panel was typed on the Illumina Immunochip and underpins KIR*IMP's models, letting large SNP-genotyped cohorts recover KIR haplotype/gene-content calls without direct KIR typing — the KIR analogue of SNP2HLA for HLA.
scale: UK Immunochip-typed reference panel; imputes presence/absence of ~16 KIR genes

provenance.maintainer: Vukcevic et al.; hosted at Murdoch Children's Research Institute / University of Melbourne

relevance.why: Enables KIR gene-content recovery in SNP-genotyped cohorts, bringing the NK/KIR axis into the same population-scale analyses already possible for HLA via imputation.

agent_access: KIR*IMP runs as a remote server job (upload SNPs); the underlying UK reference panel is not posted as a bulk open download. Not fully agent-fetchable; plan for server submission.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 covers the publication; the reference panel's own download/reuse terms are NOT separately stated — treat as request-only and confirm with authors. Imputes gene *content* (presence/absence), not full KIR allele resolution. European (UK Immunochip) reference — ancestry bias. A separate Japanese KIR panel is deposited at Japan's NBDC (different access terms).

name: Metaclust (clustered metagenomic/metatranscriptomic proteins)
description: A clustered catalog of protein-coding fragments predicted from metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets, produced with Linclust/MMseqs2. Built from ~1.59 billion predicted protein fragments across ~2,200 metagenome/metatranscriptome datasets, reduced to ~424 million clusters. A key metagenomic input to BFD and ColabFoldDB.
scale: ~1.59B input fragments from ~2,200 datasets; ~424M clusters

provenance.maintainer: Steinegger & Söding (Söding Lab / MMseqs2)

relevance.why: Large metagenomic protein corpus expanding sequence space for PLM pretraining and MSA generation; a documented input to BFD/ColabFoldDB.

agent_access: HTTP(S) bulk download; no auth. Frozen release.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: NonCommercial clause restricts commercial use (including some commercial ML training) and ShareAlike propagates to derivatives. This is why it must be flagged when it appears as an input to BFD/ColabFoldDB. Frozen 2018 build.

name: MGnify Genome Catalogues (prokaryotic MAGs/isolates)
description: Biome-specific catalogues of non-redundant, species-level clustered prokaryotic genomes (metagenome-assembled genomes and isolates) from MGnify, with pan-genome and functional annotation. A genomic (not just protein) sequence corpus spanning human gut, marine, soil and other environments — a source of genome-context and coding-sequence data for comparative and sequence-model work.
scale: Multiple biome catalogues; hundreds of thousands of genomes clustered to species-level reps
license: EMBL-EBI terms of use (verify per catalogue; underlying data generally open)

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (MGnify team)

relevance.why: Genome-level metagenomic corpus for coding-sequence extraction, genomic-context modeling and comparative analyses that complement the MGnify protein set.

agent_access: FTP bulk download per catalogue + MGnify REST API (genome-catalogues endpoint). No auth.
caveats: License is the general EMBL-EBI terms rather than the CC0 that covers the protein DB — confirm per catalogue before redistribution. Catalogue counts grow release-to-release; verify current totals.

name: MGnify Protein Database (MGnify90)
description: EMBL-EBI's non-redundant catalog of protein sequences predicted from assembled metagenomes in MGnify — the largest publicly described metagenomic protein collection. The ~2.48 billion sequences (clustered representations, e.g. MGnify90) vastly expand sequence space beyond UniProt and are the source behind the ESM Metagenomic Atlas (which folded MGnify90).
scale: ~2,477,479,951 protein sequences (current release); MGnify90 clustered set
license: CC0 1.0 (protein database; most other MGnify content is EMBL-EBI terms)

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (MGnify team)

relevance.why: The premier metagenomic protein corpus for expanding PLM pretraining into the 'dark matter' of protein space; underpins ESM-scale metagenomic structure/representation work.

agent_access: Bulk FTP download, HMMER search, and BigQuery access. Web resource in public beta. CC0 makes the protein set unusually unrestricted for ML training.
caveats: CC0 applies to the protein database specifically; broader MGnify content falls under EMBL-EBI terms — do not generalize CC0. Huge scale; heavy dedup vs UniRef recommended. Note ESM Metagenomic Atlas (structures over MGnify90) is catalogued separately in domain-9 (esm-atlas).

name: MSigDB (Molecular Signatures Database)
description: Curated collections of annotated gene sets for enrichment analysis (GSEA): hallmark (H) gene sets, curated pathways (C2: Reactome, KEGG-MEDICUS, BioCarta, WikiPathways), GO (C5), oncogenic (C6), immunologic (C7, incl. ImmuneSigDB), and cell-type (C8) collections. The standard gene-set resource for interpreting expression signatures.
scale: ~34,000 gene sets (v2024.1), human + mouse orthology collections
license: CC BY 4.0 (most sets); some subsets under separate/restrictive terms — see caveats

provenance.maintainer: Broad Institute / UC San Diego (Mesirov, Tamayo labs)

relevance.why: Hallmark and curated gene sets are the workhorse feature/annotation layer for scoring immune and oncogenic programs in expression data and for interpreting model-derived signatures across programs.

agent_access: Bulk GMT/GMX/XML/SQLite downloads over HTTPS; email registration requested on the download page. Fully script-ingestible once downloaded.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG (mixed). Core gene sets are CC BY 4.0 (v6.0-v7.5.1 and v2022.1+), but sub-collections carry third-party terms: KEGG-MEDICUS sets are CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike); legacy KEGG sets defer to KEGG's restrictive policy (commercial license needed); BioCarta and Database-of-Cell-Signaling (ST_) sets are under separate license to the Broad with disclaimer-retention requirements. Older (pre-v6) releases had non-commercial language. Audit the specific collections used before any commercial/redistribution use.

name: Four-digit Multi-ethnic HLA imputation reference panel (Michigan Imputation Server / HLA-TAPAS)
description: High-resolution, multi-ancestry HLA imputation reference panel spanning five global populations (European, African, East Asian, South Asian, Admixed/Latino), built to improve HLA imputation and multi-ethnic fine-mapping. v1 (2021) contains 18,293 samples and v2 (2022) 20,349 samples (the study describes ~21,546 individuals), on GRCh37/hg19, with four-digit classical alleles and amino-acid variants. Served through the Michigan Imputation Server; the associated HLA-TAPAS pipeline is on GitHub.
scale: v1 18,293 / v2 20,349 samples; 5 global populations; 4-digit HLA + amino-acid variants (GRCh37)

provenance.maintainer: Michigan Imputation Server (U-Michigan, Fuchsberger/Das) + Immunogenomics lab (Luo, Raychaudhuri)

relevance.why: The most widely used openly-accessible multi-ancestry HLA imputation panel; critical for calling HLA in non-European cohorts where the T1DGC/European panels underperform, reducing ancestry bias in antigen-coverage and HLA-association analyses.

agent_access: Imputation is run by uploading SNP data to the Michigan Imputation Server (account registration, one-time-password-encrypted results, deleted after 7 days) — not a bulk file download. HLA-TAPAS code is openly cloneable from GitHub; the underlying panel is described in the literature as restricted-access.
caveats: Underlying reference panel is NOT a free bulk download — it is consumed via the server or is restricted-access; confirm data-use terms before assuming redistribution rights. No explicit SPDX license located for the panel data (HLA-TAPAS code license on GitHub). GRCh37-only (liftover needed for GRCh38 inputs). Server deletes results after 7 days (plan automated retrieval).

name: neXtProt
description: Human-centric protein knowledgebase built on UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot and enriched with curated expression, PTM, variant, proteotypic-peptide and subcellular-localization data. Tracks the "missing proteins" / protein-existence (PE) evidence for the Human Proteome Project. A deeply annotated human "self" protein reference with peptide-level evidence.
scale: ~20,400 human protein entries; curated isoforms, PTMs, variants, peptides

provenance.maintainer: SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics (CALIPHO group)

relevance.why: Human-only, peptide-and-PTM-rich self reference; proteotypic-peptide and protein-existence annotation supports deciding whether a candidate antigen maps to a well-evidenced normal protein vs. an uncertain/missing one.

agent_access: REST API (api.nextprot.org) and SPARQL endpoint; bulk download of all annotations as XML/PEFF, plus per-entry XML/JSON/FASTA. No auth.
caveats: Data is CC BY 4.0 since 2018 (earlier releases were CC BY-ND; ignore journal-article CC BY-NC labels). Human only (no dog). Overlaps UniProt (it is built on Swiss-Prot) — use for the extra curation layer, dedup against UniProt by accession.

name: NMDP extended HLA haplotype frequency datasets (DPB1 / nine-locus, Zenodo deposits)
description: Updated and extended NMDP/CIBMTR HLA haplotype frequency datasets deposited on Zenodo, going beyond the classic six-locus 2013 tables. Includes CSV haplotype frequency distributions incorporating HLA-DPB1 (used for DPB1 permissive-mismatch match-likelihood work) and a more recent nine-locus classical-HLA frequency set estimated from ~10 million donors. These are the machine-readable, versioned companions to the registry match-likelihood publications.
scale: DPB1-inclusive haplotype CSVs; nine-locus set from ~10M donors across US registry populations

provenance.maintainer: NMDP / CIBMTR (Maiers, Gragert, Osoegawa et al.)

relevance.why: Current, DPB1-aware and nine-locus frequency priors improve population coverage estimates and HLA imputation validation beyond the legacy six-locus tables.

agent_access: Zenodo direct download (HTTPS), stable DOIs, no auth. Fully machine-readable CSV.
caveats: RED FLAG: the nine-locus Zenodo deposit is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — NonCommercial AND NoDerivatives, which forbids commercial use and forbids distributing modified/derived versions. This is a hard constraint for any commercial ML pipeline; the frequencies may be referenced but reprocessed/redistributed tables would violate ND. Verify the per-deposit license on each Zenodo record (the earlier DPB1 CSV may carry different terms). Registry-derived, US-ancestry-biased as in nmdp-haplotype-frequencies.

name: NMDP / Be The Match Registry HLA Haplotype Frequencies (US donor registry)
description: Population-level high-resolution HLA haplotype frequency estimates derived from the entire US National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP / Be The Match) volunteer donor registry. The 2013 release provides six-locus (A~C~B~DRB1~DRB3/4/5~DQB1) phased haplotype frequencies estimated by an expectation-maximisation algorithm from mixed-resolution typings of ~6.59 million donors, broken out by 21 detailed and 5 broad self-identified race/ethnicity categories. Distributed as downloadable frequency tables via the NMDP frequency portal.
scale: ~6.59M donor typings; 21 detailed + 5 broad populations; six-locus phased haplotype frequency tables

provenance.maintainer: National Marrow Donor Program / Be The Match (Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research, CIBMTR)

relevance.why: Reference allele/haplotype frequency priors for interpreting patient HLA genotypes, weighting population coverage of candidate epitopes, and sanity-checking HLA imputation output. Essential for population-aware antigen selection in a human program.

agent_access: Web portal with downloadable tables (no API). No auth; direct file download. Older high-resolution release is static (2011); check portal for newer versions before relying on currency.
caveats: No explicit SPDX license is posted on the NMDP frequency portal — confirm reuse/redistribution terms with NMDP before downstream distribution. US-registry-biased ancestry composition (self-identified race categories, not genetically-defined populations). Frequencies are registry-derived, not a random population sample. Cross-reference the Allele Frequency Net Database (catalogued in domain-1) for worldwide population frequencies.

name: Observed Antibody Space (OAS)
description: The reference corpus of cleaned, numbered, annotated and translated antibody repertoire sequences mined from published BCR/antibody next-generation sequencing studies. Contains both unpaired heavy/light-chain sequences and natively paired heavy-light sequences, each annotated with chain type, species, isotype, B-cell source, disease state and IMGT/ANARCI numbering. The de facto training set for antibody language models and generative antibody design.
scale: >1 billion unpaired sequences from >80 studies; paired subset on the order of ~1.5M+ heavy-light pairs (growing). 2021 paper reported ~1.5B unpaired + ~121,838 pairs; site now larger.

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), Dept of Statistics, University of Oxford

last_updated: 2025 (continuously updated as new studies are ingested)

relevance.why: The largest open antibody sequence resource and the natural prior for binder design against new targets: supplies CDR distributions, paired chains and the training corpus behind antibody LMs/structure predictors the design program would build on.

agent_access: Bulk download of the whole dataset or of filtered subsets built from the search forms (filter by chain type, species, isotype, disease, B-source). No auth. Downloads are per-study data units (CSV/JSON) served over HTTPS; easily scripted. No documented hard rate limit but be polite on bulk pulls.
caveats: Redistribution allowed under CC BY (attribute OPIG + original studies). Heavy study-to-study redundancy and sampling bias toward human peripheral blood; dedup and clonal-collapse needed before training. Paired data far smaller than unpaired. No canine repertoires — human/mouse dominate, so not a source for the comparative-oncology program.

name: OGRDB curated human IGH extended germline gene set
description: Versioned human immunoglobulin heavy-chain germline gene reference. The pinned source collection points to release 10 in AIRR format.

provenance.maintainer: Open Germline Receptor Database (OGRDB)

relevance.why: A versioned germline comparison for immunoglobulin-derived ligands.

agent_access: Retrieve the exact set and numbered release via HTTPS. Check the release date and checksum.
caveats: The downloaded data did not establish a redistribution license. A germline set omits rearranged and somatically hypermutated antibodies, including antibodies from normal B cells.

name: OMA (Orthologous MAtrix)
description: A large orthology database inferring orthologs across thousands of complete genomes, with OMA Groups, Hierarchical Orthologous Groups (HOGs), pairwise orthologs, and downloadable all-species protein/CDS FASTA. Provides evolutionarily grouped sequence sets useful for ortholog-aware corpora and comparative representation learning.
scale: ~2,983 complete genomes; ~26.5M proteins; ~1.5M OMA groups (May2026 release)

provenance.maintainer: Dessimoz Lab (SIB / University of Lausanne / UCL)

relevance.why: Ortholog groupings and all-species sequence sets for building evolution-aware corpora and for comparative (cross-species) analyses supporting design.

agent_access: Bulk download of protein/CDS FASTA + OrthoXML/TSV; REST API for targeted queries. No auth.
caveats: Current terms are CC BY 4.0 but older pages/papers cite CC BY-SA 2.5 or CC0 — rely on the live terms page. OMA name/logos may not be reused. Underlying source sequences may carry third-party constraints.

name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)
description: Curated catalogue of inherited and single-locus traits, disorders, and causal variants in animals (vertebrates), analogous to OMIM for humans. Includes many cancer-predisposition and tumor-related phenes and variants across dogs, cats, horses and other species, with cross-references to breeds, genes and literature. Full database is downloadable as a MySQL dump.
scale: thousands of phenes and likely-causal variants across >300 species

provenance.maintainer: University of Sydney (Sydney School of Veterinary Science) with ongoing community curation

relevance.why: Reference layer linking canine/feline/equine cancer phenotypes to genes and causal variants; supports breed-risk interpretation and comparative cancer-genetics annotation.

agent_access: Full MySQL dump (zipped/gzipped SQL and XML) is freely downloadable, no auth; no public API or SPARQL endpoint. A separate gene list maps OMIA internal gene IDs to NCBI gene IDs.
caveats: License is reported inconsistently across indexers (re3data: CC BY 4.0; Integbio: CC0; a Sydney library record: all-rights-reserved) — treat as CC BY 4.0 but verify, and honor OMIA's citation / co-authorship-discussion request for dump-based work. Internal gene IDs need mapping.

name: 1000 Genomes Project HLA types (IGSR high-resolution typing sets)
description: Classical HLA allele calls for the 1000 Genomes Project samples, served from the International Genome Sample Resource (IGSR) FTP. The most comprehensive set (Abi-Rached et al. 2018, PolyPheMe typing of the exomes) covers all 2,693 individuals; earlier sets (Gourraud et al. 2014) provide curated high-resolution HLA for a subset with population labels. Links genome-wide genotypes to orthogonal HLA typing for the canonical open human-genetics cohort.
scale: ~2,693 individuals (Abi-Rached 2018); subset high-resolution set (Gourraud 2014); 26 populations
license: custom (1000 Genomes Fort Lauderdale / open data)

provenance.maintainer: International Genome Sample Resource (IGSR) / EMBL-EBI

relevance.why: Ground-truth HLA calls paired with open WGS/WES across 26 populations — the default benchmark cohort for HLA typing-from-sequence tools and for linking HLA to population-genomic features.

agent_access: Anonymous IGSR/EBI FTP + HTTPS mirrors; no auth, bulk fetchable. Underlying 1000 Genomes genotypes are fully open.
caveats: HLA calls are computationally derived (imputation/typing-from-sequence), not gold-standard lab typing — accuracy varies by locus and allele frequency; different releases disagree. Confirm the exact FTP subpath and release version. 1000 Genomes open-data terms apply (attribution expected).

name: OrthoDB (hierarchical catalog of orthologs)
description: A hierarchical catalog of orthologous protein-coding genes across the tree of life, with orthologous groups computed at many taxonomic levels and bulk FASTA/mapping downloads. Provides broadly sampled, evolution-structured sequence sets; also the basis of BUSCO completeness assessment.
scale: v12.2: ~32,072 species; hundreds of thousands+ orthologous groups

provenance.maintainer: Zdobnov Lab (SIB / University of Geneva)

relevance.why: Wide-sampling ortholog groups and sequences for evolution-aware corpora, cross-species transfer, and comparative benchmarking.

agent_access: Bulk download (OG tables, species tables, gene mappings), REST API (v12), and SPARQL endpoint. No auth.
caveats: Current release CC BY 4.0; older v1x papers used CC BY-NC 3.0, and Wikipedia lists outdated CC BY 3.0 — verify current terms. v11 counts not confirmed here.

name: PANTHER (Protein ANalysis THrough Evolutionary Relationships)
description: Classification of proteins into evolutionarily related families/subfamilies with associated GO annotations, PANTHER protein-class terms, and curated PANTHER pathways. Underlies the GO Consortium's phylogenetic annotation (PAINT) and provides a protein- family and pathway feature layer and an enrichment service.
scale: ~15,000 protein families, ~180 curated pathways; ~140+ genomes
license: custom (free academic & commercial reuse; GNU LGPL for some components)

provenance.maintainer: Thomas lab (USC) / GO Consortium

relevance.why: Protein-family and protein-class assignments give a coarse, evolution-aware feature layer for grouping antigen/immune-related proteins and projecting annotation across species including dog.

agent_access: Bulk download of family/annotation flat files and HMMs, no auth. REST API and enrichment web services. Automatable; verify exact file-level terms before redistribution.
caveats: License terms are stated per-component rather than as a single SPDX id; confirm the specific file's terms before redistribution. Overlaps GO (PANTHER drives GO phylogenetic annotation) — use for the family/protein-class layer, dedup GO terms by source.

name: Pfam (protein families)
description: Library of protein families represented by curated multiple sequence alignments and profile HMMs, now delivered through InterPro. Many families carry structural mappings (to PDB/CATH via InterPro/SIFTS), making Pfam a bridge between sequence family space and structure.
scale: Pfam 37.x/38.0: ~20,000+ families

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI (formerly Wellcome Sanger); integrated into InterPro

relevance.why: Curated family MSAs and HMMs are standard conditioning/pretraining inputs for evolutionary-coupling and folding models; seed alignments give high-quality sequence groupings tied to structural families.

agent_access: Open FTP bulk download (full Pfam-A.hmm, seed/full alignments). No auth. Agent-mirrorable. Interactive access via the InterPro site/API.
caveats: Standalone pfam.xfam.org was decommissioned; access is now via InterPro and the EBI FTP. Pfam-produced data is CC0, but downstream UniProt sequence content has its own (CC BY 4.0) terms.

name: PLAbDab — Patent and Literature Antibody Database
description: A curated, literature- and patent-annotated reference set of (mostly paired) antibody sequences with functional context: each entry links back to the patent or paper it was scraped from, and many are functionally characterised (antigen, therapeutic use). Searchable by keyword, sequence and structure, with ABodyBuilder2 models attached to entries.
scale: >150,000 paired sequences, >65,000 unique; full data bundle ~4.7 GB; paired-sequence CSV ~11 MB
license: CC BY 4.0 (NAR article); database redistribution terms not separately stated

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

relevance.why: Unlike raw repertoires, PLAbDab entries carry antigen/function annotation and literature provenance, making it a high-value, functionally grounded set of developed/paired antibodies to anchor design and to find natural analogues of candidate binders.

agent_access: Web app with keyword/sequence/structure search and a Download link for all hits of a query; precomputed structural models downloadable per entry. Python API via the oxpig/PLAbDab GitHub repo (contact maintainers / open an issue for programmatic access). Structural models bulk-archived on Zenodo.
caveats: The PLAbDab "about" page states no explicit license (license: unknown), even though sibling OPIG resources OAS and CoV-AbDab are CC BY 4.0 — confirm terms before redistribution; patent-derived sequences may carry IP considerations. Attribute Abanades et al. 2024.

name: PLAbDab-nano — nanobodies from patents and literature
description: The single-domain (nanobody) companion to PLAbDab: camelid VHH and shark VNAR sequences curated from patents and literature, each linked to its source and shipped with a precomputed NanoBodyBuilder2 structural model. Annotated with domain type (VHH/VNAR), CDR lengths and CDR sequences.
scale: ~4,913 entries (VHH + VNAR)

provenance.maintainer: Oxford Protein Informatics Group (OPIG), University of Oxford

relevance.why: Literature/patent-grounded single-domain antibodies with attached structural models — directly useful for the nanobody binder-design program and for benchmarking generated VHH/VNAR loops against real ones.

agent_access: Three gzipped CSV downloads (all / VHH-only / VNAR-only) plus a Python package (oxpig/PLAbDab_nano) that reads the extracted database. Web app supports keyword/sequence/structure search. No auth; trivially scriptable.
caveats: No explicit license on the page (license: unknown) — confirm before reuse; attribute Gordon et al. 2025. The preprint warned that many patent/literature "nanobody" hits are false positives (VHH count dropped from ~21k to <7k after curation) — trust the curated published counts, not raw scrapes.

name: PRIME neo-epitope immunogenicity dataset (CD8 T-cell response training data)
description: The experimentally-tested peptide immunogenicity dataset underpinning PRIME, a predictor of CD8 T-cell neo-epitope immunogenicity. Combines peptides tested for T-cell response from pathogens and cancer-testis antigens (~1,629) with cancer mutations (~3,329) plus random negatives, each labelled immunogenic/non-immunogenic with HLA restriction — a rare *functional immunogenicity* label set (not just binding/presentation). PRIME2.0 adds further labelled datasets.
scale: ~1,629 pathogen/CTA + ~3,329 cancer-mutation peptides, immunogenicity-labelled, with HLA restriction

provenance.maintainer: Gfeller lab (Ludwig Institute / University of Lausanne; Schmidt, Gfeller et al.)

relevance.why: Functional immunogenicity labels (did a T-cell respond?) are scarcer and more valuable than binding labels for neoantigen prioritization — this is a core training/validation set for immunogenicity models.

agent_access: Training data in Cell Rep Med supplementary tables + GfellerLab/PRIME GitHub; git-cloneable. Agent- fetchable (supplementary tables may need PDF/XLSX extraction).
caveats: RED FLAG: PRIME tool/data are academic / non-commercial use per the Gfeller lab terms — confirm before commercial training. Immunogenicity labels are assay- and cohort-dependent (negatives are "not observed", not proven non-immunogenic). Some peptides overlap IEDB sources. HLA coverage skewed to common alleles.

name: Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase
description: Manually curated, peer-reviewed knowledgebase of human biological pathways and reactions (signal transduction, metabolism, immune system, etc.), with computationally inferred orthologous pathways for additional species. Provides pathway hierarchies, reaction participants, and a pathway-analysis/enrichment service.
scale: ~2,700 human pathways, ~15,000 reactions, ~11,000 proteins; orthology to ~15 species

provenance.maintainer: Reactome Consortium (OICR, EMBL-EBI, NYULMC, OHSU; NIH/EBI funded)
