caveats: Data license not explicitly stated — verify. Restricted to the 146 pMHCs with enough data. No dog.

name: NetTCR-2.0 training/evaluation data
description: Data released with NetTCR-2.0 for paired alpha/beta TCR-peptide binding prediction: positive TCR-peptide pairs from IEDB+VDJdb, negatives derived from 10x single-cell data, with similarity-partitioned CDR3b training sets and MIRA/paired external evaluation files.
scale: ~2,744 unique paired positive pairs; ~387,598 10x-derived negatives

provenance.maintainer: Nielsen Lab, DTU

relevance.why: Widely used, pre-partitioned paired-chain benchmark with a principled negative set — a standard comparison point for any recognition model we build.

agent_access: Flat CSVs in the GitHub repo data folder; git clone / direct download, no auth. Fully automatable.
caveats: Stated academic/non-commercial only — red flag for commercial ML; confirm. Negatives inherit 10x dextramer assumptions; small positive set. Human only.

name: PanPep meta-learning TCR-antigen dataset
description: Curated TCR-peptide binding data and a large control (negative) dataset released with PanPep, a meta-learning model for zero-/few-shot TCR-antigen recognition across unseen peptides.
scale: control dataset ~927 MB; code package small

provenance.maintainer: Li lab, Tongji University (bm2-lab)

relevance.why: Few-shot/zero-shot framing matches the real problem of unseen tumor neoepitopes; its control set is a sizeable negative pool.

agent_access: Zenodo direct download (~928 MB control file + code zip); no auth. A later reusability-report deposit (10.5281/zenodo.16943691) adds re-curated data.
caveats: Zenodo record names no explicit license (open access right only) — verify reuse terms. Human only.

name: PIRD / TBAdb (Pan Immune Repertoire Database)
description: CNGB-hosted pan immune repertoire database collecting annotated TCR and BCR sequencing data across species and conditions. TBAdb is its manually curated sub-database of TCRs/BCRs targeting known antigens.
scale: TBAdb: curated antigen-specific TCR/BCR records; PIRD: many repertoire datasets

provenance.maintainer: China National GeneBank (CNGB) / BGI

relevance.why: TBAdb is a third curated antigen-specific TCR set (alongside VDJdb/McPAS) for recognition training; PIRD adds repertoire breadth and some non-human species.

agent_access: Web portal on db.cngb.org; download may require a CNGB account. No documented open API; likely scripted/portal download. Confirm access gating.
caveats: No explicit license located — verify terms. Overlaps VDJdb/McPAS; dedup needed. Dog coverage not confirmed (PIRD claims multi-species but canine content unverified).

name: pMTnet / pMTnet-Omni training & validation datasets
description: Data accompanying the pMTnet family of TCR-pMHC affinity predictors. pMTnet-Omni covers Va/Vb/CDR3a/CDR3b + peptide + MHC (class I and II, human and mouse); the package ships reference databases and 5 validation datasets, with training data described in the papers.
scale: validation: 5 datasets; training: large aggregated pairs (see papers)

provenance.maintainer: Wang Lab, UT Southwestern (DBAI)

relevance.why: Paired-chain + class II coverage (incl. mouse) is rare; useful both as a baseline predictor and for its curated reference/validation pairs.

agent_access: Validation data and reference DB bundled with the pip package (pMTnet_Omni_Document); full prediction runs through the DBAI website (upload). Validation data auto-fetchable; training corpus must be assembled from the data-availability statement.
caveats: No explicit dataset license located — verify. Validation sets are formatting examples, not the full training data. Model drops records whose TCR names are not in its reference DB. No dog.

name: PRIME2.0 / MixMHCpred2.2 immunogenicity & presentation training data
description: Training and benchmark data for the Gfeller-lab PRIME2.0 (TCR-recognition / immunogenicity) and MixMHCpred2.2 (presentation) predictors: curated HLA-I ligand sets and neo-epitope immunogenicity data with position-specific TCR-contact features, applied to reveal cross-reactive SARS-CoV-2 CD8 epitopes. Distinct release from PRIME v1.
scale: HLA-I ligand + neo-epitope immunogenicity sets (Datasets S2/S3) with decoy negatives
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (paper/data); code per GfellerLab repos

provenance.maintainer: Gfeller lab, Ludwig Institute / University of Lausanne

relevance.why: State-of-the-art immunogenicity/presentation training data with explicit TCR-contact position features and decoy negatives — a strong complement to prime-immunogenicity (v1) and a benchmark for both presentation and recognition.

agent_access: Datasets in the Cell Systems supplementary files and the Zenodo archive (10.5281/zenodo.7375740); predictors on GitHub (GfellerLab). No auth.
caveats: CC BY-NC 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL only (ML/commercial redistribution red flag). Distinct from prime-immunogenicity (v1) already catalogued; dedup overlapping neo-epitopes. Negatives are same-protein decoys, not experimentally confirmed non-immunogenic.

name: PRJNA476127 — Canine IGH Repertoire, 3 Healthy Dogs x 3 Lymphoid Organs (Guelph; Vet Immunol Immunopathol 2018)
description: 5'-RACE amplicon sequencing (Illumina MiSeq) of the immunoglobulin heavy-chain repertoire from lymph node, spleen and bone marrow of 3 healthy dogs (9 biosamples, 36 runs). The data were analysed with ARResT/Interrogate in the first comprehensive NGS characterisation of the canine IGH repertoire.
scale: 9 samples (3 dogs x 3 organs), 36 runs

provenance.maintainer: University of Guelph (BioProject submitter)

relevance.why: A healthy-dog, multi-organ IGH baseline that resolves the domain-14 gap for the 2018 IGH repertoire study. It pairs with PRJNA790470 (healthy and lymphoma IGH/IGK/IGL) and the IMGT canine germline.

caveats: The paper-to-BioProject link is inferred: submitter (Guelph), registration date (2018-06, paper 2018-07) and design (3 dogs x 3 organs, 5'-RACE MiSeq) all match, but the paywalled article's data statement was not read. Heavy chain only. No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJNA790470 — Canine Immunoglobulin (IGH/IGK/IGL) Repertoire NGS (PLoS ONE 2022)
description: 5'-RACE next-generation sequencing of the canine immunoglobulin (BCR) repertoire — IGH, IGK and IGL — from 25 healthy control dogs and 18 dogs with intermediate-to-large B-cell lymphoma (pre-treatment T1; 13 also sampled post-treatment T2), with a dedicated bioinformatics pipeline (PLoS ONE 2022). One of the few unbiased high-throughput canine BCR repertoire datasets.
scale: 25 healthy + 18 BCL dogs (13 paired post-treatment); IGH/IGK/IGL

provenance.maintainer: (see paper — PLoS ONE 2022)

relevance.why: Rare canine BCR/antibody repertoire resource with a disease (B-cell lymphoma) vs healthy contrast and longitudinal treatment samples — directly supports canine antibody/BCR modeling in the recognition arm.

caveats: No explicit reuse license (NCBI/INSDC open). Reads concatenated by sample/time point. Pair with IMGT canine germline for V(D)J assignment. Repertoire depth per sample should be checked before clonality analysis.

name: PRJNA857425 — Canine FVIII-specific BCR Repertoires in Hemophilia A Dogs (UPenn 2022)
description: Antibody phage display combined with NGS of total and FVIII-specific B-cell receptor repertoires from 3 severe hemophilia A dogs with high-titre inhibitors against canine FVIII (13 runs).
scale: 3 dogs, 13 runs

provenance.maintainer: University of Pennsylvania

relevance.why: Antigen-specific canine BCR sequences are scarce. This set pairs repertoires with a known antigen, which is useful for canine antibody modelling and specificity-inference benchmarks. It is not a cancer dataset.

caveats: Not cancer: an alloimmune response to a therapeutic protein. Linked paper not located. No explicit reuse license.

name: PRJNA971129 — Canine Immunoglobulin VH/VL Repertoire in Mammary Tumour and Hyperplasia (UNESP 2023)
description: Amplicon sequencing of expressed immunoglobulin heavy and light variable-region repertoires from hyperplastic and tumoral mammary tissue of female dogs (12 samples). The project reports >18,000 filtered V-region sequences and a previously unsequenced, highly variable IGHD region.
scale: 12 samples (amplicon); >18,000 V sequences

provenance.maintainer: São Paulo State University (UNESP)

relevance.why: The only canine tumour-infiltrating BCR repertoire data we found, from the tumour bed rather than blood.

caveats: No linked publication found; runs became public 2026-06. Small n. No explicit reuse license.

name: Repitope — curated T-cell epitope immunogenicity datasets
description: R package and compiled dataset for quantitative epitope immunogenicity prediction via repertoire-wide TCR-peptide contact profiling. Bundles harmonised MHC-I and MHC-II immunogenicity tables (Human/Rodent/Primate) assembled from IEDB plus Calis, Chowell, EPIMHC, MHCBN, TANTIGEN, HCV/HIV and IMMA2 source sets, with a public TCR CDR3b set.
scale: tens of thousands of immunogenicity-labeled peptides across MHC-I and MHC-II
license: code MIT; bundled data inherit source-DB licenses (mixed)

provenance.maintainer: Masato Ogishi (University of Tokyo)

relevance.why: A ready, de-duplicated multi-source immunogenicity corpus spanning MHC-I and MHC-II and multiple species — directly usable as training/benchmark for immunogenicity and as a consolidated set of hard negatives.

agent_access: Package + raw CSVs on GitHub; large feature/fragment tables and immunogenicity scores on Mendeley Data; TCR reads in DDBJ SRA (DRA005827). No auth; bulk-friendly.
caveats: Code is MIT but the bundled data carry the licenses of their SOURCE databases (IEDB open; others e.g. EPIMHC/MHCBN/TANTIGEN vary) — verify per-source redistribution before republishing (mixed-license flag). Some sources are legacy/defunct DBs.

name: Saini et al. 2021 — genome-wide SARS-CoV-2 CD8 epitope map (DNA-barcoded multimers)
description: Genome-wide screen of SARS-CoV-2 CD8 T-cell recognition using DNA-barcoded peptide-MHC multimers against 3,141 predicted MHC-I binders, yielding a ranked list of immunogenic and immunodominant epitopes with donor-level recognition data in COVID-19 patients and healthy donors. A labeled immunogenic-vs-non-immunogenic pMHC resource at proteome scale for one virus.
scale: 3,141 peptides screened; 122 immunogenic epitopes reported (paper)

provenance.maintainer: Hadrup lab, DTU (Saini, Hersby, Tamhane et al.)

relevance.why: Rare proteome-wide positive/negative immunogenicity labeling for a single pathogen — the non-recognised-but-bound peptides are high-value hard negatives for pMHC immunogenicity models that most databases lack.

agent_access: Epitope and screening tables are in the paper's supplementary materials (publisher site). No bulk API; barcode count matrices, if deposited, are referenced in Data Availability.
caveats: Data live in journal supplementary files (license not separately stated — flag as unknown); extraction is manual. Negatives are assay-specific (binding-predicted but multimer-negative), not validated non-binders.

name: Shomuradova et al. 2020 — SARS-CoV-2 public CD8/CD4 TCR repertoire
description: Primary study deposit of SARS-CoV-2 epitope-specific TCRs, dominated by the HLA-A*02:01 spike epitope YLQPRTFLL, with tetramer-sorted alpha/beta sequences from convalescent and vaccinated donors showing a public, convergent repertoire. Underlying sequencing and analysis notebooks are released openly; curated specificity records fed into VDJdb.
scale: hundreds of epitope-specific TCR clonotypes across ~50 donors (paper)
license: code MIT/Apache per repo; curated records via VDJdb (CC BY-ND 4.0)

provenance.maintainer: Efimov & Shugay groups (data mirrored into VDJdb)

relevance.why: A clean, deeply characterised single-epitope (YLQ/A2) TCR set — a canonical positive bucket for public-repertoire and cross-reactivity modeling in TCR-epitope prediction.

agent_access: Processed tables and R notebooks on GitHub (no auth); extended-data tables in the paper. Curated specificity also retrievable via the VDJdb SARS-CoV-2 filter.
caveats: Single study, epitope-skewed (YLQ-heavy) — not a balanced benchmark. Overlaps the VDJdb SARS-CoV-2 compendium; dedup. Raw-read deposit not confirmed in an INSDC archive from public sources — verify the paper's Data Availability for any ENA/SRA accession.

name: TChard
description: Aggregated benchmark dataset for TCR-peptide/pMHC binding prediction, built to be the largest such collection at publication by merging IEDB, VDJdb, McPAS-TCR and the NetTCR-2.0 data, with controlled negative generation and hard (unseen-peptide) evaluation splits.
scale: >500,000 samples

provenance.maintainer: NEC Laboratories Europe (Grazioli et al.)

relevance.why: Ready-made, pre-split benchmark for honest unseen-peptide generalization testing — directly reusable for evaluating our recognition models.

agent_access: Direct Zenodo download (no auth) and loadable via PyTDC DataLoader(name="tchard"). Fully automatable.
caveats: Non-commercial license — a red flag for any commercial/productized ML use; confirm before use. Aggregated from upstream DBs so inherits their biases and overlaps; human only, no dog.

name: TCRdb (HUST / TCRdb2.0)
description: Large aggregated database of TCR sequences from reprocessed public TCR-seq/RNA-seq projects with a search function; TCRdb 2.0 (2025/26) massively expands it and adds a very large healthy-control reference. Mostly specificity-agnostic bulk repertoires.
scale: ~277M sequences / 130 studies (v1); ~700M sequences / 19,701 samples (v2.0)
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (paper; data terms per site)

provenance.maintainer: Guo Lab (HUST / West China Hospital, SCU)

relevance.why: Scale repertoire background for negative sampling, V/J usage priors and clonotype frequency modeling — not antigen-labeled, but foundational for repertoire context.

agent_access: Per-sample/per-project download via the web portal; no documented programmatic API or bulk tarball, so automated retrieval likely means scripted page-driven downloads.
caveats: Paper is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — flag for commercial use; confirm data terms on site. TCRdb 2.0 DOI should be verified on the site (listed here as best-effort). Specificity-agnostic (no antigen labels) — pair with labeled sets.

name: 10x Genomics CD8+ T cells of Healthy Donors 1-4 (dextramer release)
description: Four public 10x single-cell datasets (one per healthy donor) pairing 5' gene expression, TotalSeq-C surface protein, paired TCR, and ~50 dCODE Dextramer (pMHC multimer) readouts (44 antigen + 6 negative controls). Each donor is a separate downloadable dataset with a per-cell binarized specificity matrix. The canonical large single-cell TCR-to-pMHC release.
scale: >150,000 CD8+ T cells total across 4 donors; ~50 pMHC multimers each

provenance.maintainer: 10x Genomics

relevance.why: The most-used public single-cell dataset with paired TCR + pMHC specificity labels — core training/benchmark data for TCR-antigen recognition models.

agent_access: Four separate dataset pages (Donor 1-4); each offers direct file download (binarized matrix CSV, filtered feature matrices, VDJ), no auth (CC BY 4.0). Scriptable per donor.
caveats: Raw dextramer calls are noisy; specificity call = binding UMI >10 AND >5x max negative control, excluding cells with >4 specificities. Prefer the ICON-curated subset (~53,062 cells, Zhang et al. 2021) for clean labels. pMHC/HLA nomenclature: cross-ref presentation agent.

name: 10x Genomics "A New Way of Exploring Immunity" — CD8 dextramer dataset
description: Public 10x single-cell immune-profiling dataset pairing gene expression, cell-surface protein (feature barcoding) and paired TCR sequence with ~44 dextramer (pMHC multimer) readouts per cell across four healthy donors — i.e. single-cell TCR-to-pMHC specificity labels from barcoded multimer binding.
scale: >150,000 CD8+ T cells across 4 donors, ~44 dextramers each

provenance.maintainer: 10x Genomics

relevance.why: One of the largest public single-cell datasets with paired TCR + pMHC specificity labels — core training data for TCR-antigen recognition models.

agent_access: Direct file download from the 10x datasets/support site, no auth (CC BY). Scriptable per-donor. Multiple files (GEX, protein, VDJ, dextramer counts) per donor.
caveats: Raw dextramer calls are noisy (high background); most downstream work uses the ICON- curated subset (~53k cells, Zhang et al. 2021) with corrected pMHC/TCR annotations — prefer that for labels. pMHC/HLA nomenclature: cross-ref the presentation agent.

name: TetTCR-seq barcoded-tetramer single-cell TCR specificity dataset (Zhang 2018)
description: Data from TetTCR-seq, which pairs DNA-barcoded pMHC tetramers (made rapidly by in vitro transcription/translation) with single-cell TCR sequencing to link TCR sequence to antigen specificity at scale. Released as six "TetTCR-seq summary" supplementary tables (experiments 1-6) linking TCRs to tetramer-barcode specificities.
scale: Thousands of single cells; 6 experiment summary tables of TCR-to-antigen pairings

provenance.maintainer: Zhang, Ma, Jiang et al. (UT Austin / UPenn)

relevance.why: Paired TCR-sequence/antigen-specificity data from a non-10x barcoded-tetramer platform; direct training/test material for TCR-pMHC specificity prediction.

agent_access: Six supplementary Excel tables from the Nature Biotechnology article page (no auth for SI). Raw sequencing not clearly deposited in a public GEO/SRA accession.
caveats: Data only as journal SI (Springer Nature terms, no open license). Raw reads location not confirmed — pairings available, raw FASTQ may be restricted/absent.

name: TetTCR-SeqHD high-dimensional barcoded-tetramer T-cell dataset (Ma 2021)
description: TetTCR-SeqHD jointly profiles antigen specificity (DNA-barcoded pMHC tetramers), gene expression, surface phenotype, and paired alpha/beta TCR sequence in single CD8 T cells. The study profiled ~33,000 single cells from healthy donors and type-1-diabetes donors; raw sequencing is deposited at dbGaP (controlled access).
scale: ~32,992 single cells; GEX + phenotype + paired TCR + tetramer-barcode antigen

provenance.maintainer: Ma, Schonnesen, Jiang et al. (UT Austin / UPenn); dbGaP

relevance.why: A rich multimodal barcoded-tetramer dataset (antigen + TCR + transcriptome + phenotype) beyond the 10x releases; valuable for jointly modelling TCR specificity and T-cell state, if dbGaP access is obtained.

agent_access: Raw sequencing is controlled-access under dbGaP phs002441 (requires an approved Data Use Certification). Summary tables accompany the paper as SI.
caveats: Controlled-access (dbGaP DUA) for raw data — catalog but note the gate. SI tables are open but under Springer Nature terms.

name: TITAN TCR-epitope dataset (VDJdb + ImmuneCODE)
description: Training/eval data for TITAN bimodal-attention TCR specificity model, assembled from VDJdb plus the Adaptive ImmuneCODE COVID release, filtered to single-epitope productive sequences with generated negatives. ESM-1b embedding copy also released for the TDC task.
scale: large VDJdb+ImmuneCODE TCR-epitope set (incl. COVID expansion)

provenance.maintainer: IBM Research / PaccMann

relevance.why: Demonstrates the VDJdb+ImmuneCODE combination we would likely use; TDC embedding copy is a ready feature set.

agent_access: Data via GitHub repo + Zenodo (ESM embeddings); no auth. Note ImmuneCODE-derived rows inherit Adaptive terms.
caveats: Incorporates ImmuneCODE (Adaptive "Research Use Only" terms — redistribution/ML red flag). Repo data license unspecified. Human only.

name: VDJdb
description: Manually curated database of TCR sequences (CDR3 alpha/beta plus V/J) with known antigen (epitope + restricting MHC) specificity, aggregated from the literature and from paired single-cell studies. Each record carries a confidence score and, in recent releases, paratope embeddings, noise filtering and predicted 3D structures.
scale: tens of thousands of TCR-epitope records across many epitopes (growing)
license: CC BY 4.0 (database records; verify current repo LICENSE)

provenance.maintainer: Shugay/Chudakov groups (antigenomics)

relevance.why: Standardized, confidence-scored TCR-epitope ground truth — a backbone training/eval set for antigen-recognition models and for harmonizing other assay sources.

agent_access: GitHub release tarballs (vdjdb-db) and Zenodo DOI snapshots for reproducible pinning; REST API (POST /api/database/search) via vdjdb-web; vdjmatch (GPL-3) and immunarch for programmatic querying. Fully automatable, no auth.
caveats: CC BY-ND forbids distributing modified versions, a redistribution/ML red flag — our derived training files cannot be republished verbatim. License metadata is inconsistent across sources (one GitHub listing showed AGPL-3.0); verify the LICENSE file per release. Heavy overlap with IEDB/McPAS requires dedup. No dog coverage.

name: VDJdb high-confidence subset
description: Filtered view of VDJdb restricted to records with higher confidence scores (legacy 0-3 score >= 1, or the newer v3.2a assay-validation / v3.2b cross-study probabilities). Not a separate database — a quality-gated slice of VDJdb used by most benchmark pipelines to reduce false positives.
scale: subset of VDJdb; size depends on score threshold (tens of thousands)

provenance.maintainer: Shugay/Chudakov groups (antigenomics)

relevance.why: The cleaner slice we would actually train/evaluate recognition models on; filtering is done client-side after download.

agent_access: Same as VDJdb; apply score filter locally after bulk download or via the web filter params.
caveats: Thresholds are not standardized across papers — document the exact filter. Same CC BY-ND redistribution limit as VDJdb.

name: VDJdb SARS-CoV-2 TCR compendium ("pandemic-era" release)
description: A dedicated SARS-CoV-2 slice of VDJdb curated during the pandemic, aggregating TCRs with confirmed specificity to SARS-CoV-2 epitopes from many deposited studies (tetramer, MIRA, single-cell). Distributed as part of the normal VDJdb release rather than a separate file, but described and versioned in its own Nature Methods report.
scale: ~3,187 unique TCR-specificity records across 46 SARS-CoV-2 epitopes (2022 paper)

provenance.maintainer: Shugay/Chudakov groups (antigenomics)

relevance.why: The single largest curated set of SARS-CoV-2-specific TCRs; a ready viral benchmark and training supplement for TCR-epitope recognition, complementing ImmuneCODE's bulk-TCR MIRA data with paired/annotated specificities.

agent_access: Filter the standard VDJdb TSV release on antigen.species == SARS-CoV-2 after bulk download, or query the REST API. No auth.
caveats: NOT a distinct deposit — it is a subset inside VDJdb (already catalogued as vdjdb); dedup against vdjdb and immunecode-mira. CC BY-ND 4.0 forbids distributing modified versions (redistribution/ML red flag). Aggregates heterogeneous source assays of uneven quality.

name: BACH (ICIAR 2018) — breast cancer histology microscopy & WSIs
description: Breast-cancer histology challenge dataset: 400 training + 100 test H&E microscopy images (2048x1536) labeled into four classes (normal, benign, in situ carcinoma, invasive carcinoma), plus 30 pixel-annotated whole-slide images (10 train / 10 test labeled + 10 unlabeled) with region masks. A widely used benchmark for four-class breast histology classification/segmentation.
scale: 400 train + 100 test microscopy images (4-class); 30 WSIs with region annotations

provenance.maintainer: INESC TEC / i3S, University of Porto (Aresta, Araújo, Polónia et al.)

relevance.why: Four-class human breast histology benchmark (incl. in situ vs. invasive) for pretraining and validating tissue-morphology classifiers that feed multimodal models.

agent_access: Bulk download from Zenodo (DOI), no auth; challenge portal mirror also exists. Scriptable over HTTPS.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 is NON-COMMERCIAL and NO-DERIVATIVES (the most restrictive CC combination; derivative/processed-data releases are not permitted under the license). A Kaggle mirror lists license as Unknown — use the Zenodo record's terms.

name: Baker lab de novo pMHC-I binder design (code + designed structure)
description: Release accompanying "Design of high-specificity binders for peptide-MHC-I complexes": RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN design code and examples for building proteins that read out disease-linked peptides on MHC-I, plus a deposited experimental structure of a designed binder-antigen complex.
scale: Design code + examples (Zenodo v1.0.0); specific binders identified for 11 target pMHC-I; MART-1 binder-antigen complex in PDB (9O5S)
license: unknown (check Zenodo record); PDB entry 9O5S is CC0

provenance.maintainer: Baker Lab / Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington

relevance.why: The flagship public demonstration and code for de novo peptide-MHC-I binder design — the most directly applicable methodology and worked example for Veritope's pMHC binder program.

agent_access: Code + examples archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.15169815); designed structure retrievable from PDB (9O5S). Scriptable.
caveats: Zenodo license not confirmed (marked unknown). Only one designed complex is deposited (9O5S); full design sets live in supplements. Companion NY-ESO-1 minibinder paper (10.1126/science.adv0422) reuses prior RFdiffusion releases.

name: BreakHis — Breast Cancer Histopathological Database
description: Microscopy image database of breast tumor tissue from 82 patients, acquired from surgical (excisional) biopsy at four magnifications (40x, 100x, 200x, 400x). 7,909 RGB images (2,480 benign, 5,429 malignant) across eight tumor subtypes. A long-standing benchmark for patch/image-level benign-vs-malignant and subtype classification.
scale: 7,909 images, 82 patients, 4 magnifications, 8 tumor subtypes (~4 GB)

provenance.maintainer: Laboratório Visão Robótica e Imagem (VRI), Universidade Federal do Paraná (UFPR)

relevance.why: Compact, cleanly licensed human breast tumor histology set for pretraining/benchmarking morphology classifiers that feed multimodal tissue-molecular models.

agent_access: Single tar.gz over HTTP (~4 GB); no auth. Site requests (but does not require) a form after download. IEEE DataPort (DOI 10.21227/mtd3-kx92) and Kaggle mirrors exist. Fully scriptable.
caveats: CC BY 4.0 confirmed on the UFPR page. Note intro text says 9,109 images but the table (authoritative) lists 7,909. Magnification-specific folds require careful patient-level splitting to avoid leakage.

name: CAMELYON16 / CAMELYON17 — sentinel lymph node metastasis WSIs
description: Benchmark whole-slide-image datasets for automated detection of breast-cancer metastases in H&E sentinel lymph node sections. CAMELYON16 (399 WSIs, 2 centers) targets slide-level metastasis detection with lesion-level contour annotations for 209 slides; CAMELYON17 (1,000 WSIs, 5 centers) adds patient-level pN-stage classification. Together the canonical computational-pathology benchmark.
scale: 1,399 WSIs (399 + 1,000), ~3 TB; detailed metastasis contours for 209 slides

provenance.maintainer: Diagnostic Image Analysis Group, Radboud UMC / Utrecht / GigaScience

relevance.why: Gold-standard human tumor-vs-immune (lymph node) WSI benchmark; useful for pretraining and validating tissue-level tumor detection in multimodal pathology models.

agent_access: Bulk download from GigaDB (HTTP/FTP), with mirrors on Google Drive/Baidu; CAMELYON17 grand-challenge portal may require free registration. Large multi-GB pyramidal TIFFs; scriptable over HTTPS/FTP.
caveats: CC0 per the GigaScience paper and GigaDB record (a ResearchGate copy mislabels it CC BY 4.0 — the publisher CC0 is authoritative). ~3 TB total; plan storage. Test-set labels for the challenge leaderboards are partly sequestered.

name: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA)
description: The primary public repository of de-identified medical images of cancer (CT, MRI, PET, mammography, digital pathology whole-slide images and more), organized into disease- and project-specific Collections, many cross-linked to TCGA/CPTAC molecular data via shared subject barcodes. Serves raw DICOM plus expert segmentations, radiomic features and clinical metadata. Underpins most public radiogenomics and imaging-AI research.
scale: 200+ collections, millions of images, tens of millions of DICOM objects across many cancer types
license: mixed: most collections CC BY 3.0 / CC BY 4.0; some TCIA Limited-Access / Restricted

provenance.maintainer: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences / Frederick National Lab, funded by NCI Cancer Imaging Program

relevance.why: Canonical source of human tumor imaging paired (via TCGA/CPTAC barcodes) with molecular profiles; the substrate for multimodal models that relate radiology/histology phenotype to genomics and the immune microenvironment.

agent_access: NBIA REST API and the TCIA/IDC Python clients allow programmatic query and bulk DICOM download, no auth for open collections. Brain/head-neck and some others now require a signed Limited-Access or Restricted License Agreement emailed to TCIA (not agent-fetchable).
caveats: LICENSE VARIES PER COLLECTION AND PER VERSION — do not assume CC BY. Effective 2022-01-06 all brain, head, and head/neck collections moved from Creative Commons to a TCIA Limited-Access License (registration + agreement). Some older collection pages state CC BY 3.0 with a non-commercial note that conflicts with the general policy; treat the collection landing page as authoritative and cite the full data citation, not the wiki URL.

name: Canine Immunology Reagents / CD-Marker Antibody Resources
description: The practical reagent layer for canine immunology: commercial anti-dog CD-marker monoclonal antibodies (CD3/CD4/CD5/CD8/CD21 etc., with clones + RRIDs) from Bio-Rad and others, rooted in the International Canine Leukocyte Antigen Workshop (CLAW) homolog assignments. No central curated public database — a scattered vendor/literature landscape.
scale: dozens of validated clones across core CD markers; no unified count

provenance.maintainer: Bio-Rad, LSBio, BioVenic (vendors); RRID registry (SciCrunch)

relevance.why: Reagent availability constrains any wet-lab canine immunology (sorting DLA+ cells, validating T-cell subsets); documents the tooling gap relative to human/mouse.

agent_access: Vendor catalogs scrapeable; RRIDs queryable via SciCrunch API. No research dataset to download.
caveats: GAP ALERT: canine immune reagents are scarce and fragmented vs human/mouse; many rely on cross-reactive anti-human/anti-bovine clones. No open, curated reagent database.

name: cBioPortal for Cancer Genomics
description: Aggregation, query and visualization platform hosting hundreds of published cancer genomics studies (TCGA, MSK-IMPACT, GENIE public, metastatic cohorts, and more) as harmonized mutation, copy-number, fusion, expression and clinical matrices. The public instance exposes everything through a documented REST API and downloadable per-study archives; private deployments can host controlled data.
scale: hundreds of studies (public instance); counts vary by release
license: ODC Open Database License (ODbL) for data unless noted; software Apache-2.0 (AGPL-3.0 pre-2026)

provenance.maintainer: Memorial Sloan Kettering (cBio Center) + consortium

relevance.why: Fastest programmatic route to harmonized somatic mutation + expression across many cohorts without per-study DUAs — ideal for assembling neoantigen candidate sets and recurrence/frequency priors.

agent_access: Public REST API (Swagger), R (cBioPortalData, cbioportalR) and Python clients, plus per-study ZIP archives and a Data Hub for bulk. No auth on the public instance; rate limits apply to the API. Fully automatable.
caveats: Data under ODbL (attribution + share-alike of derived databases) unless a study notes otherwise — check per-study. Processed/derived data only (no raw reads). Hosts public GENIE, which still carries GENIE's no-redistribution terms (see aacr-genie).

name: CZ CELLxGENE Discover (+ Census)
description: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative portal aggregating standardized, cell-typed single-cell datasets (incl. Tabula Sapiens, HLCA, heart/gut atlases, HCA collections) with a programmatic Census for querying tens of millions of normal cells in a harmonized schema. The primary access layer for normal single-cell references.
scale: >100M cells across standardized collections; Census spans the corpus

provenance.maintainer: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative

relevance.why: Single harmonized interface + API to most normal single-cell references — the efficient way to query "which cell types express target X across normal tissues" at scale.

agent_access: cellxgene-census (Python/R, SOMA/TileDB) for programmatic slicing without downloading whole datasets; per-dataset .h5ad download via HTTPS. No auth.
caveats: Aggregator: each underlying dataset keeps its own license/consent — check per collection before redistribution. Schema standardization can lose study-specific detail.

name: CIBERSORT / CIBERSORTx & the LM22 leukocyte signature matrix
description: Reference signature matrix (LM22: 547 genes distinguishing 22 human immune cell subsets) and the associated deconvolution method for estimating immune-cell fractions from bulk expression. LM22 is a widely used immune cell-type signature reference; CIBERSORTx extends to imputed cell-type-specific expression.
scale: LM22: 547 genes x 22 immune cell subsets
license: custom (Stanford — free NON-COMMERCIAL only; commercial prohibited without license)

provenance.maintainer: Alizadeh & Newman labs, Stanford University

relevance.why: LM22 is a standard immune cell-type signature reference for estimating tumor immune composition from bulk expression — a feature source for immune-context modeling.

agent_access: LM22 matrix and tool require registration with an institutional (non-.com) email; terms restrict access to non-commercial academic users. Not freely bulk-downloadable without accepting terms — poor fit for unrestricted automated ingestion.
caveats: MAJOR LICENSE RED FLAG. Stanford provides CIBERSORT/CIBERSORTx and LM22 free for NON-COMMERCIAL use ONLY; any use by a commercial entity for any purpose (including research) is PROHIBITED without a license from Stanford OTL (docket S13-279). Registration rejects personal/.com emails. Do NOT embed LM22 or the tool in a commercial product without a Stanford license. Human only. Consider GPL alternatives (xCell, MCP-counter) where licensing matters.

name: CRI iAtlas (Cancer Research Institute iAtlas)
description: Interactive analysis platform and open data resource built on the TCGA immune-landscape (Thorsson) features plus ICI trial cohorts, exposing immune subtypes, cell composition, neoantigen/TCR metrics and immunomodulator expression through a web app and programmatic data packages/API.
scale: TCGA pan-cancer (>10,000 tumors) + multiple ICI cohorts
license: Open (code/data open; built on TCGA-derived features)

provenance.maintainer: Cancer Research Institute + Sage Bionetworks / ISB

relevance.why: Convenient programmatic access to harmonized immune features and ICI cohorts — a fast layer for pulling neoantigen/immune-context covariates without recomputing them.

agent_access: Web app plus an open API and R data packages (iatlas-data on GitHub) — no auth, scriptable.
caveats: Aggregates/derives from upstream sources (TCGA + published ICI cohorts); for read-level or controlled upstream data you still hit the original access tiers. Feature values are method-dependent.

name: EMBL-EBI BioStudies / ArrayExpress
description: EMBL-EBI's study archive; ArrayExpress (functional genomics, incl. single-cell) now runs as a BioStudies collection. European counterpart to GEO for discovering and retrieving deposited expression/single-cell studies.
scale: ArrayExpress: >70k experiments; BioStudies: hundreds of thousands of studies
license: EMBL-EBI Terms of Use; per-study terms vary

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI

relevance.why: Complementary discovery/retrieval layer to GEO (some EU studies are here first/only), widening coverage for an ingestion pipeline.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: BioStudies REST API returns JSON (search + per-study); files via BioStudies FTP organized by accession prefix. Legacy ArrayExpress v3 XML API is deprecated. bioservices (Python) and ArrayExpress Bioconductor wrap it. Automatable, no auth.
caveats: No single data license (EMBL-EBI Terms of Use + per-study terms) — check each study. ArrayExpress migrated onto BioStudies (2021); use BioStudies endpoints, not legacy API.

name: European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA)
description: Archive for personally identifiable / consented human genetic and phenotypic data under controlled access governed by per-dataset Data Access Committees (DACs). Holds many tumor genomics and some single-cell datasets not releasable openly.
scale: thousands of controlled-access datasets/studies

provenance.maintainer: EMBL-EBI + CRG (Barcelona)

relevance.why: Source for high-value controlled human tumor datasets (e.g. the one 3CA study held only on EGA) that are unavailable in open repositories.

agent_access: Public Metadata API for discovery (open); Permissions API lists datasets a requester may access. Downloads via EGA Secure Download Client / pyEGA3 over SFTP, files encrypted and decrypted client-side. Actual data retrieval requires DAC approval — NOT agent-automatable end-to-end; metadata discovery is.
caveats: Controlled access: each person/dataset needs individual DAC approval under a custom DAA; EGA does not enforce the agreement. Cannot be bulk-ingested without institutional approval. Factor approval lead time into any pipeline relying on it.

name: epiTCR training data
description: Large TCR-peptide binding training set (with/without MHC) released with epiTCR, a random-forest predictor, including categorized full-training files and negative construction.
scale: large (>3M rows across categories per repo); full-training file zipped in repo

provenance.maintainer: My Diem Pham et al.

relevance.why: One of the larger aggregated TCR-peptide training corpora; useful for scale experiments and as a comparison baseline.

agent_access: CSV (zipped) in GitHub repo data/ folder; clone/download, no auth. Automatable.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed — verify. Aggregated from public DBs (inherits biases/overlaps). Human only, no dog.

name: ERGO / ERGO-II training sets
description: Training/evaluation data bundled with the ERGO and ERGO-II TCR-peptide binding predictors. Users select McPAS-TCR or VDJdb as the training database; repos include preprocessed pairs and negative-sampling scripts.
scale: derived from VDJdb + McPAS-TCR (tens of thousands of pairs)

provenance.maintainer: Louzoun Lab, Bar-Ilan University (Springer et al.)

relevance.why: Reference preprocessing + negative-sampling pipeline over VDJdb/McPAS; useful as a baseline and for reproducing standard splits.

agent_access: Code + data in GitHub (ERGO, ERGO-II); web predictor at tcr2.cs.biu.ac.il. Clone/download, no auth.
caveats: Data is downstream of VDJdb/McPAS (inherits their licenses/biases, incl. VDJdb CC BY-ND). Repo-level license unclear — verify. No dog.

name: ERVmap — genome-wide human endogenous retrovirus transcription tool + locus set
description: Open-source pipeline and curated set of 3,220 human proviral ERV loci for quantifying genome- wide ERV transcription from RNA-seq, with an accompanying web tool. The reference method/locus annotation for measuring ERV expression — the substrate for ERV-derived tumor antigens.
scale: 3,220 annotated ERV loci; per-locus normalized/raw expression outputs

provenance.maintainer: Yale University (Iwasaki lab; Tokuyama et al.)

relevance.why: ERV-derived antigens depend on accurately quantifying locus-specific ERV transcription; ERVmap provides the standard locus set and pipeline to screen tumors for ERV antigen sources.

agent_access: Code + locus annotation on GitHub, no auth. Accuracy debated vs Telescope (see PNAS exchange 10.1073/pnas.1907705116 / 10.1073/pnas.1915450116).
caveats: NO LICENSE file located in the GitHub repo (flag before reuse). It is a tool + annotation, not a tumor antigen dataset per se. Human only; read-assignment accuracy is contested.

name: figshare
description: General-purpose research data repository (Digital Science) that mints DOIs for datasets and files. Hosts major single-cell releases (e.g. Tabula Sapiens figshare archives) and much supplementary data.
scale: millions of items; ~20 GB per-file free limit
license: per-item (CC0 default for data; MIT/GPL/Apache for code; CC-BY on some)

provenance.maintainer: Digital Science (figshare)

relevance.why: Primary host for several key single-cell atlas releases and supplementary datasets a pipeline must fetch by DOI/article id.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: REST API (articles, files, search) + OAI-PMH; direct file download by article id. No auth for public items. Automatable.
caveats: Per-item license varies (data often CC0, but confirm) — read it per record. Very large single-file archives (tens of GB) need resumable download handling. Self-deposit, so curation varies.

name: FLIP (Fitness Landscape Inference for Proteins)
description: A benchmark of protein fitness-landscape tasks with predefined train/test splits designed to stress-test representation learning for protein engineering. Core landscapes include AAV capsids, GB1, and thermostability (Meltome); FLIP2 (2026) adds seven further enzyme/photoprotein/PPI landscapes.
scale: FLIP: 3 core landscapes, multiple splits; FLIP2: 7 datasets, 16 predefined splits
license: AFL-3.0 (code); data release stated CC BY 4.0 (FLIP2) — verify per dataset

provenance.maintainer: Rost Lab / bioembeddings collaborators — Dallago et al.

relevance.why: Benchmark for protein-engineering fitness prediction with realistic low-N / extrapolation splits — tests whether PLM representations generalize for design.

agent_access: Split files + FASTA via benchmark site and bioembeddings mirror; Zenodo archive for FLIP2. GitHub for code. No auth.
caveats: Code is AFL-3.0; data license is stated as CC BY 4.0 for FLIP2 but not uniformly named for the original FLIP data — confirm per dataset/source. Underlying assays come from primary papers with their own terms.

name: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) + ArrayExpress/BioStudies
description: Primary public repositories for functional genomics (bulk + single-cell RNA-seq, arrays): NCBI GEO and EMBL-EBI ArrayExpress/BioStudies. Host the raw/processed matrices for most expression-based normal references here (e.g. GSE201333, GSE134355, GSE107011; E-MTAB-9543).
scale: >200k GEO series; millions of samples

provenance.maintainer: NCBI/NLM (GEO); EMBL-EBI (ArrayExpress/BioStudies)

relevance.why: Retrieval layer for the expression accessions cited across this catalog; enables scripted bulk fetch of normal transcriptome datasets (human and dog).

agent_access: GEO: E-utilities / NCBI Datasets API + FTP (supplementary matrices); raw reads via SRA. ArrayExpress/BioStudies: REST API + FTP. No auth for public records; NCBI API key raises limits.
caveats: GEO metadata is author-supplied (variable quality); raw reads live in SRA/ENA (large, separate fetch). Processed-matrix availability varies per series.

name: Human Cell Atlas (HCA) Data Portal
description: The Human Cell Atlas Data Coordination Platform: standardized ingestion, processing and distribution of HCA single-cell/spatial projects of (mostly healthy) human tissues, with metadata and bulk access (ERP/EGA accessions for raw data).
scale: Hundreds of HCA projects across organs; millions of cells

provenance.maintainer: Human Cell Atlas consortium / HCA DCP (EMBL-EBI, UCSC, Broad)

relevance.why: Canonical source and metadata backbone for normal human tissue single-cell atlases; resolves raw-data accessions (e.g. ERP123138 for the heart atlas) feeding the self references above.

agent_access: REST/Azul APIs + bulk matrix download; raw sequence via linked ERP/EGA accessions. Open metadata; some raw data managed-access.
caveats: Per-project licensing/consent varies; some raw data behind EGA/managed access. Processed matrices often more accessible on CELLxGENE.

name: NCI Imaging Data Commons (IDC)
description: Cloud-based node of the NCI Cancer Research Data Commons that hosts cancer imaging as standardized DICOM (radiology and DICOM-converted digital pathology), harmonized with genomic/proteomic commons for cross-modal analysis. Data live in public Google Cloud and AWS buckets with free, no-egress-cost access and co-located compute, plus web portal and viewers.
scale: >85 TB, ~60k patients, imaging converted to DICOM from TCIA and other sources (growing)
license: mixed per collection: predominantly CC BY 4.0 / CC BY 3.0 / CC0; some restricted

provenance.maintainer: NCI Cancer Research Data Commons; Brigham & Women's Hospital / Harvard (Fedorov, Kikinis et al.)

relevance.why: Cloud-native, DICOM-standardized imaging co-located with molecular commons; ideal substrate for scalable multimodal tumor models without moving terabytes of data.

agent_access: `idc-index` Python package resolves collections to GCS/AWS object paths; bulk download via gsutil/s5cmd with no egress cost from the public buckets. BigQuery metadata tables are queryable. Fully scriptable; no auth for open data.
caveats: Per-collection licenses vary (mostly CC BY, some CC0, some restricted inherited from TCIA) — check the per-series license attribute before redistribution/training. IDC re-encodes source data to DICOM; pixel content equals source but file identifiers differ.

name: ImRex TCR-epitope training data & models
description: Raw/preprocessed VDJdb-derived TCRb-epitope data (human TRB, 10x excluded, CDR3 10-20aa, epitope 8-11aa, shuffled negatives) plus trained CNN models and decoy/downsampled variants, from the ImMunoinformatics image-classification approach.
scale: VDJdb 2019-08 derived; data.zip ~34 MB; full record ~10 GB incl. models/comparisons

provenance.maintainer: Meysman lab, University of Antwerp (Moris et al.)

relevance.why: Clean, reproducible VDJdb preprocessing + negative-generation recipe and a CNN baseline for recognition; CC BY data is reusable.

agent_access: Zenodo direct download (data.zip ~34 MB is the useful part; full record ~10 GB with models); GitHub code. No auth, automatable.
caveats: Negatives are shuffle-generated (known to inflate performance vs real negatives). Underlying pairs from VDJdb. Human only, no dog.

name: Lizard / CoNIC — colonic nuclear instance segmentation & classification
description: The largest H&E colon-tissue nuclear instance dataset: 495,179 labeled nuclei across image regions from multiple sources/centers, with instance masks and 6-class labels (epithelial, lymphocyte, plasma, eosinophil, neutrophil, connective). Packaged for the CoNIC challenge as 4,981 non-overlapping 256x256 patches. Standard benchmark for colon nucleus detection/counting.
scale: 495,179 labeled nuclei; CoNIC patch set 4,981 patches (256x256), 6 classes

provenance.maintainer: Tissue Image Analytics (TIA) Centre, University of Warwick (Graham, Rajpoot et al.)

relevance.why: Labels immune cells (lymphocytes, plasma, eosinophils, neutrophils) alongside epithelial/ connective nuclei in human colon tissue — fine-grained immune-microenvironment ground truth.

agent_access: Development/patch data via the CoNIC grand-challenge page (free registration) and the Warwick TIA page; no fully anonymous bulk endpoint. Scriptable after registration.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is NON-COMMERCIAL + SHARE-ALIKE. Source/center count is reported inconsistently (6 vs. 16 across sources); verify from the Lizard paper. CoNIC test set is sequestered.

name: MCP-counter (Microenvironment Cell Populations counter)
description: Transcriptomic marker-gene signatures and method for producing abundance scores of eight immune cell populations plus fibroblasts and endothelial cells from bulk expression. Marker lists are small, curated, and directly reusable as immune-feature annotations.
scale: Marker-gene signatures for 10 cell populations (8 immune + fibroblast + endothelial)

provenance.maintainer: Etienne Becht et al. (Cordeliers Research Center, Paris)

relevance.why: Compact, open marker-gene signatures for immune/stromal abundance estimation — a lightweight, GPL-licensed feature source for immune microenvironment context.

agent_access: Open GitHub download of R package and marker-signature tables (GPL-3.0), no auth. Small and fully script-ingestible.
caveats: Code is GPL-3.0 (copyleft); the paper is CC BY 4.0. Produces relative abundance scores (comparable across samples, not absolute fractions). Human only.

name: NCBI GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus)
description: Primary public archive for functional genomics data including the majority of published single-cell and bulk tumor/immune studies (processed matrices + links to raw in SRA). The canonical first stop for discovering and retrieving deposited datasets by accession.
scale: millions of samples (GSM) across >200k series (GSE)
license: NCBI public-domain terms (no blanket license; submitter-dependent)

provenance.maintainer: NCBI / NIH

relevance.why: The main discovery+retrieval layer for nearly all deposited tumor-immune single-cell and functional-assay data — foundational to any ingestion pipeline.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: Entrez E-utilities (esearch/esummary/efetch) for metadata discovery (set tool+email; API key raises limits to 10 req/s). Bulk raw/processed files over FTP/HTTPS by accession path (GSEnnn/GSExxx/suppl). GEOparse/GEOquery wrap both. Robust for automation.
caveats: No single data license — reuse terms depend on the submitting study; GEO itself places no restriction but downstream terms vary. E-utilities does not serve all file bodies — use FTP for raw/supplementary. Rate-limit without an API key (3 req/s).

name: NCBI SRA (Sequence Read Archive)
description: Primary archive for raw high-throughput sequencing reads underlying GEO and many other submissions (FASTQ/BAM-level data for scRNA-seq, TCR-seq, etc.). Where raw reads are retrieved for reprocessing when processed matrices are insufficient.
scale: petabase-scale; tens of millions of runs (SRR)
license: NCBI public-domain terms (open) + dbGaP controlled tier

provenance.maintainer: NCBI / NIH (INSDC)

relevance.why: Raw-read source for reprocessing single-cell/TCR studies to a uniform pipeline and for recovering data not released as processed matrices.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: SRA Toolkit (prefetch/fasterq-dump) reads directly from AWS/GCP buckets; full corpus mirrored on AWS + GCP Open Data; metadata queryable via BigQuery (GCP) and Athena (AWS) for SQL-style discovery. Cloud Data Delivery Service copies originals to your bucket. Highly automatable.
caveats: Egress/compute costs when pulling from cloud outside the hosting region. Controlled human data (dbGaP) needs approval — not auto-ingestible. Large volumes; plan storage. Toolkit cannot deliver every original submitted file (use Cloud Data Delivery Service).

name: NCT-CRC-HE-100K — colorectal cancer tissue histology patches (Kather)
description: 100,000 non-overlapping 224x224 H&E image patches (0.5 µm/px) from 86 human colorectal cancer whole-slide images, labeled into 9 tissue classes including tumor epithelium, cancer-associated stroma, lymphocytes, mucus, muscle, adipose, debris, normal mucosa and background. Ships with an independent 7,180-patch validation set (CRC-VAL-HE-7K, 50 non-overlapping patients) and a non-color-normalized variant. One of the most-used tissue-classification benchmarks in pathology.
scale: 100,000 patches (224x224) + 7,180 validation patches, 9 tissue classes, 86 WSIs

provenance.maintainer: Kather, Halama & Marx (NCT Heidelberg / Univ. Medical Center Mannheim)

relevance.why: Includes an explicit lymphocyte tissue class alongside tumor/stroma in human colorectal cancer — clean, openly licensed immune-microenvironment ground truth for tissue-classification pretraining.

agent_access: Bulk download from Zenodo (DOI), no auth; HF mirrors exist. Fully scriptable over HTTPS.
caveats: Images are Macenko color-normalized; use the NCT-CRC-HE-100K-NONORM variant to avoid baked-in normalization. Patches (not WSIs); patient-level provenance limited. CC BY 4.0 confirmed on Zenodo.

name: NuCLS — crowdsourced nucleus annotations in breast cancer (TCGA)
description: Over 220,000 nucleus annotations (bounding boxes, segmentations, and class labels — tumor, stromal, immune/TIL, and others) on H&E regions of TCGA breast-cancer whole-slide images, produced by a scalable crowdsourcing + pathologist-review workflow. Provides single-rater (corrected and uncorrected) and multi-rater subsets; shares source images with the BCSS dataset.
scale: >220,000 nucleus annotations; single-rater (1,744 FOVs) and multi-rater (53) subsets; TCGA-BRCA

provenance.maintainer: Emory University PathologyDataScience group (Amgad, Cooper et al.); images from TCGA-BRCA

relevance.why: Labels immune/TIL vs. tumor vs. stromal nuclei on human breast tumors (TCGA), enabling cell-level immune-microenvironment features that can be joined to TCGA molecular data.

agent_access: Downloadable from the NuCLS site (Google Drive links) and GitHub; no auth. Underlying FOVs are TCGA-derived. Scriptable.
caveats: License stated as CC0 by the authors on the project site; confirm the current statement on the download page before redistribution. Multi-rater subset is small (53 FOVs). Shares images with BCSS — deduplicate if combining.

name: OmniPath (integrated intra- & intercellular signaling knowledge)
description: Integrated, programmatically accessible knowledgebase aggregating signaling pathways, protein interactions, enzyme-substrate/PTM relations, transcriptional regulation, ligand-receptor (intercellular) interactions, and protein annotations from ~100 source resources, with a unified R/Python/web API. Mouse/rat via orthology.
scale: Integrates ~100 resources; millions of interactions/annotations
license: custom — NO single license; each source resource's own license carries over

provenance.maintainer: Saez-Rodriguez lab (Heidelberg) & Türei et al.

relevance.why: One-stop programmatic layer for signaling, ligand-receptor, and annotation features — especially ligand-receptor/intercellular interactions useful for immune-cell communication features — without integrating each source separately.

agent_access: Open web service plus OmnipathR (R) and omnipath (Python) clients, no auth; supports a license='commercial' query parameter that returns only records whose source license permits commercial use. Highly automatable.
caveats: MAJOR LICENSE RED FLAG (mixed/per-resource). The redistributed data have NO single license — each original resource's license applies, and several are NON-COMMERCIAL (e.g. KEGG-derived, some text-mining and academic-only sources). Use the license='commercial' filter to restrict to commercially usable records before any product use. Client code is GPLv3 (pypath) / MIT (OmnipathR, omnipath). Always trace per-record provenance before redistribution or ML training.

name: PANDA — Prostate cANcer graDe Assessment challenge WSIs
description: Largest public prostate histopathology dataset: ~10,600 digitized H&E core-needle biopsy whole-slide images from two centers (Radboud UMC and Karolinska Institute), with ISUP grade and Gleason pattern labels (and segmentation masks for most). Built for AI Gleason grading; validated against expert uropathologists on US and European external sets.
scale: ~10,616 WSIs (development set), two centers; ISUP grade + Gleason masks

provenance.maintainer: Radboud UMC & Karolinska Institute; challenge hosted on Kaggle

relevance.why: Massive graded human-tumor WSI corpus for pretraining pathology foundation models and benchmarking grade/phenotype prediction that can be linked to molecular prostate cohorts.

agent_access: Download requires a (free) Kaggle account and accepting the competition rules; then bulk download via the Kaggle API/CLI. Not anonymous; scriptable after auth.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-SA-NC 4.0 is NON-COMMERCIAL and SHARE-ALIKE: forbids commercial use and requires derivative works (incl. some model/data releases) to carry the same license. Slide counts vary by source (10,616 cited by the paper; some tallies ~12,625 for the full dev set).

name: PanNuke — pan-cancer nuclei instance segmentation & classification
description: Semi-automatically curated H&E histology dataset spanning 19 tissue types with exhaustive nucleus instance masks and 5-class labels (neoplastic, inflammatory, connective, dead, non-neoplastic epithelial). ~189k–205k labeled nuclei packaged as 256x256 tiles across three folds. A standard benchmark for nuclear segmentation/classification across cancers.
scale: ~7,901 tiles (256x256), 19 tissue types, ~189k–205k labeled nuclei, 5 classes

provenance.maintainer: Tissue Image Analytics (TIA) Centre, University of Warwick (Gamper, Rajpoot et al.)

relevance.why: Pan-cancer nucleus-level labels (incl. inflammatory cells) give fine-grained cellular ground truth for the tumor-immune microenvironment across human tissues.

agent_access: Direct download of fold archives (NumPy/images) from the Warwick TIA page, no auth; HF mirror (RationAI/PanNuke) exists. Scriptable over HTTPS.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is NON-COMMERCIAL and SHARE-ALIKE. Nuclei counts differ by version/mirror (189,744 on HF; ~205,343 on Kaggle; paper cites ~216k pre-QC). Verify the exact fold version when reporting counts.

name: ProteinGym (fitness/mutation-effect benchmark)
description: A large-scale benchmark suite for protein fitness prediction and design, aggregating deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays plus clinical-variant datasets, with standardized splits and a public leaderboard. The reference benchmark for scoring protein language models / variant-effect predictors on mutation effects.
scale: 217 substitution DMS assays (~2.4-2.7M variants); 74 indel DMS assays (~300k); 2,525 clinical proteins

provenance.maintainer: OATML (Oxford) / Marks Lab (Harvard) — Notin et al.

relevance.why: Standard evaluation harness for mutation-effect / fitness prediction — directly measures whether learned representations transfer to design-relevant variant scoring.

agent_access: Zenodo zip bulk download + GitHub repo (code, splits, baselines). MIT license is permissive for ML use. No auth.
caveats: Variant/assay counts differ slightly across preprint vs repo (releases evolve) — cite the release used. Underlying DMS assays originate from many primary papers; MIT covers the ProteinGym packaging, not necessarily every upstream dataset's original terms.

name: ProteinMPNN / RFdiffusion (design models, weights & training data)
description: Open-source protein-design toolchain: RFdiffusion (backbone generation / de novo binder design, incl. target-conditioned binders) and ProteinMPNN (sequence design given backbone). Models and weights are public; training data is PDB-derived (multi-chain assemblies). No single packaged "benchmark dataset" is released — benchmarks live in the papers' supplements.
scale: Model weights + inference code; trained on PDB assemblies (RFdiffusion up to ~2020; RFD3/foundry reports PDB through Dec 2024)
license: ProteinMPNN: MIT; RFdiffusion: BSD (code + weights); RFantibody: MIT

provenance.maintainer: Baker Lab / Institute for Protein Design (UW); RosettaCommons

relevance.why: The core generative + sequence-design stack for building de novo binders, including against peptide-MHC. Public weights make it directly usable in the binder-design pipeline; benchmarks guide validation.

agent_access: Public GitHub repos; weights fetched via README wget (IPD file server for RFdiffusion) or Hugging Face mirrors for ProteinMPNN. Fully scriptable.
caveats: No standalone released benchmark dataset — reconstruct benchmarks from paper supplements. Mind license differences (MIT vs BSD) per component and whether weights are covered. Training sets are PDB-derived, not separately distributed.

name: ProteomeXchange / PRIDE (+ MassIVE)
description: Central federated infrastructure for mass-spectrometry proteomics and immunopeptidomics data. PRIDE (EMBL-EBI) and MassIVE (UCSD) are the main repositories; nearly all normal-proteome and normal-immunopeptidome accessions in this catalog (PXD*/MSV*) resolve here.
scale: >20,000 PXD datasets; petabyte-scale raw MS

provenance.maintainer: ProteomeXchange Consortium (PRIDE@EMBL-EBI; MassIVE@UCSD; jPOST; iProX)

relevance.why: The retrieval layer for every normal-proteome / normal-immunopeptidome PXD accession here (PXD016999, PXD010154, PXD000561, PXD000865, PXD020186/PXD024837); enables automated bulk fetch.

agent_access: PRIDE Archive REST API (ws/archive/v2) for metadata + file lists (JSON); download via FTP, Aspera, or Globus. No auth for public datasets. Large raw files.
caveats: Each deposit sets its own license (CC0/CC BY common but not universal) — resolve per PXD record. Raw MS usually needs reprocessing to usable tables.

name: STAPLER fine-tuning dataset
description: Data for STAPLER, a joint TCRab-peptide language model for specificity prediction. The model is fine-tuned on labeled full-length CD8+ alpha/beta TCR paired with 9-mer MHC-I peptides; the repo documents the training/evaluation data and negative construction.
scale: ~23,544 labeled TCRab-peptide pairs (fine-tuning set)

provenance.maintainer: Schumacher Lab, NKI

relevance.why: Full-length paired-chain labeled set (rarer than CDR3-only) for recognition modeling and as a strong transformer baseline.

agent_access: Data/code via GitHub; direct download/clone, no auth. Automatable.
caveats: Repo license not confirmed — verify before reuse. Underlying pairs drawn from public DBs (inherits their terms). MHC-I 9-mer scope only; human only, no dog.

name: TAPE (Tasks Assessing Protein Embeddings)
description: An early standardized benchmark + pretraining-corpus bundle for protein transfer learning: a Pfam-derived pretraining set (~31M protein domains) plus five downstream supervised tasks (secondary structure, contact prediction, remote homology, fluorescence, stability). Widely used as a reference point for PLM representation learning.
scale: Pretraining: ~31M Pfam domains (~7 GB compressed / ~19 GB uncompressed, PyTorch release)

provenance.maintainer: Song Lab (UC Berkeley) — Rao et al.

relevance.why: Foundational benchmark + Pfam pretraining corpus for evaluating protein representation learning; a baseline reference for design-relevant transfer.

agent_access: download_data.sh fetches Pfam pretraining set + task data from AWS (LMDB). pip package tape-proteins. No auth.
caveats: License differs by version: current PyTorch repo BSD-3-Clause; deprecated TF repo MIT; a PyPI listing shows a likely-typo 'BSD-1-Clause' — check the LICENSE in the exact repo used. Pfam-derived corpus inherits Pfam terms (CC0 for Pfam-produced data).

name: TIGER — Tumor InfiltratinG lymphocytes in breast cancER WSIs
description: Public WSI dataset and challenge for automated scoring of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in HER2-positive and triple-negative breast cancer. Provides ROI-level cell/tissue annotations (lymphocytes, plasma cells, tumor, stroma), whole-slide tumor-bulk masks, and slide-level visual TILs scores, enabling detection + segmentation + TILs-score pipelines.
scale: ~195 ROI-annotated WSIs + 93 tumor-bulk + 82 TILs-scored WSIs (train); 707-WSI sequestered test

provenance.maintainer: Radboud UMC Computational Pathology Group; hosted on AWS Open Data (bucket tiger-training)

relevance.why: Ground-truth lymphocyte localization and TILs quantification in human breast tumors — directly relevant to modeling in-situ immune recognition and the tumor-immune microenvironment.

agent_access: Public AWS S3 bucket (arn:aws:s3:::tiger-training, us-west-2) — bulk download with s5cmd/aws CLI, no auth; challenge evaluation on sequestered test set via grand-challenge. Fully scriptable.
caveats: LICENSE RED FLAG — CC BY-NC 4.0 is NON-COMMERCIAL. Total size not stated on the registry entry. Leaderboard-2 test set (707 WSIs) is sequestered.

name: UCSC Xena (public cancer genomics hubs)
description: Open visualization and bulk-download platform mirroring processed cancer genomics data from TCGA, PCAWG, GDC, TARGET, CCLE and others as tidy expression, mutation, copy-number, methylation and clinical matrices. The simplest no-auth route to many major cohorts' derived data.
scale: ~1,500+ datasets across public hubs (TCGA, PCAWG, GDC, TARGET, CCLE)
license: Software Apache-2.0; underlying data follow each source's policy (TCGA/PCAWG/GDC)

provenance.maintainer: UCSC (Haussler/Zhu labs)

relevance.why: Lowest-friction way to pull harmonized expression + mutation matrices across TCGA/PCAWG for building and benchmarking antigen-expression models without DUAs.

agent_access: Fully open: direct file URLs per hub (e.g. tcga.xenahubs.net/download/...), the UCSCXenaTools R client, and a query interface — no account, bulk-friendly, scriptable.
caveats: Processed/derived data only (no raw reads); these are mirrors, so the ORIGINAL source's use terms still govern (open-tier TCGA/PCAWG summaries are fine; raw/germline remain controlled upstream). No formal documented REST API beyond hub endpoints.

name: Wilhelm 2021 Prosit / ProteomeTools synthetic immunopeptidome
description: ~305,000 SYNTHETIC non-tryptic (HLA class I/II) peptides measured in ProteomeTools to train the Prosit deep-learning spectrum/retention-time predictor, boosting immunopeptidomics identification sensitivity. Ground-truth spectra, not elution data.
scale: ~305,000 synthetic non-tryptic peptides (HLA-I/II + AspN/LysN)

provenance.maintainer: TUM (Kuster/Wilhelm); PRIDE + Prosit/ProteomicsDB

relevance.why: Rescoring immunopeptidomics searches with Prosit substantially increases peptide IDs - a force-multiplier for any in-house reprocessing of raw HLA-elution data.

agent_access: PRIDE PXD021398 (API/FTP); Prosit served via ProteomicsDB/Koina. Bulk-downloadable.
caveats: Synthetic reference (for rescoring), not a ligand set. Paper also argues ~87% of proposed spliced peptides are likely wrong - relevant QC caution. Human sequences.

name: xCell (cell-type enrichment signatures)
description: Gene-signature resource and method for scoring enrichment of 64 immune and stromal cell types from bulk expression data, combining signatures derived from multiple reference datasets. Provides the signature gene sets and an R package / web tool.
scale: Signatures for 64 immune & stromal cell types (~10,800 marker genes total)

provenance.maintainer: Dvir Aran (Technion) / Butte lab (UCSF)

relevance.why: Open (GPL) cell-type enrichment signatures covering 64 immune/stromal types — a commercially-tolerant alternative to LM22 for immune-context features from bulk expression.

agent_access: Open GitHub download of R package and signature objects (GPL-3.0), no auth. Signatures are script-ingestible. Fully automatable.
caveats: Code and signatures are GPL-3.0 (copyleft — derivative software must also be GPL); the paper is CC BY 4.0. Produces relative enrichment scores, not absolute fractions. Human only.

name: Zenodo
description: CERN/EU-backed general-purpose research data repository that mints DOIs (concept + versioned) for datasets, code and supplementary files. Common host for immunology/ single-cell dataset snapshots (e.g. dated VDJdb releases) for reproducible pinning.
scale: millions of records; 50 GB per record free tier
license: per-record (depositor-chosen); must be set for public records

provenance.maintainer: CERN / OpenAIRE (EU)

relevance.why: Reproducible, DOI-pinned snapshots of community datasets and model inputs; a stable place to resolve versioned dependencies in a pipeline.

agent_access: PROGRAMMATIC: REST API (records search, metadata, file download) + OAI-PMH harvesting; DOIs resolve to files. No auth for public records (token needed only to deposit). Fully automatable.
caveats: License is per-record and must be read programmatically — ranges from CC0 to restrictive; never assume. Quality/curation varies (self-deposit). Prefer concept DOI's latest or pin a specific version.
